be, and she cannot get rid of it and does not know it is there, and it is nicer than the drawer and it is exactly the same as the drawer.** They argued about it for about an hour and a half and he did not have a single answer that was worth anything. **AND HE DID NOT IMPROVE THE SENTENCE.** He has had a pad since the fourth of September and it is the only place any of it is, and he did not take it out on that bridge and he did not write the word down, and the sentence is still exactly what it was in April and is not going in a minute and is not going on a wall and nobody in this borough may quote it. **IN THE KITCHEN, six people and a jug going round, and he was told he was not having the jug because there were nine of them and it is a jug, and then she said the thing she would not do before he asked for it: YOU ARE NOT GETTING THE LIST, and not because it is unsafe, but because THE LIST IS NOT FOR YOU AND NOT FOR A BUILDING AND THE LIST IS SO THAT WHEN ONE OF US SAYS A STREET, THE OTHER EIGHT KNOW WHICH STREET, and because if it went into a building the first thing anybody would do with it is find out who is on it, and the second thing anybody would do is take the ones who are on it off the street they are on.** **AND THEN SHE GAVE HIM ONE PIECE OF INFORMATION ABOUT THE HEAT THAT SHE DID NOT HAVE TO GIVE AND IT MADE ONE OF HIS FINDINGS SMALLER: the number of people in a street is not the number of houses, because two of the vans in that street are not anybody's address, and the difference is not an error, it is the street.** He wrote one line of it down and the line does not have the street in it and does not have the vans in it and does not have either of the two people in the vans in it, because a pad that goes in a shop is a piece of paper and a piece of paper with a street in it and a name in it is the exact thing a man of forty-five is carrying in a cardboard wallet in a van. **A PERSON WHO IS NOT COUNTED IS NOT A PERSON WHO IS HELPED WAS NOT REFUTED AND WAS NOT TOUCHED. AND NO MOMENT IN THAT CHAPTER PUTS A WORD IN HIS MOUTH ABOUT LOWGLASS, AND SHE CORRECTED HIM AND HE LET HER.** And the thing he did not do in that kitchen, which nobody knew he had not done: there is a sentence he has said out loud in rooms and a woman of nineteen had been saying the same thing on a street for eleven years, and he could have said it back to her for nothing and it would have been the truest thing anybody could have said to her, and he did not, because a sentence said in a room is a thing a room knows and it does not last, and if he had said it to her in a kitchen it would have become his and it is not his. She watched him not say it and she did not ask him why and nobody is going to know what to do with that either.

**Chapter 0151 — One Narrow Thing. Thursday the twenty-first of May 2015, from about ten past nine in the morning, a corridor and a board, the east wing, Saint Orra Civic Hospital; and about eleven o'clock, the laundry at the back of that site; and about half past two in the afternoon, the same corridor.** He asks NO QUESTION of anybody on that day and nobody asks him anything. **ONE PERSON ASKED FOR ONE THING IN WRITING AND GOT IT, IN ABOUT ELEVEN SECONDS, FROM A PERSON WHO COULD HAVE SAID NO, AND THAT IS THE FIRST TIME IN NINE MONTHS THAT ANYBODY IN THIS BOROUGH HAS BEEN GIVEN SOMETHING THEY ASKED FOR BY A PERSON WHO COULD SAY NO.** Eighty-one beds on a board and thirty-one degrees outside and two thirds of the eighty-one awake since half past four, and the board is what that building is held to, and a heat wave is not a reason to write a form. In a room the size of a garage with a door open and a fan somebody bought, a woman of about forty-four who has driven the Friday laundry round for nine years asked for one thing, on the back of a delivery note: **THAT THE LAST FOUR OF TWENTY-TWO STOPS BE DONE FIRST, THE OTHER EIGHTEEN STAYING EXACTLY WHERE THEY ARE, SAME DAY, SAME TIMES, SAME DRIVER, SAME VAN.** Her reason was a thermometer on the back of a loaded van in the sun in May and a woman of about ninety-one at stop eighteen who cannot get to a laundrette and is on no round but theirs. **It was granted by a person who could have said no, in about eleven seconds, and that is how long it takes to hand a man a piece of paper with a date on it, and nobody in that room found that remarkable and nobody in this borough is going to.** Winifred Crabbe, 62, linen supervisor, nineteen years, one of the seven filled seats of a body that has not met since the middle of January and cannot require anybody to do anything including her, and not on a rota of that laundry because there is not one. She said: *Then I will do it and I will not write it down, because if I write it down then it is a change of round and a change of round is a thing that somebody can point at in four years, and I have got a word for that and the word is not pleasant.* **AND HERE IS WHAT IT COST, AND SOMEBODY HAS TO LIVE WITH IT, AND IT IS NOT THE PERSON WHO ASKED. The east wing of that hospital is stop nine. If the last four go to the front then stop nine goes to at about nine in the evening and the linen comes off the van at nine at night in a heat and goes into a cupboard in a corridor with no mechanical extract, and bed nineteen has a warm sheet on it on Friday night and it is still warm at six in the morning, and the linen supervisor said that out loud in about four seconds BEFORE she said yes, and the patient said it to her on the Monday and she has written nothing down and there is nowhere for her to write it.** Nobody thanked anybody. **AND THE FINDING IS HIS: A PERSON ASKED FOR ONE NARROW THING, IT WAS CORRECT, SOMEBODY WHO COULD SAY NO SAID YES, IT TOOK AS LONG AS HANDING OVER A PIECE OF PAPER WITH A DATE ON IT, NOBODY IN THAT ROOM MADE IT INTO ANYTHING, THERE IS NO MINUTE OF IT, NOBODY WROTE IT DOWN, AND THE ONLY TWO PEOPLE WHO KNOW WHY IT HAPPENED ARE THE TWO OF THEM, AND HE WAS IN THE ROOM FOR THE WHOLE OF IT AND DID NOT KNOW IT WAS HAPPENING UNTIL A WOMAN TOLD HIM THE LINEN WAS GOING TO BE WARM. AND THAT IS A SHAPE. A correct request granted once is a precedent, and a precedent does not need anybody to decide anything, and the whole of the danger of a precedent is that the next one is easier and the one after that costs less, and there is no form, and the cost of it does not go to the person who asked, it goes to a woman of about ninety-one who will get her linen at half past three and to bed nineteen, and neither of them is in the room and neither of them is on anything and neither of them is going to be told. HE COULD SEE IT AND HE COULD NOT STOP IT AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM WAS GOING TO STOP IT, AND HE DID NOT WRITE IT DOWN, and the reason is that a pad that goes in a shop at the end of a street is a piece of paper and a piece of paper with a delivery note in it is a piece of paper that somebody can produce.** And it is not a service, because the counter is not the one who grants it, and asking a linen supervisor for a second one would be requiring her, and the only body in this borough that could require anybody has not sat since January. The school on Tarn Street closed at one o'clock that afternoon for want of water above the first floor and about ninety letters went home in the pockets of about two hundred and forty children and about half came back on the Friday. Nobody was harmed, nobody was helped, the register is at nineteen and the blank line is a hundred and seventy-six days old.

**Chapter 0152 — What A Person Can Be Held To. Friday the twenty-second of May 2015, from about two in the afternoon, a first-floor corridor over a shopfront in Tideglass.** **SHE ASKED HIM ONE QUESTION AND HE DID NOT ANSWER IT. He asked no question of anybody. Nobody opened a drawer. Nobody thanked anybody.** **NELL ARDENT, 39, FOUNDER OF THE OPEN COVENANTS LEGAL CLINIC, WHICH MAINTAINS THE PUBLIC CHARTER RECORD, ENTERS THIS BATCH IN A CORRIDOR, WITH A BOX ON SOMETHING, AND IT IS NOT UNKIND OF HER TO WANT ONE, AND THAT IS THE DIFFICULTY.** The heat is the first ten minutes and neither of them gets to the other thing until the hotel fan is on. A jug of water on the sill carried up a flight of stairs by somebody, two cafe glasses upside down, a lever-arch file put down on the dry side of the sill before she said anything, which is a lawyer's habit and not a clerk's. **Nine sheets, each with a box at the top that says PARTY, and on four of the nine it is empty, and that is not an accident: a record of what this city has promised and to whom, where the promise and the person go on the same sheet, which is the whole design of it and which she defended in a room four times.** She wanted the opposite, and it took her: a record with a box on it is what a person can be held to, that is the point of it, and if nobody can be held to a promise then a promise is a mood and she has watched what happens to a person who is owed something when the owing is a mood. And the other half, and she has known it since the March before last and has had nobody to say it out loud to: **a person who can be held to a promise can be FOUND, and every one of those nine sheets is a place where a person is slightly easier to reach than they were the day before, and nobody asked them, and she did that on purpose, and she would do it again on Monday.** **AND THEN SHE ASKED HIM THE QUESTION. It was: WHAT IS A PERSON IN THIS BOROUGH HELD TO. Not as an accusation, because she has never heard of a drawer and is not going to. THE ANSWER IS A DRAWER — a drawer under a counter two miles away with a tray on top of it that is not a list, no key, no list of what is in it, one hand putting things in it, a date on everything in it and no name and no reference and no box, and a man can walk in off the street and stand in front of a woman for about as long as it takes to say good morning and be told what was true on a day — and HE IS NOT ALLOWED TO SAY ONE WORD OF IT, because nobody in this borough may tell her there is one and there is no instrument in this city by which anybody could, and the whole of what a drawer is depends on nobody ever going and looking. SO HE SAID NOTHING, AND IT TOOK HIM A WHILE, AND SHE WATCHED HIM NOT SAY IT, AND SHE DID NOT PRESS HIM.** That is the part of it that is going to be in his own head for a long time. She asked what goes in an empty box and he gave her the correct answer: a node with no party is not a party and a place is not a person, and that is true and correct and is not going to be fixed, and it is also the reason four of her boxes are empty, and it is not a gap in her record, it is what her record has to say. And she is going to leave them empty, and in a few years somebody who is frightened is going to come to that corridor and ask her whether there is a thing about them, and she is going to be able to say *I do not know, and there is no box I can look up, and I could not tell you even if I wanted to, and I have built this so that I could not*, and that is not a weakness, it is the only thing she has that anybody else in this city does not have. **AND SHE SAID WHY SHE WANTS A BOX ANYWAY: if I were a person who did not care I would have got one inside a week and everybody would have come to me, and I would have been USEFUL, and useful is a service, and a service is a thing that can be given to somebody and taken away again, and I do not want to be that. AND HE COULD HAVE WARNED HER IN ABOUT FOUR SECONDS, and he is not going to, and the reason is the one that has been true since the eighth of April and it is not a good one: if he warned her, she would be the woman who was warned.** She picked the file up at about half past three with her hand flat on the top of it and said it was the whole of what she had decided that afternoon, and that she had a hearing on Thursday about a different thing and had not told him one word about it and he was not going to ask. Nobody opened a drawer.

**Chapter 0153 — Who Goes Without. Saturday the twenty-third of May 2015, from about eleven in the morning, a car park in Tideglass; and Sunday the twenty-fourth, from about twenty past six in the morning, a first-floor corridor off the lowland.** He asks NO QUESTION of anybody on either day and nobody asks him anything. **THE HOUR BETWEEN SIX AND SEVEN IS NOT STOOD IN THIS MORNING, AND THE DIFFERENCE FROM THE MORNING OF 17 MAY IS ON THE PAGE: then there were eleven people in a room who could not get into a building and the hour is why; this morning there are nine people in a corridor and they are not waiting for anything to open, the hall opens at seven, the corridor has a window and the hall has two high windows and no fan and it was twenty-six degrees in there at a quarter past six, and six of them brought clipboards and one of them was there at ten to six because he could not sit still, and every single one of them chose to be there and not one of them is obliged to be. An hour that requires nothing can be full. That is not a finding, it is what an hour is.** **THE SATURDAY, IN A CAR PARK, IN DAYLIGHT, WHICH IS WHERE A CITY STARTS ARGUING ABOUT WHO GOES WITHOUT.** Thirty-six degrees at about eleven in the morning and about fifty people and one bowser coming on the Sunday and four streets that wanted it. **There is no order, no declaration, no notice, no form, no reference, no committee, nothing chairing anything, and the seven people on a body that has not met since the middle of January are not there and are not obliged to be and would not be told.** The argument went on for two hours and everybody in it was right. A man of about fifty put the street that had been off since Tuesday first. A woman of about thirty put the school street first because there are about ninety children on it. A man of about sixty said no, the school was shut, and a shut school does not drink, and that was correct and stopped it for a minute. And a woman of about seventy who came on a bus ended it at about half past one in four seconds: *Then don't argue about the streets. Argue about the length. The one that's been off longest goes first, because the one that's only been off since this week has got the standpipe, and the standpipe is not dry. It's dear. There's a difference and it's the whole difference and you can see it from here.* And nobody wrote it down. **AND HERE IS WHAT THE BOROUGH HAS GOT: it is not a record, it is about nine people who can be asked, and a record would be a form and a form would have a box and a box would have a name in it, and the first thing anybody would do with nine names is find out whether the four streets on them are the four streets anybody is being helped on. And it is going to be gone in a fortnight, and the price of it is that the nine are findable and they know it and one of them said so out loud in that car park and got laughed at and the laughing was right.** At ten o'clock that night the eighteenth of those terms was read aloud by two tired men who are not on anything, and it began at seven the next morning and is six days long and not a week, and there is no date on it. **THEN THE SUNDAY, AT TWENTY PAST SIX, IN THE CORRIDOR: nine of them, six clipboards, a jug somebody carried up a flight of stairs, a window wedged with a piece of card, a fire door that is not locked. The decision was about four streets and it had been made in a car park and it was being made again, differently, because that is what a decision does when it is not written down: it has to be made again, by hand, over and over, by whoever happens to be in the room, and none of the versions is the version. Nobody argued. They were checking. One of them read a list out loud of four streets and nine households and the other said that number was right and the other read it again and it was right.** He stood at the end by the window for about half an hour and was asked nothing and asked nothing. **AND AT ABOUT HALF PAST SIX SOMEBODY ASKED THE MAN WHO TURNS THE BUCKET FOR SOMETHING ORDINARY AND HE ANSWERED.** A woman of about thirty-one came up the stairs with a barrow and four containers and a carrier bag from the street of ninety-one houses, and had been carrying water for three days because somebody in that street who is nine could not lift a bucket, and she had seen him about four times in two years. She said she was not asking for anything free and would pay and did not want a receipt and did not want to talk to anybody. She asked whether he would be at the stand on Monday. He said he would be there at ten. She said and if you are not. He said: I will be. But if I am not, and I am not saying that I will not be, I am saying what happens if I am not — the money in the slot does not go anywhere, and if the stand is not being worked then there is nothing to put money in, and if you put money in a slot at a stand that nobody is working that is money gone. Come at ten. If I am not there at ten then come at eleven, and if I am not there at eleven then the money in the slot is not being taken by me, and I would want to know that, and I would want somebody to tell me, and nobody in this borough has ever asked me one single thing and you have just asked me three and I have given you three and that is the whole of what has happened here in twenty-six years. **AND SHE WROTE HIS FACE DOWN ON THE BACK OF HER HAND, IN PENCIL, BECAUSE SHE HAD NO PAPER, AND HE SAW HER DO IT AND HE SAID NOTHING AND SHE ASKED HIM NOTHING.** **And that is not findability, and it is not the same shape as anything else in this borough, and it is not going to be put in the same sentence as anything else in this borough. A man who charges four pounds a bucket is the most findable man in the lowland and has been for twenty-six years and nobody did that to him, and a paragraph in a minute cannot tell a stand from a bollard, and a man a price makes findable and a man a shape in a room makes findable are two different men and the woman of about sixty who has said so four times is right. What happened on Sunday morning at half past six was neither of those things: it was a person asking a person, in a doorway, in a heat, and it lasted about two minutes and it will be gone by Wednesday. Nobody in this borough told him he was findable, he has not been asked one thing by anybody in this borough in twenty-six years, and there is no list and no list and nowhere in this city to put him.** Nobody was harmed, nobody was helped, the hall opened at about ten past seven and about thirty people were in it and the argument was not in it, and they went back down the stairs at about half past seven.

**Chapter 0154 — The Standing Of The City. Monday the twenty-fifth of May 2015 into Friday the fifth of June 2015. And on the Friday, from about one o'clock in the afternoon, a hall, Tarn Street.** He asks NO QUESTION of anybody in those days. He answered one question, in a day room at the hospital on Monday the eighteenth of May, and two people said something to him in a corridor on Friday the twenty-second of May and again on the Friday the fifth of June, and he answered neither of them. He did not chair anything and there is no chair of that body and there never was. **One item in the standing of the city is new.** He did not write any of it down and it is not going in a minute and it is not going on a wall. Nobody was harmed. **AND THE TANK AT THE SCHOOL IS A DIFFERENT SENTENCE FROM THE COUNTER, AND THE TWO ARE KEPT APART.** On Monday the twenty-fifth the register was a hundred and eighty days blank, and the school on Tarn Street had closed at one o'clock on the Thursday for want of water above the first floor and had sent about ninety letters home in the pockets of about two hundred and forty children, about half of which came back on the Friday about the heat and the water and whether it would be open on Monday; it closed again on the Wednesday of that week for the same reason and there was nothing to send anybody home with, because the letters were used up and nobody reprinted them and nobody has asked why. **AND ON THE TWENTY-NINTH OF MAY A PAGE WAS PUT IN A TRAY IN A ROOM IN TIDEGLASS. It is a page. It has a date on it, and that date is the twenty-ninth of May. It has a signature block at the bottom and the signature block is empty. Nobody in this borough knows what is written on it. It is not in a minute, it is not going in a minute, and nobody in this borough is going to be asked to sign it, and there is no form for it, and it did not come from this borough, and it is the smallest object anybody in this city has produced in nine months and it is the largest.** Then the Friday: the school had closed at one, the hall was twenty-nine degrees, about nine people in it, no agenda on the wall and none since January because the body that used to put one up has not met since the middle of January and is not obliged to, and there is no chair of that body and there never was. A head teacher with a folder. Two women from the parish. A man from the water office who had come on his Saturday. A man of about fifty-six who is not a member and has not asked Jonas Mercer anything since the twenty-seventh of April and was not going to. The woman of fifty-four who is the only person in this city anybody can write to, findable at a shopfront and at an address, unpaid since the fourth of July, who has not been told anything and nobody is going to tell her. And a caretaker of fifty-one with a ring of keys, thirty-one years at that school, whose key is a key and is not a holder, and who said nothing about any of it and got a door open because that is what he has got. **AND SHE WAS THERE IN DAYLIGHT WITH A THING IN FRONT OF HER SHE COULD DO SOMETHING ABOUT, AND SHE DID SOMETHING ABOUT IT IN ABOUT TWENTY MINUTES, AND IT WAS A THIRD OF IT. COUNCILLOR IVEN SORE, A SHE, COMPETENT, NOT CORRUPT, NOT LYING, AND EVERY SENTENCE SHE SAYS IN THAT HALL IS CORRECT; THE DIFFICULTY WITH HER IS STRUCTURAL AND IT IS NOT A MORAL THING.** She had a page with four buildings on it and three of the four were full and the fourth was Tarn Street school with a line against it and the line was the water. She telephoned twice from the corridor and did not raise her voice and was not performing for the room and nobody in that hall was asked to do anything. **What came to Tarn Street at about twenty past one was not a tanker. It was a bowser on a hired lorry and a man in a high-visibility jacket who put a hose into a tank that has been empty since the Thursday, and he put four thousand litres into it, and then he drove off to a building on the lowland with an empty tank as well. The water office's page has a full mark against Tarn Street by about half past two, and Tarn Street is the only one of the four with a mark on it at all.** And here is what it cost, and nobody in that hall was told any of it, and the head teacher worked it out herself at about ten to two and did not ask anybody: four thousand litres is not a week, the school gets through about eight hundred litres a day, four thousand litres is three days in an open building and nine in a shut one, the school opens on Wednesday on three quarters of a tank with a second delivery that nobody has booked and that the page does not show, because a page is a page of what is in a tank this afternoon and not of what will be in it on Friday. **THE OTHER THREE BUILDINGS ON THAT PAGE ARE STILL EMPTY. NOBODY WAS TURNED AWAY AT TARN STREET AND NOBODY GOT ANYTHING AT THE OTHER THREE EITHER, AND THERE IS NO QUEUE AND NO REFUSAL AND NO FORM, AND ONE PERSON MADE ONE DECISION AT ABOUT TWENTY TO ONE ON A FRIDAY AFTERNOON IN A CORRIDOR AND GOT A THIRD OF A PROBLEM.** Nobody in that hall thanked her. She said, unasked: *That is a third of it, and the other three on that page are still empty and the reason they are still empty is that the bowser went here, and the day somebody asks me why it went here the answer is going to be that I was in a hall and the school was in front of me.* He was at the back with nothing in his hands and said one thing, to the wall, about a catch tray that was recommended in 2011 and is not at the gully behind the market, and a wheel stop that is, and that nobody has looked at the wheel stop since 2011, and a wheel stop is the only thing in that yard anybody can see the purpose of. The head teacher said *Sorry* and he said he was not asking anybody to do anything, he was saying it out loud in a room in daylight because he had not said it out loud in a room in daylight before and it seemed to be the kind of thing you say in one. Nobody asked a follow-up, nobody wrote it down, and the caretaker looked at him for slightly too long and then went and opened a window. **THEN IN A CORRIDOR, AT ABOUT HALF PAST TWO, SHE TOLD HIM ABOUT THE PAGE, AND SHE PUT NO QUESTION TO HIM AND HE PUT NONE TO HER: there is a page in a tray in my office, it has the twenty-ninth of May on it, it has got a signature block at the bottom and the signature block is empty, and nobody is going to be asked to sign it, and it is not going in a minute, and it is not on anybody's desk for circulation. That is all either of us is going to know about it. I am not asking you to look at it. I am telling you it exists and not telling you what is on it, and we are both going to carry that about and neither of us is going to do anything with it, and I do not know how it ends and I have not asked anybody who does.** And his finding, which is the same finding as the laundry's and the first time he has seen it twice: a thing in this borough gets done because one person who could do it is standing in a room, and nobody in the room can be compelled to do anything, and nobody in the room is owed anything, and there is no form, and the thing gets done, and one person gets a third of it and says so out loud. He did not write it down, and a person who is not counted is not a person who is helped, and saying the name of that shape out loud in a room in daylight in June would not fill the hole, and he did not do it. And then the standing of the city on Friday the fifth of June, spoken, with one item new, and then the people, who are not in that and cannot be in it, and then the sentence, which has been true since the second of June and got heavier in May and did not get answered, and then three pieces of paper in this city that somebody has asked for or that somebody has got right — one with two other pieces of post on top of it since the eighteenth of February, one in a drawer with no key on it and no list into which a sentence about a catch tray went on Tuesday the nineteenth of May, and one on a page in a tray in Tideglass dated the twenty-ninth of May with an empty signature block, seven days old — and nobody in this borough has to deal with any of them, and there is no instrument in this city that could go and find a thing like that and ask what it is, and **the batch ends on a question and not a resolution, and it is not the question this borough asked itself in that vestibule on the thirteenth of May, and it is not about a person: SO WHICH OF THE THREE IS GOING TO BE OPENED FIRST.**

## Volume 04, Batch 0002 — Chapters 155–164

**Chapter 0155 — Nine Of The Same Answer. Friday the twelfth of June 2015, from about two o'clock in the afternoon, a car park, Tideglass.** He asks NO QUESTION and nobody asks him anything. It is the fourth week of a heat that has not broken and there is no week in this borough in which a car park is anywhere else. About nine of the same people who were in that car park on 23 May. **THE ONE LATTICE NOTICE IN THE CHAPTER, on the wall of the stair tower: a standpipe on this road is open whenever it is open, no person is required to be at a standpipe or near one or to answer for one, and a person who says a standpipe has been used is not asked when it was last used.** **THE PERSON WHO HAD GONE ROUND THE NINE WAS NOT SENT BY ANYBODY: RONNIE PEART, 52, of number fifty-eight, nineteen years, with a dog, no position of any kind. He went round nine doors over three evenings and asked one question at each of them — *if I write down what you tell me, what do I write* — and the answer at all nine was one word and the word was correct: NOTHING. The reason it is correct is that there is nothing anybody could do with it, and because if it is written down then there is a piece of paper about a house saying the house needs something and in a year's time somebody will come and ask whether it still needs it. THE RESISTANCE WAS A MAN WITH A CLIPBOARD AND IT WAS CORRECT: CALLUM NKMEDIRIM, 38, water office — a borough does not act on a conversation, it acts on a sheet, a sheet takes what a person said to you and makes it a fact because that is the only thing a sheet knows how to do, and **HE SAID OUT LOUD, IN A CAR PARK, IN FRONT OF ABOUT NINE PEOPLE, THAT HE WAS NOT PUTTING A NAME ON IT, AND THE REASON HE GAVE IS CORRECT: a name turns a street into a set of telephone numbers, and the first thing anybody would do with nine names is find out whether the four streets on them are the four streets anybody is being helped on, and the second thing is ring them, and the third thing is ask them why they have not been helped yet.** The woman of about thirty-one with a barrow gave the same answer correctly and refused to give her nine lines to anybody, and said out loud that nine lines in a row is not nine people, it is a street with a shape, and once a street has a shape there is somewhere you can point. **AND HERE IS THE THING THAT MADE THE CAR PARK GO QUIET, AND IT WAS NOT THE MAN WITH THE CLIPBOARD: Ronnie Peart said that nine of them said nothing, and that nine nothings in a row is not nine nothings, it is a street with *nothing* written against it, and in about four years somebody will be able to say that in the worst heat in nineteen years nine households were asked what they wanted and the record says they wanted nothing, and there is not one thing anybody can do about that sentence, and *that's not me saying it's a lie, it isn't a lie, that's the trouble with it, it's just a row, and a row is a different animal from a doorstep*.** Callum wrote the four streets and the nine answers in his own hand in a car park in the sun and left the name column and the contact column empty. **AND THAT IS THE MOMENT THIS PLACE STOPPED BEING A PLACE WHERE THINGS HAPPEN: a correct answer, said on a doorstep by a person who was owed nothing and would be owed nothing the next day as well, came back into a room and became a line, and a line under a street is a fact about a street, and a fact about a street can be repeated by somebody who was not there.** Nine people gave the correct answer to a correct question in a heat and not one of them has been counted and not one is going to be, and being right about it is not a thing anybody can hold. Nobody was thanked, nobody refused anything, nobody was helped.

**Chapter 0156 — Until Four O'Clock. Monday the fifteenth of June 2015, from about half past ten in the morning, a corridor, Tarn Street school; and about one o'clock, the same corridor.** He asks NO QUESTION and nobody asks him anything. Two people were in that corridor who did not have to be in it and nobody made either of them be there. The school had reopened on the Wednesday before last on about three quarters of a tank and it was about a sixth of a tank by half past ten, and the caretaker of fifty-one with his ring of keys worked it out on his own and the head teacher of about sixty worked it out on her own and they had not told each other until the Friday. **WHAT NEITHER OF THEM HAD IS A PAGE THAT SAYS WHAT WILL BE IN THAT TANK ON FRIDAY. THE WATER OFFICE'S SHEET HAS TARN STREET MARKED FULL, IN INK, WITH A TICK, AND THE TICK IS FOUR WEEKS OLD AND NOBODY HAS TAKEN IT OFF, AND THE TICK IS CORRECT ABOUT THE FIFTH OF JUNE: *they're looking at that page and seeing a school with water in it, and there's a school with water in it, there's just not one on Monday*.** Callum Nkemdirim came down that corridor to look at an isolation valve under the stairs and was not there for anybody, and the head teacher came out of her room and said four words to him, *can I ask you something*, and he said yes. **THE SECOND GRANT, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE LAUNDRY'S: a standpipe at the bottom of that street left on until four instead of two, because four of the nine households are at the bottom of a hill and cannot come up before eight in the morning and cannot carry a container up it in this heat, asked for in about four words in a passage and GRANTED IN ONE SENTENCE, and it cost this borough nothing at all because the lorry is booked for the day either way and if it stands there till four it is standing there for nothing, and he said so, and told her not to thank him because he had written four on a piece of paper. A CORRECT REQUEST GRANTED ONCE IS A PRECEDENT AND THE PRECEDENT IS NOW TWO AND HE COULD SEE BOTH AND COULD NOT STOP EITHER AND HE IS NOT ON ANYTHING AND HE WROTE NEITHER DOWN.** **AND HERE IS WHAT NOBODY IN THAT CORRIDOR NOTICED, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME IN NINE MONTHS THAT A ROTA IN THIS BOROUGH HAS WANTED TO INCLUDE ANYBODY: Callum's folder was open on the windowsill with a delivery sheet in it and a column headed *ON SITE*, and he said *put your name and I'll ring you when it's on its way*. THE CARETAKER SAID NO IN ONE SYLLABLE AND GAVE NO REASON AND IT WAS CORRECT. THE HEAD TEACHER SAID *put mine, I'll be here anyway*. AND A MAN OF THIRTY-EIGHT WROTE A WOMAN'S NAME IN A COLUMN IN ONE MOVEMENT BECAUSE SHE WAS STANDING THERE, AND NOBODY THOUGHT ABOUT IT, AND NOBODY IN THAT CORRIDOR WAS EVER GOING TO BE ASKED ABOUT IT. A ROTA IS NOT A PIECE OF PAPER, A ROTA IS A PERSON WHO CANNOT SAY NO, and nobody is required to be in a column on a delivery sheet, and she is in it, and that is a different sentence and it is the only interesting sentence in that building and it went past six people. HE NOTICED IT FROM THE END OF THE CORRIDOR AND COULD NOT DO ONE SINGLE THING ABOUT IT AND IS NOT ON IT AND CANNOT BE.** And the people who are not on that sheet are the people who were in a car park: the four streets are on it as standpipes at the ends of streets, the nine households on them are not, the woman with the barrow is not, Ronnie Peart is not, none of them has been asked and none is owed anything, **and the corridor does not know that there was a car park.** The register's blank line was a hundred and ninety-eight days old on the Friday and is two hundred and one days old on the Monday, and the rota at Saint Orra west has still not been rebuilt and cannot be and the row from eleven o'clock to half past one is still empty and still does not say *vacant*, and nobody looked at the second line under Bram Osei's Thursday and nobody is going to.

**Chapter 0157 — The Coolest Room In The Parish. Wednesday the seventeenth of June 2015, from about eleven in the morning, a church hall off the lowland; and about ten to four in the afternoon, the same hall.** He asks NO QUESTION and nobody asks him anything. There is no form for what happens in that hall and no room in this borough in which it could be minuted and not one person in it is on anything. **He went there because he cannot stop going to places with instruments, and it is the first time in nine months he has stood in a room in this borough that is not pointed at a question about owing, and nothing in that room is correct and nothing in it will ever be evidence of anything. He came off a bus shelter at thirty-three degrees in the shade and signed nothing and told nobody his name.** The hall has high windows on two sides, no air conditioning, a kitchen at the back, and twenty-five people in it at about eleven, every one of them come in off the street: a fan on a chair somebody carried from a house, a jug of water on a table with a spoon in it, a dog, a box of biscuits on its side with three biscuits in it that nobody was going to move. **THE PERSON WHO OPENED IT WAS MARGARET ODUYA, 77, THE CHURCH SECRETARY, WHO HAS THE KEYS BECAUSE THAT IS HER JOB, AND SHE DID IT BECAUSE A MINISTER SAID SOMETHING ON A SUNDAY.** Nobody was owed anything in that room, nobody was waiting for anything, there was no agenda and no notice and no reference and no box and no form, and nobody who came in was asked for a name, and if a person had wanted to be written down there was nowhere in the hall to write them. **AND THE RESISTANCE IS THE WHOLE OF IT: he looked for the instrument for about ten minutes and it was not there and it was not going to be. Every instrument in this borough is an instrument for finding out who is owed something, and in a heat everybody in a week is owed the same thing and almost nobody in this borough is owed anything at all, and every one of those instruments kept working perfectly through the fourth week of it and produced nothing. And this room had no instrument in it at all, was the coolest room on that side of the city, and nobody had asked anybody to open it, and nobody is going to be told that it was open.** He was asked three things in three hours that were not questions: whether the church roof was the parish's or the trust's, whether a chair could go by the wall for a hip, and whether he was somebody's dad. He said of course, no, and right, and nobody in that hall knew who he was and nobody was going to, **and there is no instrument in this city by which a man standing by a wall for three hours in a church hall becomes a thing anybody could be held to, and that is not a gap in the record, that is the record.** At about ten to four the woman of seventy-seven said her bus was at four, and about nine people said that was all right, and she locked it, and the spoon went back in the jug, and the box of biscuits stayed on its side for four more days. **AND HERE IS WHAT HE WORKED OUT AND DID NOT WRITE DOWN, AND THE PAD WAS IN HIS COAT AND HE DID NOT TAKE IT OUT: the cheapest things anybody in this borough has produced in nine months, and there are only two. The first is a sentence a woman said out loud, in a room that had a tray on a table in it, on a Friday morning in May, to a woman with a shopping bag who had asked a question at a counter — four sentences, correct, cost the woman who said it nothing at all, not written down, nowhere to write it down, and the woman who said it is not on anything and is owed nothing and is not going to be. The second is a date on a slip of paper that was folded and put in the inside of a coat on a Saturday morning in April last year by a woman who read it out loud first, and it is the only piece of paper in this city with nothing on it but a date. AND BOTH OF THOSE THINGS CAME FROM PEOPLE WHO WERE STANDING NEAR A THING — the woman at that counter was standing next to a tray, the woman with the slip was standing next to a door — AND NEITHER CAME FROM AN INSTRUMENT, AND HE HAS SPENT NINE MONTHS BUILDING THE INSTRUMENTS.** The reason is not a better reason than any other: a pad that goes in a shop at the end of a street is a thing he is the only keeper of, and in a few years somebody is going to be able to describe exactly what is in it, and the two things he had just thought about were made by people who did not have a pad and did not need one, and the making of them took four sentences and a fold, and if he wrote down what he worked out in a church hall on a Wednesday he would be building the fourth instrument and there would be a shop at the end of a street with a man behind a counter who had a book about how a place is kept cool. **The card in the slot is a hundred and seventeen days old and the letter in the tray is a hundred and nineteen days old, and a person who is not counted is not a person who is helped, and there were twenty-five people in that hall and not one of them had been counted and not one was owed anything, and the hall was four degrees the coolest place on that side of the city, and the reason it was open is that a woman of seventy-seven said so on a Sunday to a congregation and then came in on the Wednesday with a key. And there is nothing in this borough that can tell anybody she did that, and there is nothing in this borough that can stop her doing it again on Thursday.**

**Chapter 0158 — Nobody Can Put You In It. Thursday the eighteenth of June 2015, from about half past five in the afternoon, a canteen at the back of the Saint Orra Civic Hospital site.** **A man who stood in a corridor in this borough in May and read a sheet and asked a question it was never written to answer came back on his own. Nobody followed him up, nobody looked for him, he is not a thread, and he came because he had a question of his own. HE ASKED JONAS MERCER ONE QUESTION AND IT IS THE ONLY QUESTION ANYBODY HAS PUT TO HIM IN FOUR WEEKS AND HE ANSWERED IT, AND THE ANSWER IS WORTH NOTHING AND IT IS CORRECT. He came off that corridor and went into the canteen because there is a fan in the canteen, and that is the whole of how he was there, and he had been in the east wing three times since Monday in a heat and nobody had asked him anything on any of the three.** **SOLOMON ADJEI, 33, who works nights and has been on nothing since he was twenty, sat at a table with a tray he had not touched. HE KNEW HIM AND HE DID NOT ASK HOW, AND THE REASON HE DID NOT ASK IS THE ONLY THING HE DID IN THAT CANTEEN THAT WAS NOT PASSIVE.** Adjei said *you were at the wall, in May, I didn't know you were there that morning, I know who you are now and it's taken me six weeks, which I think is about right.* **WHY HE CAME, AND IT WAS A REASON OF HIS OWN:** he got the sheet again on the Thursday, read the fourth item again in a canteen, and worked out that he had already worked the answer out in May and that the answer is not on the sheet. **THE RESISTANCE IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT HAPPENED TO HIM: what happened to him happened to a corridor. A CORRIDOR IN THIS BOROUGH HAS NO RECORD AND CANNOT HAVE ONE, BECAUSE A RECORD OF A CORRIDOR WOULD REQUIRE A NAME ON IT, AND THE NAME IS THE WHOLE OF THE DIFFICULTY, AND THE REASON HE DID NOT SAY THE NAME IN MAY IS THE ONLY REASON HE CANNOT BE HELPED NOW. He had the correct act and it worked; a room would have given him a name on a sheet and in a few years a person in this city could have been pointed at as a person a service floor was for. He did not do that, he was right, and the price of being right is that there is now no record anywhere in this borough that a man stood in a corridor on the second of May and did the right thing, and there is no way to write that record down now without a name in it, and the name is the thing he will not say, and nobody is ever going to be asked for it, including the person it belongs to.** His question was *is there anybody in this city who is allowed to put me in that sentence without writing anything*, and the answer was **no**, with a reason, and the reason is not that anybody is keeping it from you and is not that nobody has thought about it: **anybody who could put a person inside that sentence without writing anything would have to be written down in order to do it, because that is the only way it gets done, and a person who is written down to do a thing is a person somebody can ring about it, and after that they cannot do it for you or for anybody else, and then one day they will not want to, and then they will have to pretend to.** The man said *that's what she said*, and said the woman at that counter was right and he was not going to improve on her answer, and Jonas Mercer said he had been nine feet away and had not heard her say it and had thought about it every day since. **AND THE COST OF THAT ANSWER LANDED ON A PERSON WHO WAS NOT IN THE ROOM, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME HE HAS WATCHED IT LAND ON SOMEBODY HE HAS SPOKEN TO: the man had said it at work, twice, on nights, in the break room, to two men he sits in a room with for eight hours, and he had got it wrong both times, and both times it had turned into a thing about him.** And there it was, and he did not say it, and it is a sentence a woman of nineteen named on a footbridge in this city in May and it is not his and he is not going to take it and say it back to a man in a canteen: a sentence said in a room is a thing a room knows, it does not last, and the only thing that happens to it is that it goes to a person — it went to a person on 2 May, standing up, folded, into a coat, and six weeks later the same sentence is in a break room on a night shift with his face on it. **The last thing the man said was the correctest thing anybody said in that canteen and has not been improved on: you could have told me in May, you were standing there and you knew what it was going to cost and you didn't come and find me after, and I've worked out why, and I think it's because if you'd found me then I'd have been a person you'd found. And Jonas Mercer said yes. And the man said so I wasn't found, and I still don't know whether that's a good thing, and he said neither do I, and the man said I'll be in on Wednesday and took his tray with him.** Nobody thanked anybody, nobody refused anything, nobody was helped, nobody was harmed, and nothing was written down, and there is no form in this borough on which a man of thirty-three could be recorded as having asked and a man of thirty-two as having answered, and if there were one then in a few years a piece of paper would be able to say that this borough had asked a man with nothing on it whether it had a place for him, and the true answer is on the paper, and the true answer is no. The register is at nineteen and the blank line is blank, the card is a hundred and eighteen days old, the letter is a hundred and twenty days old, and the row from eleven o'clock to half past one is still empty and still does not say *vacant*.

**Chapter 0159 — A Row. Friday the nineteenth of June 2015, from about ten in the morning, a meeting room on the ground floor of the water office; and about one o'clock, a corridor in the same building.** He asks NO QUESTION and nobody asks him anything, and nobody in that room thought about him at all, which is the whole of what his standing has ever been and he has stopped being able to improve on it. **THE SHEET IS ONE PAGE AND IT IS PRINTED AND IT HAS FOUR STREETS DOWN THE LEFT-HAND SIDE IN A COLUMN HEADED *LOCATION*, AND NINE LINES BESIDE THEM, AND EVERY ONE OF THE NINE LINES READS *No requirement stated*. Two of those four streets have two households on them, one has three and one has two, which is where nine comes from, and the man with the laptop did not collapse them into four and was right not to. There is no name box, no column for a name and no column for a day-time number, and the reason there is no space for either is that the man who filled the field sheet in a car park on the twelfth said out loud that he was not putting a name on it, and that is not written down anywhere.** In the room: Callum Nkemdirim, 38, who filled the sheet in and had it printed because a result you have got once is an anecdote; **DENISE HALLAM, 44**, who manages the contract the standpipes sit inside, who is the person the sheet goes out on and who could not stop it and does not want to; a man of about thirty with a laptop who is not a member of anything and did not speak; and a man of thirty-two at a chair on the end of the table with nothing in his hands. **Why it goes round on a Friday, and it is the only reason there is: because a sheet has to go round, and if it sat in a tray it would be a thing somebody remembered, and a thing somebody remembered is a feeling, and in August when this comes round again somebody is going to open a folder and find a page that says what this borough thought on the nineteenth of June. And: it is not a demand, there is nothing in it, nobody is being asked for anything, it says that on four streets in the eastern part of the borough, in the week of the eighth of June, nine households were asked what they needed and no requirement was stated, and that is a position, and a position has to have a date on it or it is an opinion, and it is exactly correct and nothing in this borough is more reliable than a thing that is correct and that nobody can dispute.** **AND HERE IS WHAT HE SAW, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME IN NINE MONTHS THAT HE HAS SEEN SOMETHING HE HAS SPENT THE WHOLE NINE MONTHS TRYING TO BUILD COME OUT OF SOMEBODY ELSE'S MACHINE. THE PAGE WAS NOT A COUNT. He has spent nine months on counts, and a count says how many there are, and that page said what this borough is going to do, and what it said it was going to do was nothing, and it said it about nine households, on four named streets, in a fortnight in June, in the worst heat in nineteen years. THAT IS A LEVEL OF SERVICE. It is the only kind anybody has ever written in this city that nobody has had to argue for and nobody can get out of, because in about four years there will be a sheet in a building in this city saying that in the second week of June, on four streets, nine households were asked what they needed and the answer was that they needed nothing, and that will be true in the way a printed thing is true, which is the way that survives, AND THERE IS NO WAY IN THIS BOROUGH TO SAY TO THAT SHEET THAT THE NINE WERE NOT ASKED, BECAUSE THEY WERE ASKED, on three evenings, by a man with a dog and no standing, at nine kitchen doors, and they gave the correct answer, and the answer is on the page, and the page is right.** And the part he could not put down, and the reason is not a better reason than any other, is that NOBODY HAD DONE ANYTHING WRONG: the man who went round was right and was not thanked, the woman who did not give him her nine lines was right, the man with the pen left the names out and said why, the woman who owns the contract is right that a sheet has to go round, and the man with the laptop typed nine lines and did not collapse them into four. **In nine months this borough has produced a small number of correct things that are worth anything, and every one of them was made by a person, by hand, on their own time, in about a minute, and none of them had anything written on it. **This cost nothing either, and it is the first one in nine months that was made without a single person having to be brave.** This cost nothing either, and it is the first one in nine months made without a single person having to be brave, and it is cheaper than a form, and it is worse, and it is going to win, because it does not need anybody to be brave and it does not need anybody to be owed anything. There is no form in this borough on which a person could write that they are not a series, and that absence is the only reason the page was allowed to exist, and the absence is why the page is the right shape, and the right shape is the dangerous one.** Nobody thanked anybody, nobody refused anything, nobody was harmed. **Nine people said nothing to nine doors and were right, and not one of them has been helped, and not one of them is on anything, and nobody is going to be able to find out in August that there was a car park on the twelfth of June, and the envelope is in a drawer in a kitchen in number fifty-eight and nobody has asked him for it and nobody is going to.** The register's blank line is two hundred and five days old and did not move. **And the sheet went out folded in four in a tray with nine other things in it, and it will be read that afternoon by about a dozen people, and not one of them will know where it came from, and every single person who reads it will read it as an absence of a problem, because that is what it is, because that is exactly what it is.**

**Chapter 0160 — The Man In The Stockroom. Monday the twenty-second of June 2015, from about two in the afternoon, a shopfront in Tideglass; and about four o'clock, the stockroom at the back of it.** He asks NO QUESTION and nobody asks him anything. **THE ONLY LATTICE NOTICE IN THAT SHOP, on the inside of the glass at eye height, over a notice about a card machine: drinking water is given at this counter while the shop is open, no person is asked for anything in order to be given it, and no person who is given it is asked where they live.** A convenience shop with the shutter half down because that is what a shopkeeper does with a shutter in June, a man of about twenty-four behind the counter with a fan pointed at the fridge, and a door at the back standing open with **a man of about thirty-five asleep on a folded blanket on the floor behind it, a sleeping bag rolled at one end, a bag against the wall and a jug on its side.** **AND HE DID NOT ASK, AND THE NOT-ASKING IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT THE INSTRUMENTS IN THIS BOROUGH ARE, AND IT IS NOT A THING HE HAS DECIDED TO DO. IT IS A THING THERE IS NOWHERE TO PUT: there is no form in this borough on which a person can be recorded as sleeping in a stockroom, the shopkeeper has known since about the spring and has not rung anybody and has not written anything down and has not asked him one question, and every instrument in this city that touches a person stops at a box, and the moment this man is written down anywhere he is a person who is known to be somewhere, and a person who is known to be somewhere is a person who can be moved on, and a person who can be moved on is a person somebody has handled. So the shopkeeper has a man in his stockroom and the shutter is half down and the stockroom has no air and no window that opens and it is thirty-one degrees in there, and nobody in this borough is going to be able to help him or unhelp him, and that is not a failure of a system, that is what happens at the end of every system that has ever been built in this city.** The landlord asked the shopkeeper in May to stop letting anybody in. The shopkeeper did not and did not tell him and did not tell anybody, **and that is the only instrument in the chapter and it works.** At about four o'clock **a man of about twenty-six came in with the back of a van open, said *is the ladder still in your yard*, went out and came back with a pedestal fan that was not new and not his colour and an extension lead, put the fan on the floor at the end of the stockroom where there was a socket, plugged it in, turned it round about a foot, looked at the blanket, and said *that'll be about four degrees*, and then said *it's a borrowed one, so*, and drove off. The shopkeeper said, to nobody, *he's about twice a month, he does the plastering*. **At about seven the shopkeeper put a jug of water on the crate beside the blanket and said nothing and shut the shutter all the way down at about half past seven because it had been about five in the sun. Four degrees. That is the whole of what anybody did on the twenty-second of June, it was the correct thing to do, it was the only thing anybody did, and four degrees in a stockroom with no window that opens in the fourth week of a heat is not a solution and it is not a failure, AND IT IS NOT POSSIBLE TO SAY WHETHER A MAN WAS HELPED OR WHETHER A MAN WAS GIVEN FOUR MORE DAYS OF BEING IN A ROOM IN THIRTY-ONE DEGREES, AND THOSE ARE THE SAME SENTENCE, AND THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THEM IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT THIS BOROUGH HAS TO GIVE AND DOES NOT GIVE. ON THE TUESDAY THE SHUTTER WAS DOWN UNTIL ABOUT TEN, THE STOCKROOM WAS EMPTY, THE BLANKET WAS FOLDED ON THE CRATE, THE FAN WAS AGAINST THE WALL WITH THE CORD WRAPPED ROUND THE BASE, AND THERE IS NO WAY IN THIS BOROUGH OF FINDING OUT WHERE THAT MAN WAS ON THE NIGHT OF THE TWENTY-SECOND OF JUNE, AND THAT IS NOT A GAP IN A RECORD. THAT IS THE RECORD.** **AND THE REASON HE DID NOT DO IT, AND IT IS ABOUT HIM AND IT IS NOT A PRINCIPLE: he was at the end of the counter with a bottle of water he had already paid for, and there was a man in the road about to come through that door with a ladder, and if he had gone out and said *that man on the floor is about thirty-five and he has no address and the room is thirty-one degrees*, then a man of about twenty-six would have known, inside a second, that a stranger had been in that stockroom and had looked at a man on a blanket and had made a speech about him — and he has watched what happens to the person who gets found, in three separate rooms in this borough in nine months, and every one of those rooms was his, and he does not have a room to give. He did not say the price out loud then and he is not going to say it now, because he said it once, to one person, on the thirteenth of April, and a sentence said once is a thing that room knows and it does not last. What is left, and it is enough and it is not noble: the man in the van had already got the fan out of the van before anybody said a word, and a man who is on a job at four o'clock on a Monday in June is a man who was going to be in that doorway anyway, and there is no version of this in which a man who is on nothing makes a man's chances better by being visible in a shop.** Nothing went in a document. **The shopkeeper's book that day has a jug of milk, a packet of biscuits and a pound change, and the fan belongs to a man who does plastering who came about twice a month, and nobody is going to find him and he is not a thread and he is not owed anything and he is not going to be asked. And a person who is not counted is not a person who is helped, and four degrees was given to a man on a blanket by a person he was never told the name of, and that is a kindness, and it goes to a person, and there is no box on it, and it is not going to be in any document in this city for as long as this city lasts.**

**Chapter 0161 — Twenty-Two Degrees. Tuesday the twenty-third of June 2015, from about ten past ten in the morning, the vestibule and the ground floor, the Old Ward; and about half past eleven, the second floor of the same building.** He asks NO QUESTION and nobody asks him anything. **THE HEAT TURNED ON THE SUNDAY MORNING ABOUT ELEVEN AND IT HAS NOT BEEN ABOVE TWENTY-FOUR SINCE, AND HE KNOWS WHAT THE HEAT DOES TO A PLACE AND HAS WATCHED IT DO IT IN JUNE, AND THE THING NOBODY TELLS YOU ABOUT THE FOURTH WEEK IS THAT IT IS NOT THE HEAT THAT IS THE FINDING. THE HEAT IS ONLY THE WEATHER. THE FINDING IS ALWAYS THE SAME SHAPE AND IT IS ALWAYS ABOUT A PERSON, AND THE HEAT IS THE ONLY THING IN NINETEEN YEARS THAT HAS MADE ENOUGH PEOPLE STAND STILL AT THE SAME TIME FOR ANYBODY TO BE ABLE TO SEE IT. AND A COOL TUESDAY PUTS ALL OF THAT AWAY AND GIVES YOU BACK THE THING YOU HAD BEFORE, WHICH IS A PLACE WHERE THINGS HAPPEN, AND THIS BOROUGH DOES NOT KNOW WHAT TO DO WITH THAT, BECAUSE IT HAS SPENT NINE MONTHS BEING A PLACE WHERE THINGS HAPPEN TO PEOPLE.** The counter stood at ten past ten with the door propped on a wedge of wood that nobody has taken out, because a door propped in June is a door somebody propped and nobody in that building is required to undo a kindness. **IT ANSWERED ABOUT A THING TWICE AND REFUSED NOTHING, BECAUSE NOTHING WAS ASKED, BECAUSE NOBODY ASKED IT ANYTHING ABOUT A GATE, OR A ROTA, OR A COMPLIANCE PARAGRAPH, OR A PERSON, AND IT WOULD NOT HAVE ANSWERED ANY OF THOSE IF THEY HAD BEEN ASKED, AND THE PRESSURE OF A HEAT IS NOT A REASON AND THE ABSENCE OF A HEAT IS NOT A REASON EITHER. In the heat the same eleven came through and not the same eleven; on the Tuesday it was a different eleven again, and the differentness was not a person refusing something, it was a person who did not need anything on a cool Tuesday, which is a thing that has never been recorded anywhere and is not going to be.** **AND HERE IS WHAT A COOL DAY SHOWS YOU, AND IT IS THE FINDING AND IT IS NOT A DISCOVERY: everything that got made in the heat got made by a person** — the last four of a laundry round on the back of a delivery note, four thousand litres into a school tank on a Friday afternoon by a person who got a third of a problem and said so out loud unasked, nine identical answers at nine kitchen doors, a standpipe left on until four because a woman of about sixty said four words in a passage, a cool room opened at eleven by a woman of seventy-seven with a key. **NOT ONE OF THOSE IS ON A FORM, NOT ONE HAS A NAME ON IT, NOT ONE IS A ROTA ROW, A BOARD SEAT, A REGISTER ENTRY, A MINUTE OR A COLUMN ON A DELIVERY SHEET, AND THERE IS NO MECHANISM IN THIS CITY THAT WOULD LET ANY OF THEM HAPPEN AGAIN EXCEPT THE PEOPLE WHO DID THEM DOING THEM AGAIN. AND THEY ARE NOT GOING TO BE STOPPED BY THE WEATHER. The woman of about thirty-one with a barrow was not carrying anything on the Tuesday because there was nothing to carry, and that is not a resolution, and she will be carrying again in August, and there is nothing anybody in this borough can give her that would change it, and the one thing she has that works is nine lines on a piece of paper the size of a receipt with street numbers in her handwriting and nothing at the top of it. A WEEK OF WEATHER MADE A SMALL NUMBER OF PEOPLE DO THINGS THEY ARE NOT REQUIRED TO DO, AND A COOL DAY DOES NOT TURN THAT INTO A SYSTEM, AND THE CORRECT OUTCOME IS THAT IT GOES ON BEING ABOUT FOUR PEOPLE, AND THE WRONG OUTCOME IS THAT SOMEBODY BUILDS A THING OUT OF IT SO THAT IT IS NOT FOUR PEOPLE.** Then he went up, and the room on the second floor is being repainted on the twenty-ninth of June and the shelves under the window are being counted, and **a man of about thirty-six with a clipboard and a paint tin stood at that shelf at about half past eleven counting files by the inch. NOBODY HAS EVER ASKED HIM ANYTHING EITHER. HE IS NOT ON A ROTA AND HE IS NOT ON A BOARD AND HE DOES NOT KNOW WHY THE ROOM IS BEING PAINTED AND HE HAS NOT ASKED. HE PICKED THE FILE UP BECAUSE HE WAS COUNTING AND BECAUSE IT WAS IN THE TRAY HE WAS COUNTING, AND THE BUNDLE OF POST ON THAT TRAY DID NOT MOVE, AND HE LOOKED AT IT FOR ABOUT A SECOND AND A HALF, AND HE DID NOT OPEN IT, AND HE PUT IT BACK IN THE SAME TRAY UNDER THE SAME BUNDLE OF POST IN THE SAME PLACE AT THE SAME ANGLE, AND HE WENT BACK TO COUNTING, AND HE WILL NOT REMEMBER, AND NOBODY IS EVER GOING TO ASK HIM WHETHER HE DID.** **AND HE WAS AT THE END OF THAT CORRIDOR AND HE SAID NOTHING, AND THERE WERE ABOUT FOUR SECONDS IN WHICH HE COULD HAVE SAID SOMETHING, AND IT IS NOT GOING TO BE SAID ON THIS PAGE WHETHER HE SHOULD HAVE. THERE ARE FOUR THINGS IN THIS BOROUGH THAT NOBODY HAS AN ANSWER TO AND HE CAN NAME ALL FOUR IN A SENTENCE AND HE HAS NEVER BEEN ABLE TO FINISH ANY OF THEM, AND ONE OF THEM WAS IN THAT MAN'S HANDS AT ABOUT HALF PAST ELEVEN AND THE MAN DOES NOT KNOW IT. A THING LOOKED AT BY TWO PEOPLE IS A DAY NEARER BEING ANSWERED. A THING LOOKED AT BY ONE PERSON IS A THING IN A TRAY UNDER A BUNDLE OF POST IN A CORRIDOR ON THE SECOND FLOOR OF A BUILDING IT HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH, AND THAT IS WHERE IT HAS BEEN SINCE THE SPRING, AND THAT IS CORRECT, AND IT IS NOT GOING TO BE DISTURBED, AND NO ONE IS GOING TO WRITE IT DOWN. WHETHER SAYING THE BAY NUMBER AND THE DATE OUT LOUD TO A MAN WITH A CLIPBOARD ON A TUESDAY MORNING WOULD HAVE BEEN A KINDNESS OR THE END OF THE CHEAPEST PRIVACY DEVICE IN THIS CITY IS A QUESTION HE HAS NOT ANSWERED AND IS NOT GOING TO ANSWER, AND HE STOOD AT THE END OF THAT CORRIDOR FOR ABOUT A QUARTER OF AN HOUR AND DID NOT ANSWER IT, AND THEN WENT DOWN THE STAIRS AND OUT INTO A STREET THAT WAS TWENTY-TWO DEGREES.** Nobody was helped, nobody was harmed, nobody died. The register's blank line is two hundred and nine days old, the card is a hundred and twenty-three days old, the letter is a hundred and twenty-five days old, and a cool Tuesday is not a reason to write on a blank line and nobody is obliged to.

**Chapter 0162 — Nobody Asked Me. Wednesday the twenty-fourth of June 2015, from about eleven in the morning, a room off a corridor, second floor, a building in Tideglass.** **THE PAGE OF THE TWENTY-NINTH OF MAY IS IN A TRAY IN THAT BUILDING AND IT WAS READ THAT MORNING BY A PERSON WHO WAS NOT ASKED TO READ IT, AND THAT PERSON IS NOT JONAS MERCER AND HE WAS IN THE ROOM AND DID NOT READ IT. A PAGE WITH A SIGNATURE BLOCK AT THE BOTTOM OF IT IS AN INSTRUMENT, AND THE PERSON WHO READS IT IS HELD TO BY IT, AND THE FIRST THING ANYBODY DOES WITH A PAGE THAT ASKS FOR SOMETHING IS FIND OUT WHO WANTED IT AND THE SECOND THING IS FIND OUT WHO WOULD LOSE. SHE DID BOTH AND SHE WAS RIGHT ABOUT BOTH. IT IS NOT IN FORCE. NOTHING ON IT HAS HAPPENED. WHAT IS ON IT IS NOT DESCRIBED AND IS NOT GOING TO BE DESCRIBED.** **THE ONLY LATTICE NOTICE IN THAT CORRIDOR, at about eye height, beside a fire door: a page left in a tray in this building is not circulated and is not actioned, no person is asked to sign, return or answer any page in this building, and any person may take a page out of a tray and put it back.** **AMA BOATENG, 29**, duty manager at a supermarket on the far side of the market, came in at about five to eleven with a bin rota she had written herself and a constituency of a dozen households on one street of terraces behind the market, because the collection on that street has not been for a fortnight, two men being off and nobody to send, and the woman of about seventy-six at the top of that street has been putting her bin out at six every morning and has stopped mentioning it. She is not on anything and has never been asked to fill in a box. She was let in and put in the room to wait because the councillor was at something else until about eleven, **and anybody who says a person should not have read it has not been in a room for twenty minutes with a tray on the desk.** She picked it up, read it once properly, and put it back at the same angle. **WHO WANTED IT, AND SHE WORKED IT OUT FROM THE SHAPE: one page, a space at the bottom for a person to agree, the space empty, so that is not a letter and it is not a complaint, because a complaint has a person on it — so somebody wants a thing decided once for everybody instead of nine times street by street by hand, and they want it done once because doing it nine times is slow, and because nine people doing it themselves cannot be written down, and because this building likes being able to point at things.** **AND WHO WOULD LOSE, AND NOT THEM: the people who lose are the ones who have been doing it themselves, because the day it gets decided once it gets done by somebody who works for somebody, and the people who live on her street cannot ask for it any more, and right now she can knock on the door of a woman of seventy-six at six in the morning and say *I'll take the bin out*, and that is it, and there is nothing in it, and nobody has asked her to — and the day that stops happening on her street it stops because somebody has decided it happens for the whole city instead, and it will be better and faster and will not be something a person can be blamed for and something a person cannot ask for.** **AND THEN THE ONE THING NOBODY HAD THOUGHT OF, SAID OUT LOUD, IN A ROOM, IN DAYLIGHT, AND IT IS NOT A FOURTH ANSWER AND IT IS NOT GOING ANYWHERE: THE PERSON WHO READS IT IS GOING TO BE THE PERSON WHO HAS TO DO IT. There is a space at the bottom of that for a person to agree to it and it is empty and nobody's going to be asked to sign it and I have read it, and from about ten to eleven this morning that page has got a reader in it and the reader is me and there is nowhere on that page to put that and it is not going to go on it and nobody is ever going to be able to look at that page and know that anybody in this borough has read it except the two of us — and I would rather be a person who read it and said so than a person who read it and said nothing, because a person who read it and said nothing is a person who did something on their own in a room and kept it, and that is a much worse thing to be, and I've watched people be that, and I'm not doing it.** **AND EVERY WORD THE COUNCILLOR IVEN SORE SAID IN THAT ROOM WAS CORRECT AND SHE IS NOT A MENACE AND SHE IS NOT WRONG: she would not tell her what was on it and made no secret of why, because if she told her then Ama would be a person who knows and a person who knows is a person somebody can ask and she has not got a way of protecting her from that; she would rather Ama had worked it out than been handed it; she cannot stop her having read it and would not if she could, and there is a tray and a piece of paper in it and no lock on the tray, and that is a design and not an accident, and she has been putting things in trays in this borough for a very long time and every single one has been read by somebody who was not asked to, and she has never once been in a position to do anything about that; and the correctest thing anybody has said in that office in about two years is not going to be improved on, because improving it would turn it into a policy and it is not a policy, it is a woman with a bin rota in her hand; and there is nothing on that page for her to do and nobody is going to ask her to do any of it.** **AND ON THE THURSDAY MORNING AT ABOUT NINE O'CLOCK SHE TELEPHONED THAT BUILDING AND SAID ONE SENTENCE AND HUNG UP: *I read the page in the tray on Wednesday morning at about ten to eleven. Nobody asked me to. I am telling you that so that it is not a thing that happened to a page.* The person who took the call said thank you and wrote nothing down, because there is nowhere to write it, and the page did not move and is not in force and has not been in force at any point since the twenty-ninth of May.** **A page that asks for something in this borough has now been read by one person who was not asked to read it, and she has said so out loud in a room in daylight and again on the telephone, and Jonas Mercer was at the back of that room and did not read it, was not asked about it, and said nothing, and he is not a reader of it.** The register's blank line is two hundred and ten days old, the card is a hundred and twenty-four days old, the letter is a hundred and twenty-six days old, and a person who is not counted is not a person who is helped, and a woman of twenty-nine read a page in a room she was not supposed to be sitting in and worked out who would lose from it and was right, and she has not been helped and nobody is going to help her.

**Chapter 0163 — Agreed. Thursday the twenty-fifth of June 2015, from about ten in the morning, a small meeting room at the water office; and from about one o'clock in the afternoon, a corridor in the same building, and then a lane at the end of a street that nobody in that building is ever going to walk down.** He asks NO QUESTION of anybody on that day and nobody asks him anything. **A CORRECT REQUEST WAS MADE IN WRITING AND GRANTED IN ONE SENTENCE BY A PERSON WHO COULD HAVE SAID NO, AND IT COST A PERSON IN A DIFFERENT STREET SOMETHING PHYSICAL, AND IT MUST BE A PERSON, AND HE IS NOT ON A LIST, AND NOBODY WAS RESCUED AND NOBODY DIED, AND THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THIS AND EVERY OTHER CORRECT THING THIS BOROUGH HAS DONE SINCE THE FOURTH OF SEPTEMBER IS THAT SOMEBODY WROTE IT DOWN. He found out afterwards and said nothing, and the whole of what he did about it was say nothing.** **PRITI SANDHU, 37**, of number twelve on one of the four streets, on no list and on no rota and owed nothing by anybody, with one page in her own hand and her own name at the top because it is her paper, and nobody has ever put a box in front of her: the standpipe at the bottom of that street runs off the tank, the tank is metered on a timer, the meter is correct, the timer is set for eleven till two on weekdays and not at all at weekends, none of it anybody's fault and all of it a page of what is in a tank this afternoon. She wanted it left on overnight for that week only, and gave two reasons: four of the nine households are at the bottom, and it is the bottom that everybody assumes is fine because it is near the tap. **AND IT WAS GRANTED IN ONE SENTENCE, AND IT COST THIS BOROUGH NOTHING AT ALL, AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY IT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: *yes, it can stay on overnight, I'll put the timer back at about eleven tonight* — and he told her it was not a favour and not a special one, because the water is metered on the tank and the tank is her school's, so the extra is hers, and the labour is the same labour, and if he had said no he would be a person who turns a lorry round in this heat for a preference.** Nobody in that room found it remarkable. **AND HERE IS THE DIFFERENCE, AND IT IS FOUR WORDS AND A DATE, AND HE WROTE THEM HIMSELF: Callum Nkemdirim turned the sheet over and wrote on the back of it, in his own hand, the word *agreed*, and the date. HE WROTE IT DOWN. That is the whole of the difference between this and the laundry round and the tank and the nine answers in a car park and the two hours at a school, and now it is a piece of paper. AND A PIECE OF PAPER HAS TO BE PAID FOR OUT OF SOMETHING: the allowance for that week was fixed on the Thursday before, the overnight water is a quantity, the quantity comes off a total, the total is fixed, and the only item on the whole of that list that has never once had anybody stand in front of it and ask for it was the filling round that goes down Collier Lane, because it fills butts and standpipes at the end of a lane of terraced houses and garages with no houses on it, and there is no demand against it and there never has been, and it is the last line and it is always the line that goes. **DENISE HALLAM, 44**, who manages the contract and who is the person the sheet goes out on, said the arithmetic out loud once and correctly and did not enjoy it: that is not an argument, that is what it is, if somebody at number twelve says overnight then overnight is in and the total is the same and the round at the end of Collier Lane is the round that is not in anybody's mouth.** It can move a day. It cannot move a fortnight, and nobody has asked for a fortnight and nobody is going to. **AND THEN SOMEBODY NAMED HIM, AND IT WAS THE FIRST TIME IN THIS BOROUGH THAT A PERSON WHO WAS IN A CORRIDOR ON THE MORNING OF SUNDAY THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF MAY HAD A NAME IN ANYBODY'S MOUTH, AND IT WAS NOT TO THE BOROUGH, AND IT WAS TO ONE PERSON, AND IT WAS IN A ROOM, AND IT HAD A REASON. A woman of about forty-three with a folder, who had come in late and had been standing at the back, said: *does anybody lose by it.* **And Denise Hallam said it, once, to Callum Nkemdirim and not to the room, in one sentence, and the sentence had the reason in it: *Colin Wharton. He's sixty. He is at number thirty-one at the end of that lane and he fills a butt under his own downpipe and he has filled it for about six years and he pays for every drop of it out of his own pocket, and he is not on anything and has never been on anything, and he does it because there is a woman at number twenty-nine who cannot get to the top of the lane, and that is the whole of the arrangement and it is his own, and he does not know anything about that round and nobody tells him anything about that round, and when it does not come he will work that out and he will not ask anybody.* And nobody said the name again, and nobody wrote it down, and it is in one person's mouth in one room in one building and it is not going to be in anybody else's.** **AND THAT IS THE BILL, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF IT, AND IT IS NOT ANYBODY'S FAULT AND IT IS NOT GOING IN A DOCUMENT, AND IT IS IN ITS OWN PLACE AND IT IS NOT NEXT TO ANYTHING THE READER IS BEING ASKED TO FEEL ABOUT: the round at the end of Collier Lane comes on a Thursday at about eleven, and it did not come on this one, and at about eleven that morning he put his hose on the tap at the end of the lane and there was nothing in the pipe. He carried four containers from the standpipe two hundred yards away at about one o'clock, on his own, and again at about four, and the water in the second lot was warm by the time he had finished with it because it had been standing in a plastic container in the sun since one o'clock. At about four o'clock in the afternoon he could not lift the fourth one. He left it standing full on the kerb at the bottom of the lane and he carried three up, and he is sixty, and he has a bad grip on his right hand and it has been like that since about February.** Nobody has told Colin Wharton about the timer and nobody is going to, and there is no instrument in this borough that would put a man of sixty on a list because his butt did not fill on the Thursday. **He was at the back of that room for the whole of it, he left at about half past ten, and he wrote nothing down. At about one o'clock, in a corridor outside a canteen at the back of a hospital site, a man of thirty-eight told him, in about six words and unasked, that the round at the end of Collier Lane had been taken off that week, and that there was a man at number thirty-one at the end of it who filled a butt under a downpipe, and that he was sixty. He said nothing.** **AND HERE IS WHY HE SAID NOTHING, AND IT IS ABOUT HIM, AND IT IS NOT A PRINCIPLE, AND IT IS THE WORST THING HE HAS DONE THIS MONTH: he could find Colin Wharton in about an hour — there is a street name and a house number and a man of sixty with a bad grip, and the only instrument standing between him and that house is the one that has been there all along, which is that going there is the whole of what he does. So there are two things he could have done and he did not do either and both of them are wrong. He could have gone and told a man of sixty that he is on a piece of paper in a building in the city, and that is how people get found, and he has watched it happen three times in nine months in three rooms that were his, and he said the whole of that out loud once, to one person, on the thirteenth of April, and he is not going to say it again. Or he could have gone and carried the fourth container up that lane himself, and that is what a woman of nineteen called a kindness on a footbridge in this city in May, and she was right about the word and the word is the reason he did not do it: it goes to a person, there is no box on it, and in a few years the only sentence anybody in this borough could say about Colin Wharton would be that a man came and carried his water, and he would not know who and neither would anybody, and there would be a man in this city whom a man of sixty on a lane of terraced houses and garages would be grateful to, and that man could not be asked about it by anybody, ever, which is the freedom, and it is also the whole of what he is, and it is not going to be enough and it is not supposed to be. SO HE SAID NOTHING IN A CORRIDOR, TO A MAN WHO HAD NOT ASKED HIM ANYTHING, ABOUT A MAN HE HAD NEVER MET, OVER A BUTT UNDER A DOWNPIPE.** Nobody refused anything, nobody was helped, and nobody died, and nobody was lucky. And the standing of that, on that Thursday afternoon, is that a woman of thirty-seven asked for one thing in writing and got it and it was correct, and a man of sixty carried four containers two hundred yards twice on his own and could not lift the fourth one, and the reason is a word and a date on the back of a sheet of paper in a building, and not one of the three is going to be told that the other two exist. **THIS IS THE FIRST CORRECT THING THIS BOROUGH HAS DONE SINCE THE FOURTH OF SEPTEMBER THAT HAS A PIECE OF PAPER ON IT, AND THE PIECE OF PAPER IS A BILL, AND NOBODY IS GOING TO BE GIVEN THE BILL.**

**Chapter 0164 — Nothing Else Has. Friday the twenty-sixth of June 2015, from about half past two in the afternoon, a first-floor room over a shopfront in Tideglass.** **He asked no question, he chaired nothing, there is no chair of that body and there never was, the board has not met since the middle of January, the ninth seat has not been told anything, the lowland cannot be seated, and a person who is not counted is not a person who is helped, and it is the end of June and it is still true.
