The standing of the city is said in a room in daylight out loud, without answering anything and without improving anything, and it is the third time that method has been used in this volume and it is said shorter than either of the first two, and it is not a reprise of either. THREE THINGS IN IT ARE NEW, two of them a month old and one of them the smallest thing anybody in this borough has produced in nine months, and none of the three is a document. THE ROOM IS NOT TARN STREET HALL AND IT IS NOT A CAR PARK AND IT IS NOT AN INSTITUTION.** A first-floor room lent by a woman who is a shopkeeper, and she is not on anything and nobody made a speech about that. **NOBODY WAS IN CHARGE. THERE WAS NO AGENDA AND NOBODY OFFERED TO TAKE MINUTES AND NOBODY THERE WANTED TO.** In the room: Ronnie Peart, 52, who went round nine doorways; a woman of about thirty-one with a barrow; a woman of about seventy who came on a bus; Ama Boateng, 29, with a bin rota in her coat; Callum Nkemdirim, 38, from the water office; and Jonas Mercer at the back with nothing in his hands, not on the agenda of anything. **The heat broke on the Sunday. It has been twenty-two degrees since the Monday.** **THE NEW THINGS COME FIRST, IN THIS ORDER, AND THE REST OF IT IS THE ORDER OF A ROOM AND NOT THE ORDER OF A FILING SYSTEM.** A row: one page, printed, a heading, a date, four streets down the left in a column headed *location*, nine lines beside them, every one of them the same, no name box anywhere on it and no column for one, gone round a building folded in four on the Friday in a tray with nine other things in it, now in nine other buildings, correct, and nobody in any of them knows where it came from, and nobody had to do anything wrong to make it. A page in a tray in a room in Tideglass with the twenty-ninth of May on it and an empty signature block at the bottom, not in force, not gone round anybody, not in a minute and nobody going to be asked to sign it, **now read by one person who was not asked to read it, who said so out loud, in a room, in daylight, on the Wednesday, and telephoned the building on the Thursday morning to say it a second time, and the office wrote nothing down.** And a chair: a chair on a landing on a block in Tideglass that belongs to somebody in that block and is not lost, put out on the landing at about eight in the evening, in the shade, for anybody who wants to sit down, and brought in again at about six, doing that since about the middle of June. **It is the smallest thing anybody in this borough has produced since the fourth of September and it is the only one of these three that is not a piece of paper. IT IS NOT A ROTA AND IT IS NOT A SHIFT AND IT IS NOT A ROTA THAT HAS NOT BEEN WRITTEN DOWN. IT IS NOT A FORM AND IT IS NOT ON A FORM. NOBODY IS REQUIRED TO MOVE IT AND NOBODY IS GOING TO BE TOLD WHO MOVES IT, AND NO INSTRUMENT IN THIS CITY COULD GO AND FIND OUT, AND THERE IS A WOMAN OF TWENTY-NINE IN THAT ROOM WHO WOULD BE THE RIGHT PERSON TO DESIGN THE THING THAT FOUND OUT AND SHE HAS NOT DESIGNED IT. Nobody in that room knew it happened. IT WAS NOT MENTIONED. IF IT HAD BEEN MENTIONED IT WOULD HAVE BEEN A ROTA INSIDE A FORTNIGHT, AND A ROTA INSIDE A FORTNIGHT WOULD HAVE HAD A NAME IN IT, AND THE CHAIR WOULD HAVE STOPPED GOING OUT ON THE LANDING AT ABOUT EIGHT, AND EVERYBODY IN THAT BLOCK WOULD HAVE SAID THAT WAS THE COUNCIL'S BUSINESS AND THE COUNCIL'S BUSINESS HAD KILLED IT.** It costs somebody a hand nine times a day, and it will stop at some point in July for reasons that have nothing to do with the heat, and there is nothing anybody in this city can do about that and there is nothing anybody in this city needs to do about that. **And the rest of it, which was all of it in April and is all of it now:** the counter, in a vestibule eleven feet by nine, answering in about eleven seconds, not a service, cannot be handed to anybody, does not grow, works because one person is standing at it who cannot be found from any record in this city, about eleven people a day, the same eleven in the heat and a different eleven in a cool week and no way of telling and nobody required to try; the register at nineteen with a blank line at two hundred and twelve days and the bulb on the nineteenth out; the card in the slot at a hundred and twenty-six days; the letter in the tray on the floor above at a hundred and twenty-eight days under two other pieces of post, not opened in front of a second person, and what is under the post not known to anybody; a drawer under that counter with no key and no list and a tray on it that is not a list, one hand putting things in it, and the only figure ever written down about it is nine and that was in March and it is a figure about the past; two conditions on the same wall sixteen inches apart that do not agree and have never been made to agree, nothing in this borough defining *holder*, and two letters and one word in pencil on the back of an enamel strip not read by anybody and not going to be; a public report with a paragraph number on it standing in front of four hundred and twenty women, never answered, never numbered and never stated in a room, and a machine on level zero still running, and its own strip going into a drawer in that room dozens of times a day by a hand that has not been found and was not looked for and is not going to be; seven of nine, two chairs empty, no chair of that body, not met since the middle of January and not obliged to, the ninth seat fifty-four, unpaid, findable at a shopfront and at an address, doing it since the fourth of July, not told anything and nobody going to tell her, **and the lowland not on the layer and not seated, and the reason still that a node with no party is not a party and a place is not a person, and neither the hot fortnight nor the cool weekend fixed it**; six water points at Tier 1, £11,280 a year in paragraph 6.1 of a minute as received and not as evidence, nobody asked to pay any part of it, **and the line at the end of a lane of terraced houses and garages with no houses on it is the one nobody has ever asked for either, and the man who fills it has been filling it out of his own pocket for six years and nobody in this borough knows his name**; the sentence about what a service floor is for, in the fourth item of a sheet that requires nothing, said once in daylight on the twenty-seventh of April, not repeated, not improved, not restated, not on a wall, and **nobody in this borough quoted it in June and somebody is going to want to**; a name in about eleven people and in no document and a hole in a record, and the hole still the only honest thing anybody in this borough has produced about a person in nine months; a gate that goes up at seven on a Sunday morning and stops at six on the Sunday morning after that, six days long and not a week, no date on it anywhere in this city, read aloud by two tired men who are not on anything; **and a bay behind a market with a wheel stop four feet in front of a grate and no catch tray, and a report about that bay on a shelf in a building it has nothing to do with, and nobody has opened it, and a man of about thirty-six picked it up while he was counting that shelf, read the cover, and put it back exactly as he found it, on the Tuesday, and told nobody, and will not remember doing it, and nobody is ever going to ask him.** Then the people, who are not in that and cannot be in it: the man of forty-four who cannot be asked one question, ever; the man of forty-nine who could be asked one question tomorrow morning and has not been; the man of forty-eight whom nobody has asked; a woman of fifty-four at a shopfront; a man of about forty-five with three pieces of paper in a cardboard wallet nobody owns; the man of thirty-three who read a sheet in a corridor in May, asked a question it was never written to answer, came back on his own in June, got a correct answer that was worth nothing, and is not going to be asked anything again; and **a man of sixty at number thirty-one at the end of a lane with a butt under his own downpipe that did not fill on the Thursday, and nobody is going to tell him why, and there is nowhere in this borough that anybody could put his name next to that fact.** Then the sentence, which has been true since the second of June and was not refuted by naming a purpose or by four thousand litres or by a wedge of wood in a door or by nine identical correct answers or by a printed page saying *no requirement stated* or by a cool Tuesday, and a man of thirty-two who is not on anything and is four hundred yards away on purpose and has stopped counting and the count stops at eight. **AND THEN THE QUESTION, AND IT IS NOT A RESOLUTION, AND IT IS NOT THE QUESTION THIS BOROUGH ASKED ITSELF IN THAT CAR PARK IN JUNE, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT A PERSON: there is a page in a tray in this borough that asks for one thing to be done for the whole city instead of for a street, and there is a chair on a landing in this borough that goes out at about eight in the evening and comes in at about six, and the chair is the smaller of the two, and neither of them has a person in it. Neither of them can be asked about. One of them has a space at the bottom of it for a name and the other one has nothing, and a thing with a space for a name can be refused, and a thing with nothing on it cannot be refused and cannot be required either, and this borough has spent nine months getting that exactly right and has not noticed that it has got two of them. And the heat broke on the Sunday, and every single thing that happened in June is still there in July, and nobody has to do anything about any of it. SO WHICH OF THE TWO IS GOING TO BE THE FIRST ONE THAT SOMEBODY IN THIS BOROUGH ASKS A PERSON TO AGREE TO.**

## Volume 04, Batch 0003 — Chapters 165–174

**Chapter 0165 — Under The Stairs. Monday the twenty-ninth of June 2015, from about eight in the morning, the second floor of the Old Ward.** He asks no question of anybody and nobody asks him anything. **The only Lattice notice on that floor, on the wall by the paint store, and it defines nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a tray on a shelf in this building is not an item, no person is required to keep, move, empty, list or answer for a tray, and a tray may be put anywhere in this building.** The room is being painted and the shelves under the window are being cleared, and there is nowhere in this borough for a tray of post to go that is not a list, and a tray of post under a bundle of post is not a list. **THERE ARE FOUR TRAYS ON THE TOP SHELF AND THREE OF THEM ARE NOT IN THE SAME POSITION.** The first, with the buff card under a bundle of post, is not being moved and goes back on the shelf at the same angle. The second, which is the tray the letter is in, is not on the shelf, is not in that room, and did not move, and the post on it was not lifted, and the woman of about fifty said four words about it and was not asked a second time. **The third is the one this chapter is about: about sixty pieces of internal post that came back off the Friday round on the nineteenth of June and did not go out on the twenty-sixth because there was nothing in circulation — three meeting notices for a group that has not met since March, a parking notice for a yard, and about fifty pages of something sent round in April.** The fourth is empty and has been since the spring and nobody can say what it is waiting for. **THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY AT THAT COUNTER, WHO HAS BEEN THERE ELEVEN YEARS AND WHO IS NOT THE WOMAN WHO COMES DOWN TO THE GROUND FLOOR AT ABOUT TEN AND ABOUT THREE, GAVE THREE PLACES: A TRAY, A LIST, AND THE CUPBOARD UNDER THE STAIRS ON THE GROUND FLOOR, WHICH IS THE CLEANING THINGS AND THE SPARE BULBS AND THE FIRE BLANKET AND WHICH GETS EMPTIED ON A FRIDAY BY WHOEVER IS ON. HER REASON FOR THE THIRD WAS THAT A LIST COSTS A PERSON AND A TRAY COSTS A FRIDAY.** She told him that if he called it post then in about a year somebody would put a date on it and call it a backlog and it would become a thing the building is behind on instead of a thing the building has got, and then she told him to say it's a tray, and he said it's a tray. **THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-SIX CARRIED IT DOWN AT ABOUT NINE AND IT IS HEAVIER THAN IT LOOKS, BECAUSE SIXTY PIECES OF POST WITH ELASTIC BANDS ON THEM IS NOT SIXTY PIECES OF POST, AND JONAS MERCER WENT DOWN WITH HIM AND SAID NOTHING AND WAS ASKED NOTHING. THE COST OF MOVING IT: that cupboard is emptied on a Friday, and in about a year that tray will be in a skip or a bin behind a shop, and nobody in this borough will be able to tell it was ever on a shelf under a window, and the woman of about fifty will not remember and the man of about thirty-six will not remember, and the only two people who will ever have known it was on that shelf are a man of thirty-two who was at the end of the corridor and a records supervisor who came off the bus on her own time once in May. NOTHING WAS OPENED. THE BUFF TRAY WENT BACK AT THE SAME ANGLE AND NOBODY IS GOING TO ASK THE MAN OF THIRTY-SIX WHETHER HE PICKED IT UP.** The register's blank line is 215 days, the card in the slot 129, the letter in the tray 131, and a repainted room is not a reason to write on a blank line and nobody is obliged.

**Chapter 0166 — Nobody Claims It. Thursday the second of July 2015, from about ten in the morning, a piece of hard ground four hundred yards from the end of a lane; and from about eleven o'clock, the mouth of the lane.** He asks no question of anybody and nobody asks him anything and he did not go up the lane. **A round that has been running for six years on nobody's asking came at about eleven, as it comes on a Thursday, and a man of about forty-one walked down that lane at about half past ten with a form in a plastic wallet and was told, correctly, by a man of sixty, to go away. Nothing was put to the man of sixty, so nothing was refused, and the count of refusals did not move.** The form is dated Tuesday the twenty-third of June, which was in the heat, and a form in this borough is a thing that gets written in a heat and the weather is only the reason there was time. The man of forty-one said out loud, to a man of sixty coiling a hose, what he had come for, and all of it, in about forty seconds, and none of it was a question. **THE MAN OF SIXTY TOLD HIM HE SHOULD GO AWAY, IN ABOUT FOUR SENTENCES, BEFORE HE HAD BEEN ASKED ANYTHING, AND HE WAS RIGHT, AND IT WAS NOT A REFUSAL BECAUSE NOBODY HAD ASKED HIM ANYTHING:** that round does not have a name on it, not a man's, not a crew's, not a number with a word beside it; it comes on a Thursday because it has always come on a Thursday and because the driver is on that road anyway; the day you put a name against it, the day it is a named job with a named reference, it is a job, and a job can be moved, and a job can be given away, and a job can be asked why it did not come, and the man who has to answer that is not him and will not be him, and it will be some lad on a Friday afternoon being asked where Thursday went. And: *if you do not write it, it keeps coming.* **The man of about forty-one picked up his wallet and went back up the lane on foot and was right to go and did not ask a second question, and no name was said in that lane by anybody and nothing was written down.** A round is a rota with a vehicle on it and a rota is a person who cannot say no, and that is the only reason anything works in this borough, and this round has never had a rota, and putting one on it would end it, and everybody in that lane knows that, and none of them has ever said it, and the one time it was said out loud it was said that morning by a man of sixty to a stranger with a form. **The round is not funded and does not get done and nothing is helped, and the woman at number twenty-nine was not mentioned and does not exist on any paper in this borough.** The register's blank line is 218 days, the card 132, the letter 134.

**Chapter 0167 — Nobody Asked Me Either. Monday the sixth of July 2015, from about five in the afternoon, a supermarket on the far side of the market; from about ten to seven, a corner shop; and after that, a street of terraces behind the market.** He asks no question of anybody. **The woman of twenty-nine who read the page of the twenty-ninth of May is on no committee of anything and is not going to be on one; she has a constituency of about a dozen households on one street and has said one thing out loud in a building and it changed what she did on one day, and this is Monday and it is cool and it is the first week of July.** She asked him one question — *what happens to a person who has read something they were not asked to read* — and he answered **nothing**, with the reason: a process is a place a person has to be written into, and once she is in it she is a person somebody can ask what is on it, and then she has to remember; nobody is required to tell you what happens to such a person, because nothing happens, and that is not a failure of the system, that is the system. **IT WAS WORTH NOTHING AND IT WAS CORRECT AND HE DID NOT IMPROVE IT.** She said she asked it because she already knew and wanted to hear a person who was not her say it out loud in a corridor, and that the building knows she read the page because she telephoned on a Thursday and said one sentence and the woman who took the call said thank you, **and she has been assuming ever since that a building writes down a sentence that has been said to it in daylight, and nobody can confirm it and nobody can deny it and she cannot find out, and if it is in there then what is in there is a person called in and said she had read the thing off the tray, and that sentence has a space in it where a name goes, and nobody put a name in the space, and the space will be there in August, and if it is not in there then she has spent eleven days being frightened of a piece of paper that does not exist, and from where she is standing the two of those are the same. THE BUILDING DID NOT WRITE IT DOWN — THE PERSON WHO TOOK THAT CALL SAID THANK YOU AND WROTE NOTHING, BECAUSE THERE IS NOWHERE TO WRITE IT, AND CHAPTER 0162 SAYS SO ON THE PAGE. WHAT CHAPTER 0167 RECORDS IS THAT SHE WAS NEVER TOLD THAT AND WENT ON AS IF SHE HAD BEEN.** **AND THEN SHE SAID THE CORRECTEST THING SAID IN THIS BOROUGH SINCE A MAN OF THIRTY-EIGHT LEFT A NAME COLUMN EMPTY IN A CAR PARK, AND SHE SAID IT AS A PLAN: the cheapest thing she can do is stop being findable, and she needs nobody to do anything, she just needs no route to herself, because the second there is a route somebody will use it and they will use it well and she will end up doing a thing she did not choose. He said that is correct. She said she knew it was correct and that she had checked it against about four days of not being findable and nothing bad had happened to anybody, and he said so do it.** **AND SHE DID IT BADLY. At about ten to seven she left a card at a corner shop with the shop's own telephone number on it and nothing else — no name, no initial, no address, no hours, no apology — and asked the woman who keeps it, who is about sixty-five and has a card rail by the door and has never once been asked to look after anybody's number, to say that it is the shop's number if anybody asks, and not to say who left it, and not to write it down. A shop is not a person, which is why she did it. A shop is also a thing that is open at a number on a street, and a thing that is open at a number is a route, and she has not removed herself from the map, she has moved herself from one column of it into another column of the same map, and the column she has moved into has a woman of about sixty-five in it who did not ask and who cannot refuse, and the sentence that will get said about her is a person, and a person is findable.** At about half past seven she walked back down the street and the bin at the top of it was out on the kerb where a woman of about seventy-six puts it at six every morning, and she did not take it in, and she stood on the opposite pavement for about half a minute and went home. **AT ABOUT NINE A LIGHT CAME ON AND A WOMAN OF ABOUT SEVENTY-SIX CAME OUT IN A DRESSING GOWN AND A CARDIGAN AND DRAGGED THE BIN BACK UP HER OWN PATH TO HER OWN DOOR, ON HER OWN, AND PUT IT INSIDE AND SHUT THE DOOR. SHE HAD NOT CARRIED A BIN IN SINCE THE MIDDLE OF JUNE. NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH KNOWS THAT HAPPENED AND SHE IS NOT GOING TO MENTION IT, AND THAT IS A METHOD, AND THE METHOD HAS JUST BEEN HANDED TO HER BY A PERSON OF TWENTY-NINE WHO DID NOT DECIDE TO HAND IT TO HER.** A man of thirty-two walked the street at about ten past nine, saw a light go off, did not know what it was, did not knock, did not go up, was not asked anything and did not tell her. Nothing was resolved, nobody was thanked, and the register's blank line is 222 days, the card 136, the letter 138.

**Chapter 0168 — Two Nail Holes. Tuesday the seventh of July 2015, from about half past six in the morning, a shop in Tideglass; and from about eleven o'clock at night, the stockroom at the back of it.** He asks no question of anybody and he says nothing. **A thing that was in that stockroom in June is not in it in July and nobody in that shop has been told anything about it and nobody in that shop is going to be. The looking was done by a man of twenty-four and it took him about four minutes and it is the first time anybody in this borough has gone looking for anything in nine months. A man of thirty-two was in the same room at eleven at night with about four seconds of an idea available to him and did not use it and knows who did the looking.** The fan was carried in on 22 June by a man of about twenty-six who does plastering, on a standing arrangement the shopkeeper had asked him for, and it was for a month of June. **AT ABOUT TEN PAST SEVEN ON TUESDAY MORNING THE SHOPKEEPER WENT IN FOR A CRATE AND LOOKED FOR IT PROPERLY, BEHIND THE DOOR, ON THE SHELF, UNDER THE BENCH AND BEHIND THE SHELVING UNIT THAT IS NOT FASTENED TO ANYTHING, AND FOUND NOTHING.** And he did nothing with it: he did not buy another fan, though there is one in a box in the back of that shop he bought off a stall some years ago for eight pounds which he does not put up because he does not like the sound of it; he did not telephone the man of about twenty-six; he did not write it in the book on the back of the counter where he writes down what he has ordered and has never written a thing somebody gave him; and he did not tell the man of about thirty-five who sleeps in that room, and if he had he would have been a person who knew something. **THERE ARE FOUR PEOPLE IN THIS BOROUGH WHO KNOW A FAN WAS IN THAT ROOM, AND THEY ARE THREE PEOPLE AND A WOMAN AT A COUNTER: the man of about twenty-six, the shopkeeper, and a man of thirty-two who was in that shop at half past four on 22 June with a bottle of water he had already paid for; and the woman of about fifty at the counter on the second floor of the Old Ward, who has been there eleven years and is not the woman who comes down to the ground floor, and who knows because the shopkeeper told her in about four words in June in a queue on his way out. THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FIVE DOES NOT KNOW AND HAS NEVER KNOWN, AND THE CHEAPEST PRIVACY DEVICE IN THIS CITY DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON NOBODY BEING ABLE TO TELL THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A THING THAT WAS NEVER THERE AND A THING THAT WAS TAKEN AWAY.** **AT ABOUT ELEVEN AT NIGHT A MAN OF THIRTY-TWO WENT INTO THAT STOCKROOM AND STOOD IN IT FOR ABOUT TWENTY SECONDS AND DID NOT LOOK FOR THE FAN. HE KNEW ON THE FRIDAY THAT IT HAD GONE. HE HAD ABOUT FOUR SECONDS IN WHICH HE COULD HAVE SAID SO TO A MAN OF TWENTY-FOUR, AND THE FOUR SECONDS WOULD HAVE BOUGHT ABOUT NINE WEEKS OF A MAN OF TWENTY-FOUR TELLING HIM THINGS, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE VALUE OF IT AND ALSO THE WHOLE OF THE DANGER OF IT, AND HE HAS BEEN AT THE END OF ROOMS LIKE THAT THREE TIMES IN NINE MONTHS AND IT WENT WRONG EVERY TIME AND HE DID NOT KNOW IT WAS GOING TO GO WRONG ANY OF THE THREE TIMES.** So he said nothing and he looked at the wall, and there are two nail holes in that wall about two feet apart a little above where the shelf line used to be, and the paint around them is not the same colour, and nothing else in that room has a mark on it at all, and the two nail holes will still be two nail holes in a year and there is no way in this city to find out what was hanging on them. The room is thirty-one degrees at eleven at night in July and it was thirty-one degrees at eleven at night in April, and the man of about thirty-five came in at about eleven and went up and put his bag against the wall on the side with no holes in it. Nothing was written down, nobody was thanked, and the register's blank line is 223 days, the card 137, the letter 139.

**Chapter 0169 — Date Seen Again. Wednesday the eighth of July 2015, from about half past ten in the morning, a first-floor room at the back of a building in Tideglass.** He asks no question of anybody. **The only Lattice notice in that room, above the door, and it defines nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a sheet in a tray in this building is not a return, no person is required to return, circulate, complete, explain or answer for a sheet in a tray, and any sheet in a tray in this building may be put back in the tray it came from.** Four people, and every one of them was right about something. **THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX, WHO IS ON NO COMMITTEE AND WHO READ THE SHEET OF 19 JUNE IN A TRAY IN THIS BUILDING, WENT ROUND ALL FOUR STREETS TWICE, ONCE WITH THE SHEET AND ONCE WITHOUT IT, AND THE SECOND TIME HE GOT NINE DIFFERENT SENTENCES AND ALL NINE WERE *WE HAVE ALREADY SAID*, AND NONE WAS UNKIND AND NONE WAS A COMPLAINT AND EVERY ONE WAS THE TRUTH.** He wanted the column because a thing you cannot repeat is a feeling: the sheet works for about a fortnight and then it is a piece of paper, and a piece of paper can be thrown away and this one will still be on a wall in nine buildings saying the same nine words. **DENISE HALLAM, 44, WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE COLUMN: a column is a column, and the first person to write in it decides what goes in it, and a date with a handwriting on it is a person, and a person is somebody you can come and ask why they were on that street on the second of July.** **A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-SEVEN WHO TAKES A TRAY ROUND THE FLOORS ON A FRIDAY AND HAS DONE FOR ABOUT SIX YEARS AND DOES NOT READ IT WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE ROUTE, FROM THE DOOR, CARRYING THE TRAY: the sheet went round in this tray with nine other things in it, two of them a lunch menu and a leaflet about a closure, and you cannot ask about a thing that arrived in a tray with a lunch menu in it, and only being able to pick something up and needing it are different, and only one of those is a decision anybody makes on a Friday afternoon.** **AND THEN THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX WORKED IT OUT HIMSELF, IN THE ROOM, IN DAYLIGHT, IN ABOUT TWENTY SECONDS: if I fill that column in, then that column is about me, and I will have put myself in a document in nine buildings, and in about a year somebody will want to know why a man of forty-six was going round four streets on his own time, and there is no version of that answer that is any good. So I want the column, and I am not going to be the one in it.** **THE COLUMN WAS ADDED. ITS HEADING IS *date seen again*. UNDER IT, PRINTED IN THE SAME SIZE TYPE, THREE WORDS: **no name, no initials.** AND THE SPACE IS EMPTY AND IT IS GOING TO STAY EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME. A document that asked for nothing in the worst heat in nineteen years now has a space in it for asking, and the three words under it are the only defence anybody in this borough has ever been able to write against a column wanting a name in it, and they are three words on a piece of paper and they are not a rule and nobody is required to keep to them and there is nothing behind them. IT IS THE EMPTYTEST AND THE MOST DANGEROUS OBJECT IN THIS BOROUGH AND IT IS CORRECT.** The sheet went round again on the Friday in a tray, folded in four, with the lid off, and the June sheet was not withdrawn, not annotated and not reprinted and nobody in any of the nine buildings knows there are two. He said one thing out loud, late, only to the man of forty-six, and it is the only use of the phrase *a level of service* in these ten chapters and it is not Nina Calder's nine words: it is a level of service, it is a statement with a date on it of what this borough is going to do about nine households on four streets, and it is nothing, and nobody asked anybody to be nothing, and now it cannot be got out of, and both of them in that man's hand are neither a survey nor a demand — and it is not an argument for the column, it is an argument for the column being empty. Nobody was thanked, nothing was minuted, and the register's blank line is 224 days, the card 138, the letter 140.

**Chapter 0170 — Three Things In June. Friday the tenth of July 2015, from about ten in the morning until about eleven, the vestibule and the ground floor of the Old Ward.** He asks no question of anybody and he was asked none. **A counter in a vestibule eleven feet by nine that answers what was true on a day and gives a date and nothing else, about eleven people a day, the same eleven in the heat and not the same eleven and a different eleven in a cool week, and no way of knowing which is which and nobody required to try.** The person at it is about fifty and has been doing it for nineteen years and comes down from the floor above, and the drawer under that counter has no key on it and no list, and the tray on top of it is not a list and is not a drawer, and neither is being dealt with this morning because it is a cool Friday and that is not a reason. **IT ANSWERED ABOUT A THING FOUR TIMES AND IT REFUSED NOTHING, BECAUSE NOTHING WAS ASKED THAT IT WAS REQUIRED TO ANSWER.** A woman of about thirty-three asked what the position had been in April and was told and given a date. A man of about twenty-nine asked whether a collection had been altered and was told it had not and was given the date of the notice and did not ask who had made the notice. **A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-SIX ASKED WHETHER HE COULD BE TOLD WHETHER A PERSON HAD BEEN ON A LIST, AND SHE SAID: I can tell you what was true on a day, and I can give you the date of it, that is the whole of what this counter is; it is not a list of people and I could not answer that if there was one, and I am not going to tell you there is not one, because I do not know that.** **NOTHING WAS REFUSED. NOTHING HAD BEEN REQUIRED OF THAT COUNTER, AND A COUNTER THAT ANSWERS WHAT WAS TRUE ON A DAY HAS NOT REFUSED A QUESTION ABOUT A PERSON; IT HAS TOLD A MAN THE SHAPE OF ITSELF, AND HE IS THE ONLY ONE IN THIS BOROUGH WHO HAS EVER NEEDED TO BE TOLD THAT, AND NOBODY SENT HIM. THE STANDING COUNT OF REFUSALS IS ELEVEN AND IT DID NOT MOVE THIS MORNING AND THIS WAS NOT A TWELFTH.** **AND AT ABOUT A QUARTER PAST TEN A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SEVEN CAME IN AND STOOD AT THE COUNTER AND DID NOT ASK FOR ANYTHING**, with a tap washer in a plastic bag. He said *I have got nothing to ask you*, and she said *it is not a waste of anything, I am stood here until about eleven*, and then she told him what the counter can do, and he said *June*, and she told him three things with the date on each and no name on any: a sheet went round this building on the nineteenth of June with four streets and nine lines and no name box and it is in nine other buildings; a man with a clipboard filled a sheet in a car park on the twelfth and left the name column empty and told about nine people out loud that he was leaving it empty; and on the twenty-fifth somebody got a thing they had asked for and it was written on the back of a page, and it is the only time in nine months that anybody in this borough has written a correct answer down. He said *that is better than what I came in for*, and she said she was not saying it to be interesting, she was saying it because he had a tap washer in a bag and was not taking it to anybody. **HE CAME IN AT ABOUT A QUARTER PAST TEN AND WENT OUT AT ABOUT ELEVEN AND SAID HE HAD BEEN IN THERE ABOUT THREE QUARTERS OF AN HOUR, WHICH IS THE ONLY CLOCK IN THE CHAPTER AND IT AGREES WITH THE DATELINE.** **HE HAD NOT ASKED FOR ONE PART OF IT.** Nobody in that building will be able to say who he was. **Nobody was helped in a way that lasts. The counter is the only thing in this borough that answers anything at all and it cannot be given to anybody, it does not grow, it is not obliged to be kept going, it worked because one person was standing at it, it did not move, the weather did not cause it, and the help costs about eleven seconds, and that is the measure of that counter's answers and it has never been written down anywhere, and a room remembers him, and a room is not a record, and there is no way in this borough to ask a room what it remembers.** The register's blank line is 226 days, the card 140, the letter 142.

**Chapter 0171 — Nothing Is Wrong With It. Monday the thirteenth of July 2015, from about half past two in the afternoon until about half past five, one of the four streets.** He asks no question of anybody and was asked nothing. **A street where nine people gave the same correct answer in the second week of June, in a cool week, with nothing at all wrong with it. The correct document says *no requirement stated* about this street, and it says it correctly, and it is in a folder in a building, and nobody in that street knows it exists.** No main off, no drain blocked, no collection failed, nobody carrying anything for anybody, no heat for three weeks, the pavement dry, and that is the whole difficulty with the thirteenth of July. At about three o'clock **A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-THREE was on his back at the top of a flight of steps hauling a fridge down through a window, with a card on his dashboard with a telephone number and eight items under it including *fridges* and *wardrobes* and *lofts*.** He had done four of the nine doors since the twenty-eighth of June, taken forty pounds at two and thirty at one in cash, left his card at six, and knocked at every door on the street including the nine. **HE IS FINDABLE AND HE MADE HIMSELF SO IN ABOUT NINE DAYS BY WRITING A TELEPHONE NUMBER ON A PIECE OF CARD.** **AT ABOUT FOUR O'CLOCK A MAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-SIX CAME UP THE STREET WITH A FOLDED MOVING BLANKET UNDER HIS ARM, WHICH MEANS HE CAME PREPARED, AND DID A JOB AT NUMBER NINETEEN IN ABOUT TEN MINUTES, AND DID NOT TAKE MONEY, WOULD NOT TAKE A CUP OF TEA, AND PICKED HIS BLANKET UP AND WENT BACK DOWN THE STREET, AND THE VAN THAT CAME FOR THE CHAIR WAS NOT HIS.** Nobody knows where he came from and nobody asked, and there is no way in this borough of finding him, and he is not on a rota, a list, a board, a minute or a document in his life, and the reason he came is that he came. There is no price on him, nothing has ever put one there, and he has not put one there himself. **HE ALSO KNOCKED AT NONE OF THE NINE AND THE MAN WITH THE CARD KNOCKED AT ALL OF THE NINE, AND EVERY ONE OF THE NINE LET HIM FINISH HIS SENTENCE ON THE DOORSTEP, AND NOT ONE SAID NO AND NOT ONE SAID YES, AND ONE GAVE HIM A GLASS OF WATER AND ONE TOLD HIM THEY HAD ALREADY SAID, AND BOTH OF THOSE ARE CORRECT.** **RONNIE PEART, 52, OF NUMBER FIFTY-EIGHT, OPENED HIS FRONT DOOR AT ABOUT TEN PAST FOUR, LOOKED DOWN THE STREET, AND SHUT IT AGAIN.** He did not go down the street, he did not offer, he did not call anybody, the envelope with the nine answers is still in a drawer in that kitchen, and a man of thirty-two walked past that door and neither of them knew the other was in the street. **A RIGHT DOCUMENT ABOUT A STREET DOES NOT STOP TWO MEN WORKING ON IT. IT NEVER DOES. IT SAYS WHAT A BUILDING IS GOING TO DO, AND WHAT THIS BUILDING IS GOING TO DO ABOUT THIS STREET IS NOTHING, AND NOTHING DOES NOT STOP A MAN WITH A CARD, AND NOTHING DOES NOT STOP A MAN WITHOUT ONE. NEITHER MAN IS CONTRADICTING THE SHEET. THE SHEET IS CORRECT AND THE STREET IS FINE.** Nothing was helped in a way that lasts, nothing was refused, nobody was thanked, and no name went in a box. The register's blank line is 229 days, the card 143, the letter 145.

**Chapter 0172 — The Landing. Wednesday the fifteenth of July 2015, from about ten past eight in the evening, a landing on the second floor of a block of flats in Tideglass.** He asks no question of anybody. **The only Lattice notice on that landing, at about the height of a person's eye, by the meter cupboard, and it defines nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a chair on a landing is not a shift and not a rota, no person is required to put a chair out, bring a chair in, wash a chair, or answer for a chair, and a chair on a landing is available to any person who wants it.** It had been raining since about five and it stopped at about half past seven, and at about eight a chair came out of a door and went to the far end of the landing by the window and stood in the shade with its back to the brick. **It is a wooden chair with a vinyl seat, it comes out of a flat and goes back into a flat, it belongs to somebody in that block, and it is not lost and it is not a charity and it is not lent and it is not booked and it is not on anything. Nobody is required to put it out or to bring it in or to wipe it or to know that it has been out.** **HE HAS BEEN ON THAT LANDING FOUR TIMES SINCE THE MIDDLE OF JUNE AND HAS NEVER SEEN ANYBODY BRING THE CHAIR OUT OR TAKE IT IN, HAS NEVER ASKED, DOES NOT KNOW WHICH FLAT IT COMES FROM, AND NOBODY IN THAT BLOCK WOULD TELL HIM IF HE ASKED.** **AND HERE IS WHAT THE BATCH NOTICED, IN HIS OWN HEAD, ON A LANDING, IN THE RAIN, AND IT WENT NOWHERE: a thing with a space at the bottom of it for a name can be refused, and that is not a flaw, and a thing with nothing on it cannot be refused and cannot be required either, and that is the whole of what this borough has built in nine months, all of it, and it is correct, and every piece of it is there because somebody worked the same thing out nine times independently and none of them has ever put it in a sentence that anybody else has read. AND THERE ARE TWO OF THE FIRST KIND IN THIS CITY. BOTH OF THEM ARE IN BUILDINGS. HE KNOWS ONE OF THEM AND WAS IN A ROOM WITH IT IN THE SECOND WEEK OF JUNE AND DID NOT READ IT AND WAS NOT ASKED ABOUT IT AND SAID NOTHING. HE HAS NOT GOT A NOTE OF THE OTHER ONE AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH HAS, AND THAT IS NOT BECAUSE OF HIM, AND IF HE ASKED THE QUESTION IN A ROOM IN DAYLIGHT FOUR PEOPLE WOULD ANSWER HIM DIFFERENTLY AND NONE OF THEM COULD SAY WHAT IT IS FOR. AND HE IS NOT GOING TO ASK IT, ON A LANDING, AT TEN PAST EIGHT IN THE EVENING, IN THE RAIN, ON HIS OWN, TO A CHAIR.** **AND AT ABOUT TEN PAST EIGHT A DOOR OPENED AND A MAN OF ABOUT SEVENTY-FIVE CAME OUT WITH A SHOPPING BAG AND PUT IT DOWN ON THE LANDING FLOOR.** He had put the bag on the chair at half past six when he came in, and there is no table on that landing, and the seat of the chair was wet, and he put his hand on the top of the back of it, looked at the seat, and did not sit down, and then picked the bag up off the seat and put it on the floor about two feet away and straightened it so it would not go over and went back inside and shut the door. **THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT HE DID AND IT TOOK HIM ABOUT FOUR SECONDS AND HE DID NOT DO IT FOR THE MAN OF THIRTY-TWO, WHO WAS STANDING AT THE OTHER END OF THAT LANDING WITH NOTHING IN HIS HANDS, AND HE DID NOT DO IT FOR THE NEXT PERSON TO COME OUT, AND HE DID NOT DO IT FOR ANYBODY.** **THE MAN OF THIRTY-TWO SAW IT AND DID NOT WRITE IT DOWN AND IS NOT GOING TO, AND WHETHER IT WAS THE RIGHT THING IS NOT SAID. A man of seventy-five put a shopping bag on a floor so that a stranger did not have to move a wet chair. That is a true sentence and a small one and it is a sentence about a man of seventy-five on a landing in July, and there is nowhere in this borough to put it, and saying it was the right thing would be a claim about a stranger's wet chair with no standing behind it.** The chair is on that landing and it will be brought in at about six in the morning by somebody nobody in this borough can name. The register's blank line is 231 days, the card 145, the letter 147.

**Chapter 0173 — The Hose Does Not Reach. Thursday the sixteenth of July 2015, from about ten in the morning, a service yard behind a block of flats in Tideglass, and a porters' lobby off it.** He asks no question of anybody, said nothing, and carried nothing. **A correct request, granted in one sentence, in a room, with no paper on it, and a bill. The bill is not on a person in a different street this time. The bill is on a man of sixty-three who was standing in that room, who was not asked for anything, and who could not say no because nothing had been put to him.** The block has four flats a side, a stairwell, a service yard and a cupboard in the wall with a locked standpipe in it, and the key is on a board in the porters' lobby. **THE KEYHOLDER IS A MAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-THREE WHO HAS BEEN THE PORTER OF THAT BLOCK FOR ABOUT NINE YEARS AND IS ON NO ROTA AND THERE IS NO ROTA, AND THE ONLY THING THAT MAKES HIM FINDABLE IS THAT HE IS STANDING IN A DOORWAY HOLDING A KEY, AND THAT STOPS THE MOMENT HE GOES INSIDE.** A man of about forty-two who fits washing machines said, without asking for it, that he needed the yard tap for an hour, because the machine has to be filled before it will start and all the taps inside were off since the Monday, and he had a van and the other one in at two. The man of about sixty-three said **yes, you can have the tap**, and when the man said *that is it?* he said *that is it, there is no paper for it, it is a tap*. **AND THAT TOOK ABOUT FOUR SECONDS AND HE WROTE NOTHING DOWN AND NOBODY IN THAT YARD ASKED HIM TO.** **AND HERE IS THE COST, AND IT IS NOT ON ANYBODY'S LIST AND IT IS NOT ANYBODY'S FAULT: the standpipe is in a cupboard on the wall of the yard, the tap is about two feet out from the wall, the hose on the reel does not reach the foot of that stairwell, and he did not know that until he had the cupboard open. So he filled a bucket from the standpipe and carried it up a flight of steps and put it in the machine, and he carried it up four times, in daylight, at ten in the morning, in front of about nine people.** A woman of about forty-one with a shopping trolley, a boy of about sixteen who got up off the step, two men at the far end, a woman at a first-floor window, and a man who came out of number four to ask about the riser and did not ask about the riser. **THE MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-TWO DID NOT HELP HIM AND DID NOT OFFER AND SAID NOTHING ABOUT IT, AND HE IS RIGHT, AND IT IS NOT ON AN INVOICE, AND A MAN WHO FITS WASHING MACHINES FOR A LIVING DOES NOT CARRY BUCKETS UP A STAIRWELL FOR FREE AT TEN IN THE MORNING, AND BOTH OF THOSE THINGS ARE CORRECT. HE PUT A TOWEL DOWN ON THE STEP SO THE YARD WOULD NOT BE TRACKED ACROSS, AND THAT TOOK ABOUT TWO SECONDS AND COST HIM NOTHING, AND THE TOWEL IS NOT ON ANYTHING EITHER.** **BY ABOUT THE THIRD TRIP SOMEBODY AT THE FAR END OF THE YARD SAID *LET ME TAKE THAT* AND HE SAID NO AND WAS RIGHT TO AND DID NOT EXPLAIN WHY AND THE MAN DID NOT ASK AGAIN.** **AND HE DID IT BECAUSE HE SAID YES TO FOUR SECONDS' WORTH OF SOMETHING, AND THE THING HE SAID YES TO WAS A TAP, AND NOBODY HAS SAID THE WORD TAP SINCE. NOBODY IS A PRICE. NOBODY IS ON A LIST. THERE IS NO FORM IN THIS BOROUGH ON WHICH ANYBODY COULD WRITE THAT A MAN OF SIXTY-THREE CARRIED A BUCKET OF WATER UP A FLIGHT OF STEPS FOUR TIMES ON THE SIXTEENTH OF JULY, AND THE REASON THERE IS NOT GOING TO BE ONE IS THAT IT WOULD HAVE TO HAVE A NAME AT THE TOP OF IT. AND THERE IS NO WAY IN THIS BOROUGH TO STOP A THING BEING HANDED OVER: HE WAS HANDED A THING AND THE PRICE OF A PRICE IS THAT SOMEBODY ELSE PAYS IT SOMEWHERE YOU CAN LOOK, AND THE PRICE OF A CORRECT REQUEST IS THAT SOMEBODY ELSE PAYS IT HERE, IN A DOORWAY, IN DAYLIGHT, AND THIS TIME THE PERSON PAYING IS CLOSE ENOUGH TO HAND IT OVER.** **AND A MAN OF THIRTY-TWO WAS AT THE BACK OF THAT YARD FOR THE WHOLE OF IT AND SAID NOTHING AND CARRIED NOTHING. HE HAS GOT A WORD FOR IT. THERE IS A PERSON OF NINETEEN IN THIS BOROUGH WHO HAS A WORD FOR WHAT THAT IS, AND SHE HAD IT IN MAY, AND SHE WAS RIGHT ABOUT IT, AND IT IS HER WORD AND IT IS NOT HIS, AND THE WORD WAS NOT SAID AND WAS NOT NAMED. HE HAS GOT IT ONCE AND HE IS NOT GOING TO USE IT AGAIN, AND THAT IS NOT A PRINCIPLE AND NOT A RULE HE SET HIMSELF: THE WORD BELONGS TO A PERSON WHO IS OWED NOTHING AND GOT IT FOR NOTHING, AND SAYING IT WOULD MAKE IT HIS, AND IF IT WERE HIS HE WOULD BE THE MAN WHO NAMED WHAT A PORTER OF SIXTY-THREE DID WITH HIS MORNING, AND HE IS A MAN WHO CARRIED NOTHING, AND THE WORD COSTS THE PERSON WHO CARRIES NOTHING, AND HE CANNOT PAY FOR IT. IT IS A DIFFERENT PERSON AND A DIFFERENT STREET AND A DIFFERENT SUMMER, AND WHETHER IT IS THE SAME SHAPE IS NOT SAID.** Nobody died, nobody was rescued, nobody was thanked. The register's blank line is 232 days, the card 146, the letter 148.

**Chapter 0174 — Eight Days. Friday the seventeenth of July 2015, from about two in the afternoon, a first-floor room over a lock-up in Tideglass, lent by a man who had the keys and was not coming back until Monday.** He is not on the agenda and he may not chair anything and there is no chair of that body and there never was and the board has not met since the middle of January, and the ninth seat has not been told anything, and the lowland cannot be seated, and a person who is not counted is not a person who is helped, and it is the middle of July and it is still true. **The standing of the city, said in a room in daylight, out loud, without answering anything and without improving anything, and said in the order of the weeks instead of the order of a room, and it is the third time anybody has said it and it is not better than the other two and it is not worse. It is 2,671 words as it now stands after the repair pass of 26 September 2026, against Chapter 0164's 2,222 and Chapter 0154's 5,263.** There were four people in it. Nobody was in charge and nobody took minutes. **IT IS TOLD IN THE ORDER OF THE WEEKS: the end of May, the twenty-ninth, a page in a tray with a space for a person to agree and the space empty, read by one person who was not asked; the eighteenth of February, a letter under two other pieces of post, a hundred and forty-nine days; the twentieth of February, a card in a slot, a hundred and forty-seven days; the twenty-sixth of November, a blank line under the nineteenth entry, two hundred and thirty-three days, the longest it has ever been, the bulb on the nineteenth out; the second week of June and the worst heat in nineteen years, nine doors and the same correct word and the printing of it on the nineteenth with no name box, a laundry round, four thousand litres, a cool hall, nine lines on the back of an envelope, and not one of it on a form; the second half of June, the grant with *agreed* and a date on the back of a woman's page, the bill on a man of sixty at the end of a lane nobody is going to tell, the 2011 report nobody opened, the man of about thirty-six who picked it up and put it back at the same angle, the repainted room, and the tray that went into the cupboard because a list costs a person and a tray costs a Friday; the first week of July, a form in a lane, a column with three words under it, a card in a shop window, two men on a street, a counter that told a man three true things, a chair on a landing and a shopping bag on a floor.** **AND THE PART OF JULY THAT IS THIS WEEK, AND IT IS THE ONLY THING IN THIS THAT IS NEW, AND IT IS NOT A DOCUMENT, NOT A FORM, NOT A PAGE AND NOT A BUILDING: since about the third of July there have been two trestle tables and a cardboard box of water bottles on the pavement outside a shop on the far side of the market, put out at about eleven and brought in at about five, in the shade, with nothing written on them and nothing hanging over the front of them. A man who works in the cold store at the back of that shop puts them out, because he was already going out into the sun at about eleven with a sack truck and there was a box of water going soft behind the counter that nobody was drinking, and the pavement outside that shop is in the sun from about eleven until about two. He is not on a rota, nobody is required to put it out or bring it in, and there is no list of it, no name on it and no sign. IT IS THE SECOND SMALLEST THING ANYBODY IN THIS BOROUGH HAS PRODUCED. THE CHAIR ON A LANDING IS SMALLER, AND THE CHAIR HAS BEEN GOING OUT SINCE ABOUT THE MIDDLE OF JUNE, AND NO ONE IN THIS BOROUGH HAS SAID OUT LOUD THAT ONE OF THESE IS SMALLER THAN THE OTHER, AND IF THEY HAD IT WOULD HAVE BEEN A ROTA INSIDE A FORTNIGHT AND THE TABLES WOULD BE INSIDE BY ONE.** Then the rest of it, which did not move in July: the drawer and the tray and the van and the sentence nobody knows is there; the public report with a paragraph number on it standing in front of four hundred and twenty women; two conditions sixteen inches apart; two letters and one word in pencil; seven of nine and two chairs empty and no chair of that body; the ninth seat; the lowland; six water points at Tier 1; the gate; the empty row that does not say *vacant*; the porter's refused Thursday and the second line nobody has looked at; and the four people nobody can ask. **AND THE SENTENCE: A PERSON WHO IS NOT COUNTED IS NOT A PERSON WHO IS HELPED, WHICH THE HEAT DID NOT REFUTE AND THE COOL DID NOT REFUTE, AND WHICH A FAN, A PAGE, A ROW, A COLUMN, A CARD, A BAG ON A FLOOR AND TWO TRESTLE TABLES DID NOT REFUTE.** A man of thirty-two is not on anything and is four hundred yards away on purpose and has stopped counting, and the count stops at eight. **AND THE LAST OF IT, WHICH IS A QUESTION AND NOT A RESOLUTION, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT A PERSON: there are eight things in this borough that anybody can walk in and read, and every one of them has a day on it, and not one of them has a name on it — the eighteenth of February, the twentieth of February, the twenty-sixth of November, the nineteenth of June, the twenty-fifth of June, the sixth of July, the eighth of July, and the seventeenth, which is today. **SEVEN OF THE EIGHT ARE ON PAPER SOMEWHERE AND A PERSON CAN WALK IN AND LOOK AT THEM. THE EIGHTH IS THE ROOM ITSELF, AND THERE IS NOTHING ON THE WALL OF IT AND NO PAGE AND NO MINUTE, AND THE ONLY ACCOUNT OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF JULY THAT EXISTS IS FOUR PEOPLE SAYING IT OUT LOUD WITH NOBODY TAKING IT DOWN, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE EIGHT THAT COULD BE LOST BY FOUR PEOPLE DYING.** A day can be pointed at. A name cannot. In nine months nobody in this city has found a person by a date, and nobody has been found by a name either, and that is the only privacy anybody here has ever had, and it was never designed and it is not defended and it is one table away from not existing. A room is not a record, and there is no way in this borough to ask a room what it remembers, and the eighth of these eight is a room. SO WHICH OF THE EIGHT IS THE FIRST ONE SOMEBODY IN THIS BOROUGH DECIDES TO KEEP, AND IS IT GOING TO BE KEPT BECAUSE IT WAS GOOD OR BECAUSE IT WAS EXPENSIVE.**

**Chapter 0175 — Nobody Put Them There. Saturday the eighteenth of July 2015, from about eleven in the morning, a pavement on the far side of the market; and from about five in the afternoon, the same pavement.** He asks no question of anybody and nobody asks him anything. **The only Lattice notice on that pavement, on the pillar at the end of a shop's frontage, and it defines nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a thing on a pavement is not a service, no person is required to put one out, bring one in, count one or answer for one, and a thing on a pavement may be left on a pavement.** Two trestle tables and a cardboard box of water bottles have been on that pavement since about the third of July, put out at about eleven and brought in at about five, in the shade, with nothing written on them, put there by a man who works in the cold store at the back of that shop because he was already going out into the sun with a sack truck and there was a box of water going soft behind the counter. There is no list of them, no name on them and no sign, and nobody has ever put the question to him. **AND A CRATE APPEARED BESIDE THEM ON THE FRIDAY OF THE TENTH OF JULY AND NOBODY BROUGHT IT.** The man from the cold store did not decide to have it: somebody put an empty back in the box, and he could not carry a bottle back in in front of people without carrying the thing he had brought out, so he picked the empty out and stood it in a crate that was already behind the shop for onions. **THE CRATE IS NOT A DECISION, IT IS A CONSEQUENCE, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH CAN TELL YOU THE DIFFERENCE.** By the eighteenth it has a place: against the leg of the near table and not beside the bin, four empties standing up in it and two fulls at about half past eleven, and at about five the man from the cold store carried four empties and two fulls out to a sack and took the crate in with them. **THE TABLES AND THE BOX CANNOT BE POINTED AT. A CRATE CAN: A CONTAINER IS A PLACE A THING CAN BE PUT, AND A PLACE A THING CAN BE PUT IS THE FIRST HALF OF AN ARRANGEMENT, AND THE MAN WHO FILLS IT IS A MAN. Four people in this borough know the crate is there and three of them work at that shop.** He stood at the end of that frontage for about a quarter of an hour and did not ask, and at about half past eleven **A MAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-EIGHT WHO HAS SOLD FRUIT OFF THAT FRONTAGE ON SATURDAYS FOR NINE YEARS said, unasked, to the pavement and not to anybody, that he does not know who put the crate there, that it was there at about half past nine when he came with the van, that that is what he knows and all he knows, that nobody is going to be able to tell him either, and why: the second one of us says the name of the thing out loud, it becomes a thing two people know about, the thing has got a route, and by the following June there is a young man with a clipboard and a form, and the form has a name box on it, and the form is worse than the table, and at least the table was free. **THE FINDING: THIS IS THE FIRST TIME IN NINE MONTHS THAT ANYBODY IN THIS BOROUGH HAS FOUND OUT THAT A THING IN IT HAS AN ORIGIN NOBODY CAN NAME, AND THE ORIGIN IS NOT A DOCUMENT AND NOT A PERSON ANYBODY CAN BE ASKED ABOUT.** The crate is the part that worries the fruit seller and the crate is not his: a crate of bottles is a thing on a pavement with a man's routine in it, and a man's routine in a thing is the whole difference between a table and a facility. And the cost, in numbers, that nobody is going to count: four empties in a crate is a number of people who drank some water on a Saturday in July in a sun, and it is a number of bottles, and it is not the same number, because a person can drink two, and a number of people with nobody's name on it is a list of people, and this borough has two of those already and has never once wanted a third. At about five the man from the cold store put the tables in, took the box in, went round the side for the crate, and put four empties and two fulls into a sack on the way in, and the pavement had nothing on it at all by about ten past five. Nobody was thanked. The register's blank line is 234 days, the card in the slot 148, the letter 150.

**Chapter 0176 — A Month Old. Sunday the nineteenth of July 2015, from about half past ten in the morning, a first-floor room over a shop in Tideglass.** He asks no question of anybody. No Lattice notice in that room. **THE SHEET WENT ROUND THIS BOROUGH ON FRIDAY THE NINETEENTH OF JUNE AND IT IS A MONTH OLD THIS MORNING, AND IT IS IN NINE BUILDINGS AND NOBODY IN ANY OF THEM KNOWS WHERE IT CAME FROM.** Four people, every one right about something. **A WOMAN OF ABOUT FORTY-THREE, WHO WORKS IN THAT ROOM ON SUNDAYS AND WAS NOT IN IT IN JUNE, PROPOSED THAT IT BE PRINTED AGAIN — four hundred copies, in trays, round every building in the borough on a Friday, with the lid off, asking nothing of anybody — AND IT IS THE CHEAPEST THING ANYBODY HAS DONE ON THOSE FOUR STREETS IN NINE MONTHS, AND EVERYTHING ELSE THAT HAPPENED IN JUNE WAS SOMEBODY STANDING SOMEWHERE.** **A MAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-FOUR, A DUTY CLERK WHO IS THE PERSON A PRINTING RUN GOES THROUGH, AGREED WITH HER AND THEN SAID HE WOULD NOT DO IT, TWICE, FOR TWO DIFFERENT CORRECT REASONS: a sheet put round on a schedule is a service, and a service has a person who sends it, and that person is findable; and the second copy's column is the only piece of paper in nine buildings that anybody could ever answer, and if a third copy went round without it then the two of them would argue about which is current and the answer to that is a date.** **A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-SIX, WHO HAS THE KEYS, WAS AGAINST IT, ON THE GROUNDS SHE HEARD FROM A WOMAN OF FIFTY-SEVEN CARRYING A TRAY IN JUNE: the June sheet reached nine buildings because it went round in a tray with nine other things in it, two of them a lunch menu and a leaflet about a closure, and you cannot ask about a thing that arrived with a lunch menu in it, and sending trays round on purpose takes that away and puts a schedule in its place in about five months, and a schedule is a person.** He said one thing, late, unasked, in two sentences: the second copy is the one to be careful of and none of you are talking about it, and it is dangerous not because of the words under the column but because it is the only piece of paper in nine buildings that anybody could ever answer. **THE PROPOSAL WAS NOT STOPPED AND NOT HELPED AND NOT MINUTED AND NOT REFUSED AND NOT AGREED, AND A MAN STANDING UP IN A ROOM WITH AN IDEA IS NOT A REQUEST. The June sheet was not withdrawn, the second sheet was not withdrawn, and nobody in any of the nine buildings knows there are two of them. The man of sixty-four took two hundred June sheets out of a cupboard on 10 July because that is what happens to the second hundred of anything in a building with a tray round.** At the door, at about twenty to twelve, the woman of fifty-six said to him that it is the cheapest thing anybody has done on those four streets this year, that it has got no name on it, and that is the whole of why it works, and the day somebody asks her why it works she will have to say who told her and she is not going to — and told him that so that he could be the person she does not tell, and he said he would be that person. **In about a year somebody is going to want to know where that sentence came from, and three people in that room could answer it, and which of them will is not going to be written down either, and the reader is not told.** It does not go in a minute and it is not a fourth answer. The register's blank line is 235 days, the card 149, the letter 151.

**Chapter 0177 — Two Hundred Yards And A Gate. Tuesday the twenty-first of July 2015, from about ten in the morning, a first-floor room over a builder's merchant on an industrial road.** He asks no question of anybody. No Lattice notice. **A CORRECT REQUEST, GRANTED QUICKLY, IN A ROOM, WITH NO PAPER ON IT, AND THE COST OF IT LANDS FOUR MILES AWAY ON A PERSON WHO WAS NOT IN THAT ROOM, WHO IS NOT IN THIS BOROUGH, WHO IS NOT OWED ANYTHING, AND WHO IS NEVER GOING TO BE TOLD.** A woman of about sixty-one, market trader of about twenty-two years, is on site at five; she has asked for a tap twice this year, was polite both times, and has stopped asking; she asked for a loo, in about that many words, and did not explain. **A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE, A PROJECT COORDINATOR, SAID YES IN ABOUT THREE SENTENCES: there is a welfare hut in the yard on this compound, it has been locked since June, it is not ours, it is standing here until the next job, there is a unit on the water inside it and a tap on the wall outside it; put your people on the corner by the gate and not by the office, and be off by half six, because the gate is shut by a man who will not be nice about it; and I will have the hut open by twelve and I am going to leave the padlock unlatched, and that is not permission, that is a man who has not locked it.** No paper, no reference, nothing written down, nobody asked him to write anything, and nobody in this borough has been given a reference for a loo this year. **AND HERE IS WHAT IT COST. The unit is hired from a yard over the boundary. It was booked into that yard on Friday 17 July at about ten past four by a man with a job and a compound and a padlock. Before that it was pencilled in on a board for a market hall in that same next borough, and the pencilled booking was released on the Friday afternoon at about half past three by the woman who keeps that board, because one firm booking and one pencilled one is a very ordinary Friday. So a market hall four miles away is still without a cistern, and it will be on the Tuesday and the Wednesday and probably longer.** THE PERSON PAYING IS A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-THREE WHO HAS THE KEYS TO THAT HALL AND CLEANS IT HERSELF AT HALF PAST SIX ON A CONTRACT WITH HER NAME AND AN ADDRESS ON IT, and who has been telling six traders a day for six weeks that the toilets are at the leisure centre, and who is telling them the truth, and who does not know that a unit was released off a board on a Friday evening. **NOBODY IS GOING TO TELL HER, AND THE REASON IS NOT DISCRETION AND NOT KINDNESS AND IT DID NOT OCCUR TO ANYBODY AS A DECISION: SHE IS WRITTEN DOWN. The day anybody rings that contract to ask whether a unit was released on the Friday, she stops being a woman who cleans a hall and becomes a person who has been asked about, and she will have to remember it in front of somebody who has come a long way to find out. A PERSON WHO IS WRITTEN DOWN TO DO A THING IS A PERSON SOMEBODY CAN RING ABOUT IT.** He could have rung the yard, driven four miles, or asked the man of fifty-five four words in daylight, and used none of them, and the reason is about him and not about the market: he is on nothing, has no department, there is no building he could ask in on a Tuesday, and the whole of his standing is that he can say a true thing out loud to a person in a room, and that goes into the room and has never once come back with an answer. **Nobody is hurt, nobody dies, nothing is helped: a thing has been moved from a place nobody was looking at to a place nobody is looking at, the traders wash at a compound about two hundred yards and a gate away and are standing at a pitch for another hour and a half afterwards, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS PLAINLY THAT THIS IS THE CHEAPEST OUTCOME ANYWHERE IN THIS BOROUGH AND IS ALSO THE REASON THERE IS NOTHING IN THIS BOROUGH ANYBODY CAN POINT AT.** He is not Colin Wharton and no Weir resident is described in anything. The register's blank line is 237 days, the card 151, the letter 153.

**Chapter 0178 — Not For The Bags. Wednesday the twenty-second of July 2015, from about half past three in the afternoon, a block of flats off a parade of shops in Tideglass, and a stairwell with a half-landing and a window at the turn.** He asks no question of anybody, he carried nothing, and he says nothing. No Lattice notice. **A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-NINE, WHO LIVES ON THE SECOND FLOOR, TOOK TWO BAGS OFF A WOMAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-SEVEN AT THE BOTTOM OF THAT STAIRCELL WITHOUT ASKING AND CARRIED FOUR UP FOUR FLOORS, IN DAYLIGHT, IN FRONT OF PEOPLE.** She came in with four full bags from a supermarket and was going to do it in four goes and her fingers had gone white. He went down past her, came back up with his hands out, took two bags and said *it is four floors and a bag each, I have to go down anyway*. **There is no arrangement, no rota, no list and no person he cannot say no to, and nobody asked him to.** A man with a pushchair waited on the half-landing, two people at the bottom stepped aside, a woman at a window looked down and looked away, nobody offered and nobody came up behind him with a third bag. He put the bags on her floor and said he was going down and would be two minutes ahead of her and she said she would come in a minute and he said do not bother. **THIS IS THE SECOND TIME IN A MONTH THIS BOROUGH HAS SEEN THIS SHAPE, AND THE SHAPE IS THE SAME AND THE PERSON IS DIFFERENT AND THE STREET AND THE WEEK ARE DIFFERENT, AND WHETHER IT IS THE SAME THING IS NOT SAID.** On the sixteenth a man of sixty-three carried four buckets up a flight of steps in front of about nine people. The one word that differs is that a bag of shopping is the cheapest thing anybody here has ever been asked to carry, and the reason it costs nothing is that it is worth nothing, and that is the entire mechanism, worked out independently in about nine places in nine months and written down in none of them. **AND THEN SHE SAID THANK YOU, AND IT WAS NOT FOR THE BAGS: she thanked him for telling her in June that the water would not be off on the Wednesday, on the Monday, in a corridor, when she could still have done something about it, so that she did not have to fill a kettle for a fortnight. He said it was on a board. She said it was on a board in a corridor and he read it and he told her, and nobody has ever asked him for that and nobody is going to. THE THANKING WENT TO THE CORRIDOR, THE CARRYING WAS STANDING RIGHT THERE, AND NOBODY PUT THEM TOGETHER, INCLUDING THE MAN WHO WAS CARRYING.** In about a year she may tell it as a story about a man who carried her shopping, and by then the two will have been in the same story so long that the person telling it will not know which one was the favour. **AND THE COST FELL ON THE PERSON WHO WAS NOT BEING CARRIED ANYTHING, AND THAT PERSON WAS IN THE ROOM: a man of thirty-two was on that half-landing going down with nothing in his hands, and he is the only person in that block who knows both halves of it, and if anything is ever asked about that stairwell the person anybody would ask is him, and he has never in his life been the person anybody brings an answer back to.** HE HAD A WORD FOR IT IN JUNE AND IT IS NOT HIS: it belongs to a person of nineteen who is owed nothing and got it for nothing, and she had it on a footbridge in May about something else, and he did not say it then and is not going to say it here. **AND THERE WAS NO OTHER WORD. He looked for one on that half-landing for about as long as it takes to go down a flight of stairs and there was not one, and not having one is not better and it is not a principle and it did not occur to him as anything at all. IT IS A TUESDAY, AND THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A WORD THAT STOPS A THING HAPPENING AND NO WORD AT ALL IS NOT A MORAL POSITION. IT IS ONLY THAT THE BAG GOT CARRIED EITHER WAY.** The register's blank line is 238 days, the card 152, the letter 154.

**Chapter 0179 — Harker Street. Thursday the twenty-third of July 2015, from about two in the afternoon, a first-floor room over a shop on a parade of shops in Tideglass.** He asks no question of anybody and nobody asked him anything. No Lattice notice. **IT IS THE FIRST DAY IN ABOUT SIX WEEKS THAT ANYBODY IN THIS BOROUGH HAS HAD TO THINK ABOUT WEATHER. The window has been open since about one, there is no fan in it, and it is twenty-nine degrees, and NOTHING IN THAT ROOM MOVED BECAUSE OF IT.** Four people: a man of about sixty-nine, a woman of about fifty-eight who has the keys, a man of about seventy-four, and a man of thirty-two at the back with nothing in his hands. **THE MAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-NINE HAS LIVED ON HARKER STREET FOR TWELVE YEARS, IS ON NOTHING, AND HAS A CONSTITUENCY OF ONE STREET. HE SAID ONE THING AND HE SAID IT ONCE: THERE IS NOWHERE ON HARKER STREET TO SIT IN THE SHADE AFTER TWO O'CLOCK. A wall on the north side has about two feet of shadow on it at four in July, the south side has nothing, there are thirty-one doors, and he has counted them about four times this year because he keeps looking at them.** Asked who it is for, he said he did not know, and that it is not for old people, it is for whoever is out in the street at four o'clock in July, and he has watched three men try to do it in a fortnight and one of them do it in a hat. **THE MAN OF ABOUT SEVENTY-FOUR, WHO DROVE THAT STREET TWICE A DAY FOR TWENTY-TWO YEARS, SAID THE OTHER HALF AND IT IS WHY THE ROOM IS GOING TO BE A PROBLEM: in twenty-two years the one thing he could have done about anything on that street was stop and say something; there is no list, no form and nobody he could have rung; and that has been the most useful thing about that street and it is going to be the most dangerous thing about it, and the two things are the same thing. If something ever did happen on that street, the person this borough would come to is him.** And the man of sixty-nine said about himself, once, and did not ask for it not to be minuted, and nothing is going to be minuted anyway: he has never asked anybody for anything in twelve years and is not going to start, and if somebody built him a bench on that street he would be the person who asked for it and then the person who can be asked why there is a bench, and in about two years he would be a man in a magazine with a photograph of a street with a man in it, and after that nobody on that street could say anything about the shade without him being in it. **EVERYBODY IN THAT ROOM AGREED WITH HIM, AND THE AGREEING IS THE COST, AND IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT HAPPENED THERE.** The woman of fifty-eight said it was right and not on anything; the man of seventy-four said he had driven past it two thousand times; **a man of thirty-two said one sentence, unasked, that a street with a person in a building who is right about it is not a service, does not become one, is not a document, and is now going to exist whether anybody in this borough likes it or not — and that there is no instrument in this city that can stop a room remembering a person and none that can tell him it has not.** The woman of fifty-eight said that is not a comfort, and he said no, it is not a comfort and it is not a threat and it is not anybody's fault; it is what a room is. **AND THE HEAT DID NOTHING. At about half past three she said it was the first hot day since June and he said in 1998 it had been thirty-four, and nobody connected that to anything, and nobody in that room suggested a tap, or a bottle of water, or a rota, or a form, or a list, or a shade, and nobody went out of the room. A hot day is not a reason to rebuild a rota and the rota has not been rebuilt, is not a reason to look at a board, and is not a reason to look at a second line under anybody's handwriting, and nobody looked.** HE WAS ASKED NOTHING FOR THE WHOLE TIME HE WAS IN THAT ROOM: a man of thirty-two has asked no question of anybody since the twenty-fifth of February and did not ask one, and it is the one afternoon in this borough where he could have asked two good ones and got good answers and it would have cost a man of sixty-nine about ninety seconds of his life. Nobody asked his name, nobody asked which number he lives at, and nobody wrote Harker Street down on anything. He left at about four, walked to the parade, got on the bus, went nine stops to a shop he has been going to for twelve years, and the man of seventy-four said good afternoon to him on the stairs. The register's blank line is 239 days, the card 153, the letter 155.

**Chapter 0180 — Emptied On A Friday. Friday the twenty-fourth of July 2015, from about half past eight in the morning, the ground floor of the Old Ward, and the cupboard under the stairs.** He asks no question of anybody and he says nothing. No Lattice notice. **THE CUPBOARD IS EMPTIED ON A FRIDAY BY WHOEVER COMES THROUGH WITH A SACK, AND THE TRAY THAT WENT INTO IT ON THE TWENTY-NINTH OF JUNE WENT OUT AGAIN, AND THE SACK WENT INTO A SKIP.** There is no rota for the cupboard; the building's Friday rota covers a different floor. The man with the sack is about thirty-six and is the same man who counted that shelf on 23 June, painted that room on 29 June and carried the tray down at about nine that morning, and **he has not been asked about the tray, was not asked then, is not being asked now and is not going to be.** Emptied in the order things come out: string, bulbs back in their box, fire blanket, stepladder, bucket, and then the tray. **WHAT WAS IN IT, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT ANYBODY IN THIS BOROUGH WILL EVER KNOW, AND THREE PEOPLE SAW IT: three meeting notices for a group that has not met since March, one of them a second reminder with a different date on it; a parking notice for a yard, with a yard on it and a date in June on it, and NOBODY IN THAT BUILDING CAN PLACE THE YARD AND IT HAS NOT BEEN ASKED ABOUT; AND ABOUT FIFTY PAGES OF SOMETHING SENT ROUND IN ONE BUILDING IN APRIL TO A LIST SOMEBODY HELD, WHICH CAME BACK OFF THE FRIDAY ROUND ON THE NINETEENTH OF JUNE AND DID NOT GO OUT AGAIN.** Nobody looked at what it was. Nobody in that building, nobody on the floor above, nobody in this city. The man of thirty-six asked *do you want that out* in the tone of a man clearing a cupboard, and was told *it goes with the rest*, and he put the sixty pieces into the sack with the string and the bucket, and the sack went out of the back door across a small yard into a skip, and the skip is out at the back because it is Friday. **AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME IN NINE MONTHS THAT A PIECE OF THIS BOROUGH'S PAPERWORK HAS ACTUALLY BEEN DESTROYED — NOT FILED, NOT MOVED, NOT PUT IN A CUPBOARD, NOT SCANNED — AND IT IS NOT SAID WHETHER THAT IS A LOSS OR A CORRECTION, AND THIS IS NOT A RHETORICAL WAY OF PUTTING IT: both are available, they do not exclude each other, and no instrument in this city can tell which one it is, because telling would require somebody to have decided, and nobody decided, and the only person who ever came near deciding it said *say it's a tray* in a room on 29 June and went back to a counter.** The woman of about fifty came down at about half past eight, stood in the doorway for about a minute and a half, looked at the cupboard and the man and the sack, said nothing, and went back up. **SHE IS THE ONLY INSTRUMENT THAT COULD SAY WHAT WAS IN THAT TRAY AND SHE IS NOT GOING TO BE ASKED, AND NOT BECAUSE SHE IS DIFFICULT: IF SHE IS ASKED THEN IT WAS A DECISION, AND IF IT WAS A DECISION IT WAS MADE BY A PERSON, AND THE NEXT TIME A TRAY COMES BACK OFF A FRIDAY SOMEBODY WILL SAY *LAST TIME WE MADE A DECISION ABOUT A TRAY*, AND THE SECOND TIME A THING IS A DECISION IT HAS A PRECEDENT, AND A PRECEDENT HAS A NAME ON IT, AND THE NAME ON IT WOULD BE HERS.** And the two of them are both entirely right and neither will ever know that the other one is: she — it was post that came back and was never post again, a list would have cost a person, a tray cost a Friday, and on the day she made that choice it was the cheapest of the three things available to her and she was on her own time; he — it was a tray of paper, and paper is not a record, and nothing in that cupboard had a shelf, or a place, or a person, and a thing nobody can put a name on is a thing nobody can be asked about. Both are true and they cannot both be tested, because testing means asking one of them a question, and asking is what turns it into a decision. **HE STOOD IN THAT VESTIBULE FOR ABOUT TWENTY MINUTES AND SAID NOTHING AND ASKED NOTHING AND WROTE NOTHING DOWN, AND DID NOT PICK UP A PAGE, AND DID NOT READ ONE, AND DID NOT ASK THE MAN OF THIRTY-SIX WHAT THE FIFTY PAGES WERE, AND DID NOT ASK HIM TO REMEMBER.** Nothing was minuted and nothing at all was described in anything that leaves that building, because nothing was written. The register's blank line is 240 days, the card 154, the letter 156.

**Chapter 0181 — The Bench. Sunday the twenty-sixth of July 2015, from about two in the afternoon, the forecourt of a block of flats and the pavement outside it.** He asks no question of anybody. **The only Lattice notice in that forecourt, on the wall by the bin store, and it defines nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a bench on a pavement is not an inspection, no person is required to report a bench, clean a bench or answer for a bench, and a bench on a pavement is a bench on a pavement.** The bench is a two-slat bench on two cast-iron ends, about nine years old, facing a wall with nothing on it, with a plate on the iron end the size of a playing card and nothing written on it because there has never been anything to write on it, and nobody in this borough has ever looked at it to establish that. **Somebody in this borough is obliged to deal with it — not a person, a thing of this borough, a schedule held by a works depot on the far side of the tracks, which lists street furniture on estates and says in the ordinary way that such things are inspected and defects are reported.** Nobody has to do anything about it this afternoon. The man who comes is about twenty-seven with a flatbed and a clipboard; he comes to that estate when he is on that estate; the depot gives him about nine estates a week and the nine are not the same nine every week; the list of the nine is in a building nobody in that block has ever seen. **HE WAS LAST AT THAT BENCH IN APRIL AND HE HAS NOT BEEN BACK AND NOTHING WILL BRING HIM BACK. A DUTY IS AN ACT AND NOT A PLACE: the duty is not the bench, the bench is a place, a place can be pointed at, and a place that can be pointed at is a thing this borough has spent nine months refusing to produce; the duty is that somebody has to look at it, an act has to be done by a person, the person is not on a rota, the rota cannot be rebuilt, and the reason the rota cannot be rebuilt is that nobody in this borough is under any obligation to rebuild it.** Everybody knows that. Nobody says it. A rota is a list of people who cannot say no; put a name against that act and it is a job, and a job can be moved and a job can be asked why it did not happen, and it would be a young man on a Friday afternoon being asked where April went. **AND AT ABOUT TEN PAST TWO A WOMAN OF ABOUT SEVENTY-ONE CAME OUT OF THE BLOCK WITH A CLOTH AND WIPED THE LEFT-HAND SLAT, AND SHE DID IT BECAUSE SHE WAS GOING TO SIT ON IT.** She had the cloth in her coat pocket, which means she knew before she came out. There is grit on that slat and there has been since before April. **NOBODY IN THAT BLOCK SAW HER DO IT AND NOBODY IN THAT BLOCK KNOWS THAT A DUTY EXISTS THAT HAS NOT BEEN DONE, BECAUSE A DUTY THAT HAS NOT BEEN DONE IS A THING YOU CAN ONLY KNOW ABOUT FROM A LIST, AND THERE IS NO LIST IN THAT BLOCK, AND THE NOTICE ON THE WALL SAYS IN THREE LINES THAT NOBODY HAS TO DO ANYTHING ABOUT A BENCH, AND THAT NOTICE IS CORRECT AND IS ALSO THE REASON NOBODY IN THAT BLOCK IS GOING TO BE TOLD. NOBODY LIVING IN THAT BUILDING WILL EVER KNOW, NOT THIS YEAR AND NOT AFTER THE MAN OF TWENTY-SEVEN COMES BACK IN NOVEMBER, BECAUSE THEN THE BENCH WILL BE CLEAN AND HE WILL HAVE NOTHING TO WRITE, AND A MAN WITH A CLIPBOARD WHO HAS NOTHING TO WRITE IS A MAN WHO HAS A CLEAN DAY.** **Four hundred yards up the road, past the parade, is the office that would know when the man of twenty-seven comes to that estate, and it was shut because it was Sunday.
