Thursday the twenty-fourth of September 2015, from about ten in the morning, a street in Tideglass.** He asks no question. **The only Lattice notice on the street, on a railing, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a sheet of paper about a shape says nothing about what anybody did on the street it is about, a thing done on a street before anybody asked is not wrong, and nothing on this notice is held against any person.** **NOTHING HAS HAPPENED TO ANYBODY ON THIS STREET SINCE FRIDAY AND THERE ARE MORE PEOPLE ON IT THAN THERE WERE, AND NOBODY CAN SAY WHY.** About nine people are on it; a man in a hired jacket has been down twice this week to look and says the second time was better; a woman of about twenty-two came to see whether this street was one of the eight and it is not a street, it is a district, and there is no district for a bit of one. **A PLACE THAT HAS BEEN DISCUSSED IS A PLACE THAT HAS BEEN DISMISSED.** The drawing went out on the Friday morning into four places, was on forty walls by that night, has gone onto more since, and nobody has said how many; forty is the one figure and no chapter in this batch states another. At the bottom of the yard a doorway has sandbags stood against its frame two deep, a new ferrule on a stopcock, a key in the hole, pallets of block moved to the wall side of the yard, a dry floor with dust on it and a broom in a corner. **AND THE FINDING IS THAT SOMEBODY USED THE DRAWING TO DO A CORRECT THING BEFORE ANYBODY ASKED AND IT CANNOT BE CHECKED BY ANYTHING:** he cannot establish that the man of about fifty-seven read the sheet and never will be able to, and the reason is not concealment, it is that the sheet has no address on it and not one word about a street, a yard, a gate, a kerb or a run of surface water. If the doorway had flooded on the Tuesday night there would be a man sweeping water out of it with a yard brush; if it had not, there is nothing at all. And the other way is the same: a loss in a yard would be a thing that happened to people and not a thing anybody could be shown happened because of a decision, because there was no decision — there was a man, a key and four hours. **A man a price makes findable is a different man from a man a shape in a room makes findable, and the two are not in one sentence.** He puts a corner of a sheet back against a shutter. **A person who is not counted is not a person who is helped, and a drawing on a shutter is not a count, and a man did a correct thing because of a map and nobody counted him and nobody is going to and the yard is dry.** The register's blank line is 302 days, the card 216, the letter 218.

**Chapter 0196 — The Permission. Wednesday the thirtieth of September 2015, from about eleven in the morning, a first-floor room over a shop in Tideglass.** He asks no question and says one sentence. A document came in by hand: **a mutual-aid permission, two pages, reference AM/15/221, between this city and Alderwick, correct in every sentence, signed at both ends, and it is the first document in nine months with a person's name on it.** Its seven clauses are printed in the chapter: a person named may be asked to work in the other city for not exceeding fourteen days; a person asked takes the work or does not take it at the hour the work begins; a person named is paid the printed going rate in money in full before the work begins; a person named keeps a right of return on the day the work ends without asking anybody for anything; where a person is receiving care in one city the other city pays and the person does not move; a claim arising out of work done under it is made in the city where the work was done and not in the city the person came from; and nothing in it requires a person to be asked, to be found, to be named or to be told anything. **THERE IS NO LINE UNDER EITHER SIGNATURE WITH NOTHING IN IT, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING HE LOOKED AT; SOMEBODY IN THIS CITY SIGNED IT AT A COUNTER IN A BUILDING BY THE WATER AND NOBODY COULD SAY WHICH OF THE PEOPLE ON THAT COUNTER, AND THE WATER OFFICE DOES NOT HAVE A LIST EITHER.** A woman of about fifty-two, Irene Sandiford, a duty clerk, read it out, said she was not the person who agreed to it and could not say whether it was a good idea, said both of those were correct, and went back on the twelve-fifteen. The schedule carries **nine** names. The eighth row is **ASHGROVE, EWEN, ABOUT SIXTY-TWO** — one room, second floor, a house in Kilburn Street, left in the second week of April, fourteen days' rent outstanding to the person who let it, entry made 11 August 2015, at Alderwick since 11 August on a fourteen-day contract renewed six times. **AND THE GOOD NEWS IS THAT A PERSON THIS BOROUGH COULD NOT FIND HAS BEEN FOUND, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH ASKED FOR IT AND NOBODY IS GOING TO BE ABLE TO SAY WHETHER IT IS A RESCUE, AND IT IS NOT A RESCUE.** About ninety pounds has been in a tin in a drawer in Kilburn Street since April and the person who let the room has been to three places in this city about it and has been told the correct thing at all three. A duty clerk was sent a schedule to fill in, one of the names on it went to a person who had been carrying it, and nobody had a reason to take one out. *A man of about sixty-two is now in a document.* The register's blank line is 308 days, the card 222, the letter 224.

**Chapter 0197 — The Kerb. Tuesday the sixth of October 2015, from about ten past six in the morning, a yard entrance in Tideglass.** He asks no question. **The only Lattice notice at that yard entrance, on a gate post, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a permission says a person may go somewhere, it does not say the person has to go, it also does not say the person has to come back, and nothing on this notice is held against any person.** **HE WAS TOLD AT TEN PAST SIX IN THE MORNING BY A MAN HE HAD MET ONCE, WITH HIS SLEEPING BAG ALREADY IN THE CAB, AND HE WENT, AND HE IS ALL RIGHT, AND HE IS GONE.** A man of about thirty-seven with his own tipper and a flatbed loads a kettle, a charger, two clean shirts and his tools in an order he has done before. **HE IS ON NO ROTA AND ON NOTHING AND THERE IS NO LIST IN THIS CITY WITH HIS NAME ON IT.** A man of about sixty-seven from the water side, with a waterproof and a lanyard, who met him once in June when a pallet of pipe went into a pond, reads a line off a folded piece of A4 and puts the paper in his pocket: *There's fourteen days. Pay's in the cab, it's in an envelope, it's the whole of it, it's before you start, and it's the going rate for that work over there, not the going rate here, and it's more than the going rate here.* He had said yes on the Saturday and nobody told him in between. A woman of about twenty-seven over the yard gates has a box of his washing and will keep it until the twentieth, and says *you said yes on Saturday and it's Tuesday morning*, and then stops, because there is no way of asking a person a question about that which is not a question about the answer. **AND WHAT A PERMISSION DOES TO A PERSON WHO CANNOT DECLINE IS MAKE HIM FINDBLE FIRST: he is findable because he has a telephone and that is the whole of his address, and on Saturday a man wrote that number on a folded piece of A4. A MAN A PRICE MAKES FINDABLE IS A DIFFERENT MAN FROM A MAN A SHAPE IN A ROOM MAKES FINDABLE, AND THE TWO ARE NOT GOING INTO ONE SENTENCE.** **AND HE WENT, AND HE IS ALL RIGHT, AND HE IS PAID, AND HE IS GONE, AND THIS BOROUGH HAS NEVER HAD A MECHANISM FOR A PERSON COMING BACK AND THERE IS NOT GOING TO BE ONE:** clause four gives a right to come back and not a way of being brought back, a right of return needs nothing and a mechanism for a return needs somebody to be in it, and if this borough had one then somebody here could say out loud that a man of about thirty-seven was due back on the twentieth, and that sentence about a person would then exist, and he would be a person somebody could ask about. The young man in the high-visibility jacket writes something on a borrowed clipboard. The register's blank line is 314 days, the card 228, the letter 230.

**Chapter 0198 — The Low Corner. Monday the twelfth of October 2015, from about ten to five in the morning, the bottom of Peverell Street in Tideglass.** He asks no question. **The only Lattice notice at that point, on the railings, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: water does not ask anybody permission, a thing done at night in the dark is not wrong and is also not right, and nothing on this notice is held against any person.** **THE RAIN CAME IN FROM THE WEST DURING THE NIGHT AND STOPPED BEING HEAVY AT ABOUT HALF PAST SEVEN; FOUR PEOPLE DID THE FOUR CORRECT THINGS, A FIFTH THING HAPPENED THAT IS NOT CORRECT AND IS NOT WRONG, AND NOBODY DIED.** The run was at six inches on 24 September and was at two feet and rising. About five people are on that ground and they are the same four or five as in May, June and August, and they are not chosen, they are not on anything, they cannot be sent for, and there is nothing anywhere in this city that could put a sixth person into a yard at ten to five in the morning. **AND AT ABOUT TEN TO FIVE SOMEBODY WENT ALONG THE OLD BRICK BASE OF A CLOSE-BOARDED FENCE AND PULLED THREE BOARDS OFF THE BOTTOM, AND THE WATER WENT THROUGH, AND THE WALL STOOD.** He was about ten feet away with a spade facing the other way, heard it, turned round, saw a light behind a man and a set of boots and then there was nothing, **DID NOT SEE A FACE AND DID NOT ASK, AND THERE IS NOBODY IN THIS CITY HE COULD HAVE SAID IT TO EVEN IF HE HAD.** Two doorways stayed dry. A yard next door took about a foot and a man of about seventy-seven lost a shelf of stock and said that anybody with a bucket could have done it, which was true, and that there is no way on God's earth of finding out who, which was also true. The boards went down the yard and under the run and were not seen again. The man of about fifty-seven, who had bought two hundred bags on the Saturday morning after the eighteenth and put forty across his own doorway on the Sunday night because of a sheet of paper with no address on it, finished on about six of them, and Jonas Mercer carried four up the street without saying why and he said nothing and took them. **AND NOBODY FOUND OUT, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME AND IT IS ALSO THE ONLY THING THAT MAKES THE MORNING WORK.** A woman of about twenty-two opened nine doors between about four and about eight off a list on the back of an envelope and did not knock on one of them and there is no list of which ones. The register's blank line is 320 days, the card 234, the letter 236.

**Chapter 0199 — The Back Room. Sunday the eighteenth of October 2015, from about half past two in the afternoon, a room over a shop in Tideglass.** He asks no question. No Lattice notice. About nine people at a Sunday branch meeting in a room that is free on Sundays because the people in it work six days, and a woman of about thirty-six called Mrs Obi taking the minutes in her own hand on a pad she takes home in a handbag. **TOMAS RENN SAID THE ONE SENTENCE NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH HAS SAID OUT LOUD IN A ROOM: A PERMISSION AND AN OBLIGATION ARE OPPOSITES, AND THIS BOROUGH HAS BEEN LIVING ON THE SECOND ONE FOR NINE MONTHS, AND IT WAS HANDED THE FIRST ONE EIGHTEEN DAYS AGO IN PRINT, AND A MAN WENT OFF WITH IT TWELVE DAYS AGO ON A TUESDAY MORNING IN AN ENVELOPE. THE EIGHTEEN IS FROM WEDNESDAY 30 SEPTEMBER AND THE TWELVE FROM TUESDAY 6 OCTOBER; A REVIEW FOUND *SIX DAYS* HERE AND IN THREE OTHER STATE FILES AND IT WAS NOT AN INTERVAL IN THIS ACCOUNT, AND THE PROSE WAS CORRECTED AT THE SOURCE FIRST.** His three asks, minuted and still correct: a bond, not money but something a person hands over before taking a decision that affects other people and gets back if the decision was right; tools that belong to nobody, one set at the shop on a Friday for anybody with a job and no van; and **the person who does the work saying whether the work is safe — which is clause one, clause three and the field in clause two with four things in it of the document made in August, which he asked for in a room like this one in March, and which HE IS NOT WITHDRAWING AND IS GOING TO KEEP ASKING FOR IN THIS ROOM EVERY THREE MONTHS.** Nobody argued with him and a man in an apron said *he's right* to nobody in particular. He then reads the two clauses against each other out loud: one of them is a door, the other one is a hand on it, and this borough has been standing on the hand for nine months and the hand does not need a reason and nobody has ever been able to write the reason down. **JONAS MERCER IS RIGHT TOO AND COULD NOT IMPROVE IT AND DID NOT TRY:** he had a better sentence ready, that a permission stops being a permission the minute somebody needs it, and he did not say it; he said *you are right* and *there is nothing I can put next to it*, and then gave Renn the one true thing he had — **he has asked for three things and not one of them has ever been said no to, and that is the reason he has not got any of them, and it is not the reason anybody in this city would give if they were asked.** Renn said it was the first useful thing anybody had said to him in six months. **AND RENN'S OWN QUESTION IS UNANSWERED AND IS STILL THE ENGINE, AND HE SAID ALOUD IN THAT ROOM THAT IN THE SPRING HE IS GOING TO PUT IT TO SOMEBODY WHO CAN ANSWER IT, AND THAT IT IS NOT GOING TO BE JONAS MERCER, AND THAT JONAS MERCER IS NOT GOING TO BE IN THE ROOM, AND HE TOLD HIM THAT THEN SO THAT HE COULD NOT STAND IN A CORRIDOR IN SIX MONTHS AND SAY NOBODY THOUGHT HE SHOULD HAVE BEEN THERE.** Jonas said *that's right*. Yolanda Fofana is not named and is not in a room and is not told anything. The register's blank line is 326 days, the card 240, the letter 242.

**Chapter 0200 — The Boxes. Saturday the twenty-fourth of October 2015, from about ten in the morning, the open covenants legal clinic in Tideglass.** No Lattice notice. **THERE ARE FOUR CARDBOARD BOXES ON THE TABLE UNDER THE WINDOW WITH THE WORD PARTY WRITTEN ON THEM IN MARKER PEN AND THEY HAVE BEEN EMPTY SINCE THE CLINIC OPENED, AND A PARTY IN A THING LIKE THIS IS A PERSON OR A BODY THAT CAN BE NAMED AS ONE SIDE OF IT, AND THERE IS NO MONEY IN THIS CITY FOR A BOX.** A man of about seventy-six came in with a folded piece of A4 and a question that had a person's name in it: **Ashgrove, whose name is not his, and who was his tenant and is his tenant's was.** He let the room in Kilburn Street in 2011, the man was in it until April, walked out in the second week of it owing fourteen days, the room was let again in June, and about ninety pounds has been in a tin in a drawer since April and has not been touched and is not going to be. **AND NELL ARDENT GIVES A CORRECT ANSWER THAT NOBODY CAN ACT ON, AND SHE IS RIGHT, AND SHE IS THE ONLY PERSON IN THE ROOM WHO IS, AND BEING RIGHT IS NOT A FINDING AND IS NOT A VICTORY AND IS NOT A LOSS.** No document in either city mentions a landlord, a room, a deposit, an arrears or a sum of money, and the clause about claims is about claims arising out of work and his money is not that, so he can hand it over and nobody can stop him and nobody will know. And if he does, two things happen: a man with money sent to him is a man with a bank, and a bank is a thing that can be looked at, and he is currently only findable because a duty clerk put a line next to his name in a list; and he will have done a thing, and there is no place in this city to write down that a landlord in Kilburn Street offered a man ninety pounds in October and was refused, or accepted, or ignored, or never got an answer. *So what do I do.* **Nothing today. That is the answer.** A man of about seventy-one who volunteers there is right that there are solicitors in Alderwick and that a power of attorney could be got, and she agrees with all of it and does not answer it. She said it to about nine people in three years and about five of them were not glad to hear it. Jonas Mercer was in the corridor and not in the room; she came out and said: *the day I start telling a man what he is in a corridor is the day this room turns into something else, and it would not be a good something.* He said thank you to her on the stairs. The register's blank line is 332 days, the card 246, the letter 248.

**Chapter 0201 — The Drawer. Friday the thirtieth of October 2015, from about half past three in the afternoon, a canteen in a building in Tideglass.** He asks no question. **The only Lattice notice on the canteen window, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a thing done on a Friday is a thing done on a Friday, a note about it is a note about somebody, and nothing on this notice is held against any person.** **THE HATCH ON THAT CANTEEN GOES UP ON A FRIDAY AFTERNOON FOR ONE MAN AND ONE PERSON PUTS IT UP, AND THE ONLY THING IN THIS BOROUGH THAT COULD BE CALLED A LEVEL OF SERVICE IS A PRINTED SHEET THAT WENT ROUND NINE BUILDINGS IN JUNE WITH NINE LINES ON IT, EVERY ONE OF THEM SAYING *no requirement stated*, AND IT IS IN ALL NINE OF THOSE BUILDINGS STILL, AND NOBODY PUT A NAME ON IT.** The head was re-cut by a review because it opened on the printed sheet, which is a `state/current.md` object, and not on the canteen; the one permitted use of the phrase survives, about the printed row. The canteen shuts its hatch at two and has for about nine years; a woman of about sixty-four called Beryl has worked behind it for six years and is on nothing and there is no document in that building with her name on it. A man of about thirty-one comes in at about ten to three every Friday and has done since he was at the college, and she opens the hatch for him on her own unpaid time with a mop, a bucket and about six minutes of a gas ring, and nobody asked her to and nobody can. **AND SOMEBODY SAID THE SENTENCE THAT IS ALWAYS AVAILABLE IN THAT KIND OF ROOM, WHICH IS THAT SOMEBODY OUGHT TO WRITE IT DOWN, AND IT WAS A MAN WHO WANTS HIS TEA AND IS IN NO HURRY, AND A WOMAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-FOUR BEHIND A HATCH THAT SHUTS AT TWO SAID NO, AND SHE WAS RIGHT ON EVERY PART OF IT.** **A DRAFT OF THIS LINE GAVE IT A NUMBER — *THE ELEVENTH TIME*, AND HE HAD BEEN COUNTING SINCE THE SPRING — AND BOTH WERE CUT: *THE ELEVENTH TIME* IS A CLOSED FIGURE IN THIS ACCOUNT AND A RUNNING TALLY IN JONAS MERCER'S HEAD IS THE ONE INSTRUMENT THIS BOROUGH HAS SPENT NINE MONTHS REFUSING TO BUILD.** She gives three correct reasons why it is not written down: a piece of paper saying a thing was done on a Friday turns that building into a building where things get written down, and it took a year and a half in the last one for the writing down to become somebody else's job, and then there is a man upstairs who wants to know how many people come through that hatch on a Friday; and a note without a name is a note about a hatch that anybody could have done, and in nine months somebody will ask who did it, and she will either say it was her, which puts her name in a second thing, or say it was nobody in particular, which is a lie about a Friday. **AND THEN SHE DID SOMETHING NOBODY HAS DONE IN THIS BOROUGH FOR NINE MONTHS, AND SHE DID IT ON PURPOSE, AND SHE PAID FOR IT HERSELF.** At about ten to four she took the back of a bread delivery docket off the pad and wrote *Fri. hatch open. till 6.* — five words, no date, no year, no hatch number, the last stroke through the printer's word underneath, and the truth is that she shut it at about half past four. She folded it once, put it in a drawer under the counter that has no lock on it and never has, and shut the drawer. **HE SAW HER DO IT AND SHE KNEW HE SAW HER DO IT AND NEITHER OF THEM SAID A WORD AND HE IS NOT GOING TO ASK HER ABOUT IT AND HE IS NOT GOING TO TELL ANYBODY, AND NO LIST OF PEOPLE WHO CANNOT BE FOUND HAS BEEN BUILT IN THIS BOROUGH IN NINE MONTHS AND ONE HAS NOT BEEN STARTED.** The register's blank line is 338 days, the card 252, the letter 254.

**Chapter 0202 — Nobody Asked Me. Tuesday the third of November 2015, from about half past three in the afternoon, a first-floor room over a shop in Tideglass.** He asks no question and says one question about nothing. No Lattice notice. **A MAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-TWO CAME ACROSS THE ESTUARY ON MONDAY MORNING TO FIND OUT WHY HIS NAME WAS ON A PIECE OF PAPER IN A CITY HE HAD LEFT IN APRIL, AND NOBODY BROUGHT HIM AND NOBODY ASKED HIM TO COME.** He got a letter on Friday from a woman in Alderwick saying his details had been passed to a city he used to live in, with a reference and an offer to object in writing; he has not written, and he came over on the Monday morning boat and has been sitting in a café since Monday morning because he did not know what to do with it. *If I write I am in it, and if I am in it then somebody over there is in it, and I have been in it since the eleventh of August without anybody asking me and I would rather just be in it quietly.* **AND THEN HE SAID IT BETTER HIMSELF, AND HE SAID IT TWICE, AND BOTH TIMES IT WAS TRUE, AND NOBODY OBJECTED TO ANY PART OF IT: NOBODY ASKED ME TO BE FOUND.** A woman of about thirty-eight at the back of the room had got as far as the true thing — a permission finds people the same way the August document finds them, and the only difference is the handwriting and the fact that one of them was signed twice — and stopped, because a person in a room saying that is heard as an objection and she was not objecting and about four people in that room thought the same sentence at the same moment. He said it had cost him nothing, that nobody had come and found him, and that he would not go back to the room in Kilburn Street on a Tuesday. **AND THEN HE SAID THE PART NOBODY IN THE ROOM WANTED:** a doctor over there in a town he cannot name, paid for out of a council that has never heard of him, and he has a card for it, and it is correct, and he cannot say no to it, and he would like to; and everything in the arrangement can be got out of by writing, and he cannot write, and that is the whole of what is wrong with him and it is not a thing their document has done. He told Jonas Mercer he knew who he was on the Friday in September and was not asking him about it. *He is on a schedule in two cities. He is the most counted man in this building.* *He has never been asked one thing.* The row with his name on it went back across the water with no mark against it anywhere. The register's blank line is 342 days, the card 256, the letter 258.

**Chapter 0203 — The Square. Saturday the seventh of November 2015, from about half past ten in the morning, a hall off a parade of shops in Tideglass.** He asks no question. No Lattice notice. **A WOMAN WHO HAS THE KEY TO A ROOM ASKED HIM IN FRONT OF A ROOMFUL OF PEOPLE WHICH SQUARE ON THE DRAWING IS THE EMPTY ONE AND WHAT IS SUPPOSED TO GO IN IT, AND HE TOLD HER THE TRUTH, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME HE HAS SAID ANYTHING ABOUT IT TO ANYBODY.** She has had the key for about nine years, lets the hall out for a Saturday class and a Wednesday mothers' group out of a notebook in a drawer, and put a copy of the drawing on the inside wall on the Friday, because a man of about twenty-seven had done four without being asked and because the ones on shutters are outside and this one is inside where the people are. About nine people in the hall. **AND SHE ASKED HIM IN THE MIDDLE OF THE ROOM, IN DAYLIGHT, WITH EVERYBODY LOOKING, BECAUSE SHE HAD BEEN ASKED FOUR TIMES THAT WEEK AND SHE IS THE ONE WHO HAS TO STAND IN THAT ROOM AND SHE IS NOT PUTTING HER NAME TO AN ANSWER SHE HAS NOT GOT.** *I do not know what goes in it.* And then: *I read that sheet on the eighteenth of September, before it went on any wall, and it has been empty on every copy of it that has been put up since, and I have not said that to anybody until this morning, and I am not going to guess. If I told you what went in that square I would be making it up, and I have not made anything up in this borough for nine months and I am not going to start on a Saturday.* She said *it is a fact, it is not a better answer*, and he said *it is a worse one, and you should be annoyed with me*. The room then offered six correct and useless answers: a district nobody has made yet (it has no term in it); a person (a seat on that sheet is a shape with a name over it and there is no name over this one, and there is no person on any of that paper anywhere and that is not an oversight); a poster since 18 September; the place where you put the thing you have not decided yet. **WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS NOTHING:** somebody drew a square and left it, and the line that comes into it goes nowhere because there is nothing on the other end of it yet. *So somebody left a room.* *Somebody left a room, or somebody is going to walk into it, and I know which of those two I would rather it was, and I have not got a reason.* **NOTHING WAS RESOLVED AND THE SQUARE IS NOT FILLED AND HE WAS GIVEN NOTHING** — no department, no form, nothing stood up and given to him, because it was half past ten on a Saturday and the nine people had come about a class and about a warm room. **THE SENTENCE IS IN THE ROOM NOW AND CANNOT BE GOT BACK OUT OF IT, AND THERE IS NO WAY OF KNOWING ON ANY EVENING IN DECEMBER WHICH ROOM IT IS IN OR WHO IS IN IT. A ROOM CAN HOLD A SENTENCE AND A ROOM CANNOT HOLD A PERSON, AND IT IS A SENTENCE OF CHAPTER 0144 AND IT NOW SITS INSIDE THAT PARAGRAPH INSTEAD OF STANDING ALONE ABOVE IT AS A COMMENT ON THE SCENE.** The register's blank line is 345 days, the card 260, the letter 262.

**Chapter 0204 — The Gully. Tuesday the tenth of November 2015, from about six in the evening, the low end of Peverell Street in Tideglass.** He asks no question. **The only Lattice notice on that street that evening, on a post, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a door you can get out of is a door, nobody has to have done anything to it, and nothing on this notice is held against any person.** **TWO PEOPLE CLEARED A GULLY OUTSIDE A DOOR ON AN ORDINARY TUESDAY EVENING, AND NEITHER OF THEM IS ON ANYTHING, AND NOBODY IS GOING TO FIND OUT.** The water of Monday 12 October had gone out of the city by the Wednesday, the river is down about two feet, and there is about an inch of silt on the pavement from the top of the yard to the fourth door back. A man of about fifty-four with a handcart and a fridge and a shovel stopped at the third door, had the gully open in about ten minutes, and was still at it at about a quarter past seven, because a gully is not a hole and it is not the top of it that matters. A woman of about eighty-five came out about ten minutes after he started, went in and came out with a stiff broom and a bucket, and swept what he had put on the pavement down to the kerb. *You've not got a brush for it.* *I've a bar.* *You've a bar and you've got no brush. That's not a criticism, that's a survey.* He gave her the bar when the gully was open and she gave it back, and that is the whole of what was said between them, and neither of them knew the other's name. **AND JONAS MERCER WAS THE ONLY PERSON ON THAT STREET WHO SAW ANY OF IT, AND HE DID NOT ASK EITHER OF THEM ANYTHING, AND THERE IS NOBODY IN THIS CITY HE COULD HAVE HANDLED IT TO.** A man of about thirty-seven went back across the water on Monday and is out again on Thursday, the money is in an envelope before the work, and nobody in this borough has asked him one question. A man of about sixty-two came across on Monday morning to find out why his name was on a piece of paper and said out loud in a room on Tuesday that nobody had asked him to be found. **Everything that has happened on this stretch of this city in seven weeks is correct and none of it is written down, and the drawing is on more walls than it was in September and nobody can say how many, and there is a square in the middle of every copy of it with nothing in it.** **A permission is a thing a person may do. An obligation is a thing a person has to do. This borough has stood on the second of those for nine months and has never once been asked to show anybody what it did, and about six weeks ago a sheet of two pages came from a city on the other side of the water with the first of them on it in print, signed at both ends, correct in every sentence, and it is in force on this street tonight, and it is in force in a yard at the bottom of a street where a man with a pump and his own bags kept a doorway dry in September and nobody is ever going to know. NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH HAS WORKED OUT WHAT EITHER OF THEM WAS HANDED. IT IS THE TENTH OF NOVEMBER AND IT IS OPEN, AND A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-FOUR AND A WOMAN OF ABOUT EIGHTY-FIVE HAVE GONE IN ABOUT A QUARTER PAST SEVEN.** The register's blank line is 349 days, the card 263, the letter 265.

## Volume 05, Batch 0002 — Chapters 205–214

**Chapter 0205 — The Line. Wednesday the eleventh of November 2015, from about nine in the morning, a first-floor room over a shop in Tideglass, and then a building by the water.** He asks nobody a question and says the mechanism out loud. **AT ABOUT NINE IN THE MORNING ALL SEVEN CLAUSES OF THE ORDER MADE IN THIS CITY ON THE THIRTEENTH OF AUGUST STOPPED BEING IN FORCE AT THE SAME MOMENT, AND NOBODY DID ANYTHING, AND NOBODY WAS ASKED, AND NOTHING WAS CANCELLED, AND THE LINE UNDER THE DATE ON PAGE TWO IS STILL EMPTY AND HAS BEEN EMPTY SINCE THE THIRTEENTH OF AUGUST.** He puts a cup of tea down and something that has been on since the middle of August is not on, and there is no sound. **The only Lattice notice in the lobby of that building, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a line under a date is not a signature, arriving on the day is a different act from putting a name in it, and neither of those is false and neither of them is a duty.** He goes and asks Nina Calder, records supervisor, nineteen years in that building, seven refusals, for a book, having asked her for nothing in a long time. **The field is not a field: a working book about two inches deep on a table by the wall, a column ruled in pencil with a name, the hour called, the hour home and the thing the person was called for, a run of entries in one hand from the middle of August to 14 September, not emptied, not wiped, no line through anything, no note in the margin. *It is not a field any more.* *No. It is a column with things in it.*** **The mechanism, in a quarter of an hour:** a clause that says an order is renewed, or is not renewed, needs a person; there is no body in this city that can require a person, and a thing that needs a person is not a thing a city can do by itself; it came off what it was standing on at nine o'clock and did not come to the end of itself because there is nothing in it that ends; it has not expired and it has not been cancelled and somebody would have had to cancel it. **There are two people in this city with a department over any of this, one of whom made it and one of whom did not, and neither of them is going to be asked to sign anything and he is not going to ask them, because asking would mean picking one of them, and there is no answer to that which is not him deciding which of the two this city ought to be frightened of. Neither is named.** The second half of the card in a Methodist hall about two miles away, *a body that cannot require anybody cannot be told what it will do*, has been on that card since the spring and he has read it about nine times and every one of those times it was a fact about a meeting he was not at, and it is the first thing it has ever been the answer to. **THE PERMITTED SAINT ORRA GATE SENTENCE IS USED ONCE HERE, UNSTAGED, AS THE ONLY THING HE KNOWS IN THIS CITY THAT GOES ON BY ITSELF: a gate that goes up at seven on a Sunday morning and stops at six on the Sunday morning after that, six days long and not a week, with no date on it anywhere in this city. That is what a thing looks like when it does not need a person, and it is not a moral advantage, it is only a thing that does not need a person.** Then the thing nobody is told: **he has not had anything to do about clause six since the eighteenth of September, and that was the only reason he had anything to do about it — it was in force, and the only thing anybody could do to it was stop it, and you can only stop something that exists; he has been the only person in this city who could tell you which of two clauses outranks the other since the fifteenth of August, and that is not a gift anybody gave him, that is a hole in a piece of paper and he has been standing in it.** *And now you're standing in a hole with nothing in it.* *Yes.* **A man of about twenty-three at the top of Peverell Street with a back that has been bad since the spring, who came out on 18 September because a hand went on him, is not a man who has been let go. His back is in nobody's field because there is no field, nobody in this city was told that this is what happened, nobody could be told, and if he said it in a room it would sound like a man explaining why the thing he had been standing in had stopped.** He walks past him at about eleven and does not stop and the man does not look round. **The register is still at nineteen, the line under the nineteenth is still blank, and it is still the only thing in that building that has not moved, and that is the first finding of the eleventh of November and it is not a relief.** Day-counts at this date: 350 / 264 / 266.

**Chapter 0206 — What Is Left. Tuesday the seventeenth of November 2015, from about ten in the morning, the low end of Peverell Street in Tideglass, and then a vestibule on the ground floor.** He asks nobody a question and says one word. **A MAN OF ABOUT SEVENTY-THREE HELD A GATE OPEN FOR NINE HOURS IN AUGUST, WAS PAID THE GOING RATE, WAS CALLED NINE TIMES SINCE THE TWENTY-SECOND OF AUGUST, HAS DECLINED NOTHING, AND ON TUESDAY THE SEVENTEENTH OF NOVEMBER HE WAS NOT CALLED AGAIN, AND HE SAID NOTHING ABOUT IT TO ANYBODY, AND SOMEBODY NOTICED.** He has spent six days not walking the city, on the grounds that a person who has heard a thing stop cannot tell the difference between a thing that has stopped and a thing he has decided has stopped. He walks it in fifty minutes and it is all exactly as it was: a quarter of an inch of silt on the pavement at the low end, the gully outside the third door packed with it because a gully silts up in a month and nobody came back with a bar, the drawing on the shutter at the top and the shutter at the bottom and the inside wall of the hall with its square still empty, and nothing taken down and nothing new put up and no gap anywhere he could put a finger into. **The man of about seventy-three is at the corner by the parade with his coat over his arm and nothing in his hands, and that is the difference, and Jonas Mercer could not have put it in a sentence afterwards if he had tried for a week, and it was not that he looked unhappy or looked well or looked like a man who had been let off something.** He said good morning. He is not a man who has been set free and nobody is going to say that he has. **The only Lattice notice in that vestibule, on the inside of the glass, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a question asked at this counter is a question and nothing else, so is the answer, and no answer given here is a record of anything.** The vestibule has three doors off it and a shuttered shop with a telephone number in the window, and the counter is the width of two people, and a woman of about sixty-five has been behind it for about nine years and has never been told anything. **A MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-EIGHT, WHO WAS IN THE ROOM OVER A SHOP ON THE THIRTIETH OF SEPTEMBER AND SAID ONE SENTENCE ABOUT A SCHEDULE AND A RATE, AND WHO HAD BEEN IN THAT VESTIBULE ONCE BEFORE IN JUNE, CAME IN AND ASKED WHETHER THERE IS ANYWHERE A PERSON CAN PUT THE LOW END OF PEVERELL STREET. THE ANSWER HE GOT, TWICE AND IN THE SAME WORDS, WAS *THERE'S NO FORM FOR THAT*, AND HE SAID *I KNOW*, AND THAT IS WHERE IT STOPPED.** He had been trying since June to get the bottom of that street onto any piece of paper that exists in a drawer in this city; there is a drawing on the walls and no bottom of Peverell Street on it, and he knew that, and he came anyway, because the answer was going to be worse in a room than at a counter and he wanted to have asked it in a room with somebody in it. **He said one other thing, once, to the floor, and did not tell anybody, including Jonas Mercer, who stood at the other end of the vestibule the whole time: since the middle of September there has been no reason on any street in this city for anybody to be asked anything at all, and he had noticed it the way a man notices a bus that has stopped coming.** *Right. Same time in a month, if you're here. — I'm here on Tuesdays.* **Nothing is minuted, nothing is put on a sheet, the gully outside the third door is still packed, and the counter answered nothing and gave no count and was not asked about the order, a gate, a rota, a person, a permission or a lapse.** The exact motif *there is no form in this borough* is at zero in this chapter; the shorter construction is the counter's answer, twice, and is about a street. Day-counts: 356 / 270 / 272.

**Chapter 0207 — Not A Party. Sunday the twenty-second of November 2015, from about eleven in the morning, a parade of shops in Tideglass.** He asks no question and says one sentence to three people. **A REGIONAL GROUP THAT RUNS THE WATER FOR THREE TOWNS WROTE ABOUT A THING THAT CROSSED AN ESTUARY IN SEPTEMBER AND ASKED FOR A PERSON TO COME AND SIT IN A ROOM IN ANOTHER CITY, AND HE SAID HE WOULD GO BUT NOT ALONE, AND HE SAID IT OUT LOUD TO THREE PEOPLE BEFORE ANYBODY HAD ASKED HIM FOR ANYTHING, AND WHAT HE SAID WAS THAT HE WAS GOING AS A PERSON WHO WAS THERE AND NOT AS ANYBODY'S DELEGATE, AND THE ARRANGEMENT HAS NO WORD FOR WHAT THAT IS.** The letter came on the Friday, one page, polite, signed by **Iselin Krogh, about fifty-one, the clerk of that group, not the person who decided to write it**. It thanks this city for the arrangement of the thirtieth of September, asks to hear the account of the person who stopped a clause on the eighteenth of September from the person who stopped it, invites him to a sitting on the fourth of December, and in its fourth paragraph says: *We record you as our correspondent on the above.* **The word is not true. There is no budget for this, there is nothing in this borough he can book a seat on and no way of booking one anywhere else, and nothing in this borough that can make him be in a room in another city, and the whole of what they have got is a man who has gone.** He wrote back on the Saturday, on a sheet of his own, saying he would come and would sit in the room and was not their correspondent and was not anybody's delegate, and that if the group had a word for a person who is in a room and is not standing for anything he would be glad to have it. **The only Lattice notice in the stairwell of the building the clinic is in, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a letter can ask for a person without naming a job, a person can say yes to a room and no to a seat, and nothing agreed like that is a minute of anything.** He said it first to Nell Ardent on the stairs, who had also been sent a copy by somebody she could not identify and is not going to find out; *that is the first useful thing anybody has said to me since about March, and it is a definition, and I am not going to tell you what it is a definition of, and the day either of us starts writing that kind of thing down is the day this borough has an office of it.* *I'm not agreeing to anything.* Then to Sanaa Iqbal in a hospital car park, who let him say it before he had got to it and then said: *I am not going to be the reason you are not in a room, and I am not going to be the reason you are in one either, and if I find out afterwards that either of those things happened I am going to be extremely unpleasant about it, and you can tell them that when you write. Twenty minutes a week, and the paragraph behind it where it has always been, and neither of those has moved since September.* Then to Tomas Renn in a room over a shop, before Renn could ask him anything. **And Renn's answer is the finding of the chapter: IT IS THE FIRST TIME ANYBODY HAS SAID THAT SENTENCE TO HIM BEFORE BEING ASKED. IN NINE MONTHS. HE HAS BEEN ON THE OTHER SIDE OF IT ABOUT NINE TIMES, HE HAS NEVER ONCE BEEN TOLD IN ADVANCE, AND EVERY SINGLE TIME HE HAS COST HIMSELF THE WHOLE OF THE EVENING GETTING IT RIGHT ON HIS OWN IN A CORRIDOR FIRST.** *So yes. Go. And I will come, and I have not said when, and you do not get to decide that either.* **And the thing nobody worked out, which is still open: how did a standing group of three authorities in another city hear of a sheet of two pages that went down on a counter by the water in front of six people on the thirtieth of September and went back across the estuary in a plastic wallet. The permission from Alderwick is the reason that letter exists and not one of the three has worked out what that means.** Day-counts: 361 / 275 / 277.

**Chapter 0208 — The Crossing. Sunday the twenty-ninth of November 2015, from about half past six in the morning, a doorway in Tideglass, and then the landing, and then the water.** **FOUR PEOPLE WENT ACROSS THE ESTUARY ON THE MORNING OF THE TWENTY-NINTH OF NOVEMBER AND NONE OF THEM HAD BEEN IN A ROOM WITH THE OTHER THREE SINCE SEPTEMBER, AND THE FIRST THING SAID WAS SAID IN A DOORWAY BY A WOMAN WHO HAD SAID IN ADVANCE THAT SHE WAS GOING TO SAY IT, AND IT WAS A BOUNDARY, AND IT WAS NOT A QUARREL, AND NONE OF THE FOUR IMPROVED IT.** No Lattice notice. At about half past six, with the boat at ten past seven, **Sanaa Iqbal says it in advance, on purpose, and will stop talking about it for the rest of the day: she is not going to be fixed; she is not going to be the reason anybody is talked out of anything or talked in to anything; and if she finds out in three weeks that either of those things happened she will be extremely unpleasant about it and he can put it in the letter; and she is going because there is a boat and four of them are on it and a room on the Friday, and she would have got in that boat if there had been three of them and if there had been five, and that is the whole of the reason and there is not a second reason underneath it.** *I am not going to argue with it in a doorway at half past six in the morning.* **They had not been in a room together since the middle of September, when two of them argued in front of about thirty people and stopped, and neither of them decided to stop.** Renn arrives with a holdall, a folder and a flask he brought on purpose and will not say so. Ardent with a rucksack, no coat, and a paper cup of coffee from a machine on the parade which she had to cross the road to reach, and she gives it to Iqbal and Iqbal drinks a third and hands it back and says thank you and neither of them found it difficult, which is the sort of thing a room full of these four used to be unable to get through. **NOBODY READ ANYTHING OUT. THERE WAS NO LIST AND NO ROLL AND NOBODY SAID ANYBODY'S NAME IN ORDER.** The boat is the smaller one and the engine is loud enough that anything said on the crossing is said standing at the rail; a bucket comes loose and goes the length of the deck; a woman with a dog comes on at the last minute; a man in a waterproof has a flat tray with four newspapers and a stone on it and is selling nothing and nobody asks him for anything. **Nell Ardent is sick over the side about a quarter of the way over and says *Don't* and is told *I wasn't going to*.** Then Renn, once the water has gone out of everybody's ears, asks what the room is like and is told nineteen chairs, a table the length of it, printed paper face down, a woman at the end who writes things down and argues with none of it, not a court, not a hearing, nobody whose job it is to be disappointed — and Jonas says the water is the best thing on that river and Renn says *You were about to tell me about the water.* **THEN JONAS TELLS RENN ABOUT THE ELEVENTH OF NOVEMBER, BECAUSE HE WILL FIND OUT IN ABOUT SIX WEEKS AND WOULD RATHER HEARD IT FROM HIM: a document made in this city on the eleventh of August, a line with a date under it on page two, and on Wednesday morning at nine o'clock the date came round and the document stopped being in force, all seven parts of it, at the same time, and nobody did anything and nobody was asked and nothing was cancelled. Nina Calder knows and wrote nothing down and is the only person in this city who knows. And the field is not empty and nobody wiped it; it is a column in a book on a table in a building by the water, and it is not a field any more, it is nine months of somebody's handwriting.** *That's not a resignation.* *No.* **And Renn refuses to be the one who says the rest of it out loud, because if he does it will be in Jonas's mouth for the rest of his life and he will be a man who was relieved of something.** Ardent has two questions for that room and neither is the expected one, and a third she will not be asking because she has no standing in that room and neither has anybody else on the boat; and *you are not on the agenda, and I am not on the agenda, and Tomas is not on the agenda, and neither is she. There is a line on a piece of paper with our names nowhere near it. I read it on the Friday. I would like it minuted that I read it.* They land at about ten past eight at a slip past a bridge; a man in a peaked cap says the works is the second one past the bridge. **Day-counts: 368 / 282 / 284.**

**Chapter 0209 — What Everybody Agrees About. Friday the fourth of December 2015, from about half past nine in the morning, a works office at the second pumping station past the bridge in Ravensmere.** **THE FIRST OF THE THREE REGIONAL SYSTEMS WORKS, IT IS CHEAP, IT IS CORRECT, IT HAS NOT FAILED, AND EVERY PART OF IT IS HELD BY SOMEBODY PRIVATELY, AND NOT ONE PERSON IN IT IS HIDING ANYTHING, AND A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE PUT TWO SENTENCES NEXT TO EACH OTHER IN A CORRIDOR AND THEN WISHED HE HAD NOT.** He asks no question. **The only Lattice notice in that lobby, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: using something is not the same as having a say in it, a reading belongs to the thing that was read, and neither of those is false.** Ravensmere takes water off an intake, filters it and delivers it to three towns; the works was built before anybody in that room was born, the bill went down when the filters were done, the pressure at the far end of the third town is good enough that the clinic there has not had to ask for a tank in nine years, and a standpipe at the edge of the second town costs a person nothing and asks nothing. There is a night rota on the wall and he reads every name on it and learns nothing. About fourteen people in the room and printed paper face down in front of every chair, which he has seen done once, in a room over a shop in his own city, on the eighteenth of September, and he does not say so. **Iselin Krogh does the first twenty minutes and every sentence is right: the group is three authorities and about six staff; nothing in it asks a person to give anything up; nothing about it is secret; and a person who uses the standpipe and gives nothing has exactly the same rights as a person who uses it and gives everything, and that is deliberate, and she says the word deliberate out loud and nobody at the table disagrees.** **What they cannot do is tell you what happens to a reading, and it is not kept back, it is not theirs: in the first town the works is a company's, in the second the mains are a trust's, in the third one pumping station is municipal and the other two are not, and the two that are not have both changed hands inside ten years, and every time one changed hands nothing was broken and nothing was promised and the obligations stayed exactly where they were.** *Whose obligations.* *The region's. Which is a word that means the three of us and nobody else, and I will put my hand to that as a description of a legal arrangement and I will not put my hand to it as a description of a place.* **The sheet is good and clear and short and everything on it is true, and at the bottom, in the same type, the same size, with the same space above each, it says: *Nothing is required of any person in order to use any part of this system.* And: *A person has no standing in respect of anything recorded under this.*** He reads it twice and looks for ten minutes for anything about who keeps the readings and there is no way to look for the absence of a thing in a document and find it. **A man of about thirty-one, who comes to a canteen hatch at ten to three on Fridays in this city, is on nothing and is not a party to anything, and has crossed on a Friday boat and gone back on a Sunday four times since August and has told nobody, and he has been stood in that corridor twenty minutes and says: *that's two lines* — and, when Jonas agrees: *I'd rather I hadn't said that. Not because it's wrong. Because I've just said the only thing anybody's said about that wall in about ten years and I'm in a corridor, and I don't know who heard it, and I can't un-say it, and I'm going to have to go back into that room in twenty minutes and sit down.*** He goes back in and says nothing else all morning. **Nobody lied and nobody hid anything, and the two sentences were printed six inches apart on the same sheet by the same people on the same day, and one of them is a door and the other one is a hand on it, and everybody at the table thought it was a good sheet.** At one o'clock she gave him a copy in a plastic wallet: *That is yours. Take it with you. There is no charge for it and there is no record of who has taken one.* Day-counts: 373 / 287 / 289.

**Chapter 0210 — Two Names. Wednesday the ninth of December 2015, from about two in the afternoon, a second-floor office in Ravensmere and the corridor outside it.** He asks no question. **A MAN FROM THIS CITY WHO IS ON NOTHING IS BEING PAID BY A CITY ACROSS THE WATER FOR WORK HE IS DOING IN HIS OWN CITY, AND BOTH CITIES CALL IT SOMETHING DIFFERENT, AND HE IS THE ONLY PERSON WHO CAN EXPLAIN THE DIFFERENCE, AND NOBODY IS GOING TO ASK HIM.** **The only Lattice notice on the wall behind the table, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a person may be paid by a body they have never entered, the place a person works in is not the place that pays them, and both of those can be true at once and usually are.** On the second Wednesday of every month people come into a room with a tin on the table and are paid in envelopes and initial a corner of a sheet, and the money is in the envelope before the work, which is the condition of the whole arrangement and which nobody in the room thinks is remarkable. **THE LAST NAME ON THE SCHEDULE IS A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-NINE, and Jonas Mercer has had that sheet in his head since a duty clerk read nine names out in a room over a shop on the thirtieth of September, and he knew the name and did not use it, and there is nobody in that corridor who could have heard him use it.** He has a job at a pumping station in this city four days a week on the distribution side of the estuary, doing the work of two men. **The water undertaker here calls it a relief contract. Ravensmere's sheet calls it an attachment and says in one line what an attached man is, and the line says a man attached to the works. NOBODY IN THIS CITY COULD PRODUCE EITHER PIECE OF WRITING EVEN IF THEY WERE ASKED, BECAUSE THE PERMISSION IS IN A PLASTIC WALLET ON THE OTHER SIDE OF AN ESTUARY AND THE ATTACHMENT SHEET IS AT THE END OF A CORRIDOR IN ANOTHER CITY, AND WHAT HE HAS IS A NAME ON A SHEET IN EACH PLACE.** He crosses the estuary to be paid, four times since September, and will do it in January, and has a house and a road and a bed about two miles from where he stood at seven o'clock that morning and is attached to a works he has never once been asked inside. **JONAS MERCER STOOD IN THE CORRIDOR, COULD HAVE ASKED HIM ONE QUESTION, AND DID NOT. HE IS THE ONLY PERSON IN EITHER CITY WHO COULD HAVE, BECAUSE HE IS THE ONLY PERSON WHO HAS READ BOTH OF THE TWO WORDS. HE IS NOT GOING TO. THE ENVELOPE WAS STILL SEALED WHEN THE MAN WENT DOWN IN THE LIFT AT ABOUT FOUR O'CLOCK AND THEY DID NOT EXCHANGE ANOTHER WORD. THE ARRANGEMENT IS IN WRITING AND THE WRITING IS CORRECT.** The afternoon item, which he was in the corridor for and did not hear, was two documents both taken from that permission: **the number the arrangement had moved, which is six, and the six dates on a sheet in a duty clerk's bag; and the sentence about where a claim arising out of the work is made, read out by Iselin Krogh in the voice she uses for things that are already settled, and nobody argued with it, and the minute says the item was noted.** **A PRICED-ACCESS CASE IS NOT A RECOGNITION CASE. A DUTY IS AN ACT AND NOT A PLACE. A PERSON WHO IS NOT COUNTED IS NOT A PERSON WHO IS HELPED.** Day-counts: 378 / 292 / 294.

**Chapter 0211 — The Corridor. Tuesday the fifteenth of December 2015, from about half past three in the afternoon, a first-floor corridor at the works in Ravensmere.** He asks no question and says nothing at all. **A PERSON WITH STANDING IN THE FIRST OF THE THREE REGIONAL SYSTEMS SAID THE TRUE THING ABOUT THE BARGAIN INTO A CORRIDOR, TO ONE PERSON, COULD NOT FINISH THE SENTENCE, SAID IT ANYWAY, SAID AFTERWARDS THAT SHE SHOULD NOT HAVE SAID IT, AND IT WAS NOT TAKEN BACK, AND HE DID NOT REPEAT IT TO ANYBODY AND DID NOT WRITE IT DOWN.** No Lattice notice. The afternoon item is the standpipe hours and it takes fifty minutes and they get to seven in the morning to eight in the evening, which is nobody's number: the clinic in the third town wants it shut at eight because the last bus is at ten past eight and the people who use the standpipe after that are the people who walk to it, and the man from the first town wants it shut at six because the walk back in the dark is not four miles, it is longer, and nobody in the room is prepared to be the first to write the number down. **Outside, afterwards, Nell Ardent is at the far window with a cup of tea out of the machine at the bottom of the stairs and says the decision is correct and that she would have written it herself, and he says nothing at all, and they look at a car park for about six minutes.** Then Iselin Krogh comes out with a folder, turns left into a corridor, and stops. *I want to say a thing, and I am not going to finish it, and I have known I was not going to finish it since about the middle of November, and I have decided that not finishing it is worse than not saying it, which I did not think was possible in October.* She does not say it. She puts the folder on the window ledge and cleans her glasses. **The first half is about why she cannot: in that room the sentence is an accusation, and it is not an accusation, and there is no way of putting it in that room that it does not come out as one, and she has been in that building nineteen years and has stopped looking for a way round it.** Then she says it anyway, to him, in a corridor: **it is not a bargain between two things; it is an agreement between three of them and a great many people outside that building that the part everybody is responsible for will always be the part somebody owns; the obligations were written first and the ownership came afterwards in pieces over a generation in rooms she was not in; nobody has had to do anything wrong for any of that to happen and nobody in that room has done anything wrong and every part fits and the water is good and the standpipe runs and the filters were done on time; and the result of it, which nobody has ever put in a sentence in that room, is that the whole of the part of this that three towns are answerable for is the part that nobody owns, and the part nobody owns is the part that gets sold.** She stops there. **She cannot finish it because the next part is the part she cannot say, and if it comes out of that room it will be in a corridor in a building three towns away and then in a newspaper, and then the trust that owns the mains and the company that owns the works will both read it in a newspaper, and neither of them has done anything they can be shouted at for, and both of them will be gone inside a year, and the three towns will still have the same water and the same standpipe and the same sentence with a new set of names on the top of it.** *I should not have said that.* She says she said it to a man from a city three towns and an estuary away who has no standing here and no office and no department and no body behind him, which is the only reason she could not stop herself, and she goes back in and says nothing for another fifty minutes. **HE SAID NOTHING AT ALL AND THE NOTEBOOK IN THE INSIDE POCKET OF HIS COAT STAYED IN THE INSIDE POCKET OF HIS COAT, AND ON THE FRIDAY IN A ROOM OVER A SHOP SHE SAID *YOU'VE BEEN IN THAT BUILDING TWICE. WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT* AND HE SAID *NOTHING'S WRONG WITH IT. THE WATER'S GOOD*, AND SHE LOOKED AT HIM FOR SLIGHTLY TOO LONG AND WENT BACK TO HER PAPER, AND IT STAYED IN THE CORRIDOR WHERE SHE PUT IT.** Nobody was given authority and nobody's sentence improved. The standpipe hours are the only thing decided that week and the minute is in a filing room and it is not about anybody in this borough. Day-counts: 384 / 298 / 300.

**Chapter 0212 — An Ordinary Sunday. Sunday the twentieth of December 2015, from about two in the afternoon, a street in Ravensmere.** He asks nobody a question. **TWO SMALL CORRECT THINGS HAPPENED ON ONE SUNDAY AFTERNOON IN A CITY THAT IS NOT THIS ONE, AND NEITHER PERSON WAS ON ANYTHING, AND NOBODY FOUND OUT, AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME IN THREE MONTHS THAT A CORRECT THING HAS BEEN DONE IN A STREET BY SOMEBODY WHO IS ON NOTHING AND NOTHING HAS COME OF IT, THE FIRST BEING A DOORWAY KEPT DRY WITH A PUMP AND THE SECOND BEING A GULLY CLEARED WITH A BAR, AND THE ONLY PERSON WHO KNOWS BOTH OF THESE HAPPENED WALKED DOWN THE SAME STREET TWICE.** The group does not sit on a Sunday, nobody has given him anything to do in this city, and on the Monday after this one he would get a boat back across the water. **The first, at about twenty past two, in a queue of about seven outside a chemist's: a man of about eighty-four, third from the front, with a basket and a folded newspaper under it, says *that's the wrong price* and is wrong about the bottle and right about the label.** The window shows a smaller bottle at ninety-one pence and the shelf a larger one at a pound four. *Put a card on the big one.* *We're not doing cards on a Sunday.* *Then do it on a Monday, and do it before anybody's paid, and I don't mind. I'll be in on the Monday at about ten.* *I'll put a label in. I can't do a card.* *A label's a card. A label's a card with a price on it. I'll take the small one for the small money and you put the label in and nobody's been done out of anything.* He pays the window price and goes out; **the chemist writes a note on the back of her hand and puts the bottle somewhere else on the shelf, which is a system, and it is the whole of the system.** A label went in on the Monday at about ten past nine. Nobody saw him again and nobody is going to find out. **The only Lattice notice inside that bus shelter, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a time printed somewhere is not a time given to anybody, a sheet on a wall is a sheet on a wall, and neither of those is a promise. The second, smaller, four hundred yards up the same street, at about ten to three: a woman of about sixty-nine is right about a timetable.** The four o'clock bus comes at ten to, has done since the Sunday service was changed, nobody reprinted the timetable, and the board in the shelter and the sheet in a shop in the third town are not even out of the same year. *The driver's been driving it since the change. He knows. He doesn't say. You get on and he goes at ten to four and he looks at you in the mirror once and you can say what you like after that.* **And she is not going to stand in a shelter and shout at a bus driver about a printed sheet on a Sunday, and the four o'clock is at ten to until somebody who owns the printing says different, and she has not got an idea who that is and neither has Jonas Mercer.** They get on the bus and say nothing else and the driver looks in the mirror once. **They were four hundred yards apart and neither knew anything about the other, and he told neither of them anything, and by Monday morning there was a label on a shelf in a chemist's and a timetable in a bag and nothing else anywhere in either city.** Day-counts: 389 / 303 / 305.

**Chapter 0213 — The Claim. Saturday the twenty-sixth of December 2015, from about half past ten in the morning, a building by the water in Tideglass, and later that afternoon a telephone call to Ravensmere.** He asks no question and does not say what the document is. No Lattice notice. **A CLAIM CAME BACK TO THE CITY THAT GRANTED THE PERMISSION, IT IS CORRECT, IT ARRIVED IN AN ORDINARY WAY, IT IS ABOUT MONEY, AND THE CLAUSE THAT SENT IT IS THE SIXTH, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH CAN TELL WHETHER IT IS A PRICE, A RECEIPT OR A PRECEDENT.** He has come in on a Saturday for the second time since the eleventh of November, for the same reason and with the same result, which is that you cannot tell by looking at a book twice. The book is the same book, the column is the same column, **the last entry in it is the fourteenth of September, which is the last time anybody was called on, and it is the same length, and nothing sits at the end of it.** Nina Calder told him on the Thursday there was nothing to see and he came anyway and she said only that the door sticks. A woman from the sorting office brings a bundle, she signs for it, and then she reads the top one twice and puts it down face up and does not put it in the tray. **IT IS ONE SHEET, DATED THE ELEVENTH OF DECEMBER, CARRYING THE REFERENCE OF THE PERMISSION, HEADED AS A CLAIM MADE UNDER THE MUTUAL-AID PERMISSION OF THE THIRTIETH OF SEPTEMBER 2015 AND MADE IN THE CITY IN WHICH THE WORK WAS DONE. IT NAMES ONE MAN, WHO IS ABOUT TWENTY, WHO WAS EMPLOYED FOR FOURTEEN DAYS IN OCTOBER AT A PUMPING STATION ON THE NORTH BANK AT ALDERWICK, WHO WAS INJURED ON THE LAST DAY OF THAT FORTNIGHT, AND WHO CLAIMS A SUM THAT IS ABOUT WHAT A MAN OF THAT AGE COSTS TO KEEP FOR ABOUT A MONTH. THE LAST PARAGRAPH ASKS THE AUTHORITY THAT GRANTED THE PERMISSION TO PROVIDE THE SUM. IT IS ADDRESSED TO THE WATER OFFICE, WHICH IS TWO FLOORS UP AND HAD GONE FOR CHRISTMAS.** **THE SIXTH CLAUSE SAYS A CLAIM ARISING OUT OF WORK DONE UNDER THE PERMISSION IS MADE IN THE CITY WHERE THE WORK WAS DONE AND NOT IN THE CITY THE PERSON CAME FROM. THE CLAIM IS MADE IN ALDERWICK. IT IS CORRECTLY MADE. IT HAS COME TO THE CITY THAT GRANTED IT, AND IT CANNOT BE DEALT WITH HERE.** It goes into a tray under a window, which is a tray and is not a register, and *I would like you to put it in the tray* and *put it in the tray*, and she puts it in the tray. **AND HE KNEW WHAT IT WAS AND HE DID NOT SAY SO AND HE DID NOT GO AND FIND THE MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY.** It is a price, because the first thing to come back to a city that handed something out for nothing is a bill. It is a receipt, because six people here took fourteen days across the estuary in October, were paid in an envelope before the work, all six came home on the dates on a sheet, one of the six has since had a claim made about him, and nothing here could tell those two things apart. It is a precedent, because if this borough answers it then it has agreed that the permission runs backwards as well as forwards, and if it does not answer it then a man of about twenty who worked a fortnight at a pumping station and came home has not got anybody. **All three are true and they are not the same shape and this borough has no instrument for choosing between them, because a body that cannot require anybody to do anything cannot be told what it will do, and because the two people with a department are not going to write anything down this Christmas, and because the woman in another city has one of her own and is not going to be asked by anybody to put hers next to this one.** Then, on the Saturday afternoon, he telephones Ravensmere, and Iselin Krogh says before he has got to anything that she had a letter with the same reference on it on the eighteenth and has put it in a folder in a drawer, and when he asks what it is she says *I am not going to say that on a telephone. You have not told me what yours is*, and he says he has a letter as well, and she says *I did not think you had not.* **NEITHER OF THEM SAID WHAT EITHER OF THEM HAD, AND BY THE TIME SOMEBODY ELSE KNEW WHAT IT WAS THERE WERE TWO OF THEM IN TWO CITIES AND THERE IS NO DOCUMENT IN EITHER OF THOSE TWO CITIES THAT SAYS THAT EITHER OF THEM KNEW. THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-SEVEN IS NOT THE MAN THIS IS ABOUT AND IS NOT IN ONE SENTENCE WITH HIM.** The man of about twenty was at a football match in this city that afternoon with about eight hundred other people. Day-counts: 395 / 309 / 311.

**Chapter 0214 — Two Hands. Wednesday the thirtieth of December 2015, from about seven in the evening, a first-floor room over a shop in Ravensmere.** He asks no question. **ON THE LAST EVENING OF THE YEAR THERE ARE TWO PIECES OF PAPER IN THIS CITY AND BOTH OF THEM ARE IN FORCE, AND ONE OF THEM IS A PERMISSION AND ONE OF THEM IS AN OBLIGATION, AND THEY DESCRIBE THE SAME ACT, AND ONE OF THEM IS SHORTER THAN THE OTHER, AND NOBODY IN EITHER CITY CAN SAY WHICH OF THE TWO THE PEOPLE WERE HANDED.** **The only Lattice notice on the wall of that room, and it defines nothing, requires nothing and nothing on it defines *holder*: a sheet on a wall and a sheet in an office can both be in force, one of them is shorter, and neither of them is a lie.** The room has a gas ring that does not work and an electric one that does. Jonas Mercer has the office sheet in a plastic wallet in his inside coat pocket, given to him in a corridor on the fourth of December, no charge, no record of who has taken one. **Nell Ardent has four sheets of her own on the table: the top two in her own writing, the third the group's printed agenda for the fourth of December with two lines pencilled beside item three, the fourth empty.** The first sheet is the corridor wall sheet, and it says one thing and only this: *Nothing is required of any person in order to use any part of this system.* — one line, six inches of type, four inches of white underneath it — and there is a woman of about seventy-three who comes to that standpipe at about half past six every morning and has been coming since before the filters were done and has never in her life been asked for anything and is right not to be. **The second is the office sheet: the same first line, in the same type, and under it, at the same size, with the same space above it, *A person has no standing in respect of anything recorded under this.*** Same type, same size, same sheet, same printing, same day near enough, because both carry the date the filters were done in a footnote. **One of them has had a line taken off it, and it has not been left blank, it has been taken off, and the four inches underneath are white and they are not white because there was nothing there.** Then, as a fact about two pieces of paper, and unanswered: **a permission is a thing a person may do and an obligation is a thing a person has to do, and every one of those is a permission, and on the same sheet in the same type it says that whatever the water made a note of is now not yours to have a say about, and those are not two different systems, that is one system, and it has a front door and no back, and the front door is the sentence on the wall and the back of it is the sentence underneath, and the sentence underneath is not hidden from anybody, and if you never ask for it then the thing on the wall is the whole of what that region has ever told a person about itself.** *Which of the two did they hand them.* **That is exactly it, and I have not got an answer and I have looked, and I am not going to make one up in a room above a shop on the thirtieth of December, and if I did make one up then it would be the first thing anybody has said in nine months about any of this that was not true, and I would rather turn up in March with nothing.** Jonas Mercer says the answer is on the second sheet, and Ardent agrees and says the sheet with both lines on it is in an office in a building that owns a works and is not in any building in this borough, and the short one is on a wall about two hundred people a day go past without reading, and he is the only person who has asked. **And Sanaa Iqbal says: *Nobody is required to ask, and everybody who comes to that standpipe is better off than they would be if somebody stood at the end of it with a clipboard, and I want that said in this room, because in about six months one of us is going to be tempted to make this into a fight about the sheet, and it is not a fight about the sheet. It is a fight about whether two sentences that are both true can be printed one above the other. And the answer to that is yes, and I do not like it, and there is nothing anybody can do about it before the end of the week, and we should go home.*** **AND NOTHING WAS RENEWED ANYWHERE IN EITHER CITY THAT DAY, AND NOBODY NAMED ANYTHING, AND NOTHING WAS MINUTED, AND THE DOCUMENT MADE IN THIS CITY ON THE THIRTEENTH OF AUGUST IS NOT IN FORCE AND ITS LINE UNDER THE DATE ON PAGE TWO IS STILL EMPTY, AND THE ARRANGEMENT OF THE THIRTIETH OF SEPTEMBER IS IN FORCE, AND THE REGIONAL SYSTEM IS NOT GOING TO EXPLAIN ITSELF BEFORE THE END OF THE WEEK, AND NOTHING THAT HAD BEEN OPEN IN THIS BOROUGH SINCE THE SUMMER GOT CLOSED IN THAT ROOM, AND THE ONE THING THAT WENT IN WENT OUT EXACTLY AS IT WENT IN. NOBODY WAS RESCUED AND NOBODY DIED.** There was a bus at about ten past nine. The group does not sit between Christmas and the sixth. The early boat is at ten past seven on the Wednesday and all four of them will be on it. Day-counts: 399 / 313 / 315.

## Volume 05, Batch 0003 — Chapters 215–224

**Chapter 0215 — Five Things. Wednesday the sixth of January 2016, from about eleven in the morning, a corridor in Marrowgate, and then a room off it.** He asks one question of a room. Lattice notice. **THE SECOND OF THE THREE REGIONAL SYSTEMS IS CHEAPER THAN THE FIRST ONE AND BETTER, AND THE WHOLE OF WHAT THAT TOWN AGREES ABOUT IS THAT ONE NAMED MAN IS RESPONSIBLE FOR FIVE THINGS, AND NOBODY HAS ASKED HIM.** Marrowgate is a town of about three thousand, eight miles up the estuary past the works, and the town owns the works, the clinic, the shelter, the gate and the yard; a house has a water bill of about ninety pence a quarter and nobody who lives there has ever been asked for a card. **The clerk is Mavis Bray, sixty-six, twenty years in post, and every sentence she says is correct, including that the old filter was done by the people who owned the works and cost them money and cost the town nothing and was not generosity.** The man is **Walter Sallow, about eighty-six**, the fitter at that works for about fifty years, on the books at the going rate, in a house at a small rent, named on an arrangement on the wall. **He is not on a rota, there is no list, and the clerk has tried to write his job in a sentence eleven times and cannot.** The room's argument, and everybody agrees with all of it: a duty is an act and not a place, you cannot give a job to a man and you cannot give a man to a job, so he cannot be replaced, so nobody has asked him. The last step is never drawn and it is true. **He is the only person who can do any of the five and he is not in the room; at half past one Jonas Mercer walks up to the intake and finds him sitting on an upturned crate with his hat over his face, and does not go down and does not ask him anything.** The line he brings away, said to himself and to nobody: *a place cannot be handed over, so when the person goes, the thing goes, and everybody in that room has said yes to that, and none of them has thought about the day.* Word *warden* nowhere.

**Chapter 0216 — The Week. Tuesday the twelfth of January 2016, from about ten past five in the morning, the intake at Marrowgate.** No Lattice notice. **HE IS NOT ON A ROTA AND THERE IS NO LIST AND NOTHING HE DOES IS WRONG, AND HE HAS BEEN DOING IT FOR ELEVEN YEARS, AND HE COULD NOT EXPLAIN IT TO ANYBODY IF HE TRIED.** The intake screen is raked by hand from a steel platform with a rake older than he is; the water is off for the whole town while it is done, and it is done on a Tuesday and a Friday, and 0215 and 0223 are Wednesdays and neither of them shows him raking. **THERE IS NO TANK BIG ENOUGH, AND A WOMAN OF ABOUT EIGHTY WHO TAKES IN WASHING CANNOT START UNTIL THE WATER COMES BACK AT ABOUT EIGHT, AND HAS STOPPED WASHING ON THOSE TWO DAYS WITHOUT TELLING ANYBODY, AND THE TOWN'S HOSE HAS BEEN ON THE LORRY FOR YEARS AND NOBODY HAS COME.** The five things are walked in full: the intake, the clinic unlocked at eight and locked at six, the shelter boiler at a quarter to six and a night round at ten, the gate up at seven and down at six by hand because the motor was replaced in about 2010 by somebody hired for a day, and the yard with its corner of broken things that is not a skip. **THE MAJOR TURN: HE IS THE ONLY PERSON WHO COULD READ A PUMP HOUSE, STRIP A STOPCOCK, RELIGHT THE SHELTER BOILER, WORK THE RACK AND CHANGE THE CHAIN — AND HE IS NOT THE ONLY PERSON WHO DOES ANY OF IT.** A gardener rakes the yard, a woman of about seventy-four sweeps the clinic and said no once to somebody in an office in a different town and has not been asked again, a man of about ninety-one opened the gate on the only Sunday in nine years anybody can remember. He is asked in a yard whether it is a burden and says no, and says why: if he said it was a weight, somebody in that room would have to do something about it, and there is no version of that room doing something about it, and if he said it was fine that would be a lie. **HE WAS NOT RESCUED, HE WAS NOT ASKED TO STOP, NOTHING WAS ARRANGED FOR HIM.**

**Chapter 0217 — The Fourth Thing. Sunday the seventeenth of January 2016, from about half past two in the afternoon, a square in Marrowgate.** Lattice notice. **TWO SMALL CORRECT THINGS WERE DONE ON ONE AFTERNOON BY TWO PEOPLE WHO ARE ON NOTHING, FOUR HUNDRED YARDS APART, AND NOBODY FOUND OUT.** A man of about ninety is right that a bench has been four feet from the parish notice board instead of six since about 2008, for a funeral nine years ago; a man of about eighty-eight with a barrow walks it a foot and a half and neither asks the other for anything. On the other side of the square, a woman of about eighty-three is right that a hardware shop's door sign says half past eight when it has opened at a quarter to eight for a year, because the woman who opens it has a bus to get; it is done with a marker, it does not look very good, it rains on the Thursday, and it is done properly with a stencil on the Tuesday and nobody is told. **THE FOURTH TIME SINCE THE PUMP AT THE BOTTOM OF PEVERELL STREET, AND 0217 NAMES ALL THREE OF THE EARLIER ONES IN ITS OWN HEAD: the man of about fifty-seven and his pump in September in this borough; the man of about fifty-four with a handcart and the woman of about eighty-five with a broom and the gully on 10 November; and the man of about eighty-four with a basket and the woman of about sixty-nine four hundred yards apart in Ravensmere on 20 December.** The man who holds the five things is not in this chapter.

**Chapter 0218 — The Bill. Friday the twenty-second of January 2016, from about ten in the morning, a room in Marrowgate, and a yard.** No Lattice notice. **THE PAY IS GOOD, THE HOUSE IS GOOD, THE WORK IS ORDINARY, THE WRITING IS CORRECT, AND THE COST DOES NOT FALL ON HIM AND FALLS ON EVERYBODY ELSE, AND THE CORRECT SENTENCE ABOUT THAT SOUNDS LIKE AN OBJECTION.** The year: ninety pence a quarter for water, a shelter nobody has stayed in since the summer before last, a clinic on four days and five, a gate that is a chain on a bar and has never been a machine, and a works line that is a quarter of the sheet and is maintenance, materials and labour, and the labour is one man. The clerk will not have anybody believe the town is clever. **WHERE THE MONEY GOES WHEN THE MAN IS NOT WORKING: nine days in the February of the year before, something in his chest, a man hired from Nether End for three days who could not read the pump house and did not do the rack, water cloudy on the Thursday, the clinic shut for most of a day and about sixty people coming and going, the yard gate shut because nobody had a key, the shelter boiler out at about eleven on a Sunday night and got going at about half past one in the morning by a man of about ninety-one after two goes, and a fortnight of no washing. THE BILL FOR THOSE NINE DAYS WAS THREE DAYS OF THAT MAN, A FORTNIGHT OF THE MAN'S WAGES AND A TANK.** The figure for the works has not moved in eleven Januaries because there is no nine days line. **The clerk says all of it in a yard, to a man who is never going to be in that room, and then says the thing she has never said in that room, and says out loud that she is not asking anybody to do anything. ABOUT FOUR PEOPLE IN THE ROOM THINK THE SENTENCE AT THE SAME MOMENT AT HALF PAST TWO. NOBODY PUTS IT IN THE ROOM. JONAS MERCER WAS IN THE CORRIDOR OUTSIDE IT ALL DAY AND IS THE ONLY PERSON IN TWO COUNTRIES WHO COULD HAVE.** He asks for a copy of the four-line arrangement and refuses one himself. A woman of about seventy-five has come on the first of the month for nine years and has not been asked to be there.

**Chapter 0219 — Not Worse. Thursday the twenty-eighth of January 2016, from about half past four in the afternoon, a parade of shops in Tideglass, and then a hall off the parade.** Lattice notice. **HE HANDED A PIECE OF WORK TO A PERSON WHO HAD NOT AGREED TO BE ANYTHING, HE WAS WRONG ABOUT HOW TO DO IT, THE OTHER PERSON DID IT DIFFERENTLY AND DID IT BETTER, AND NOTHING WAS GIVEN TO ANYBODY.** Two letters, both binding, dated the seventh and the eleventh of January, for the same Sunday in February; a christening lunch and a leaving party; the letting place says the later one wins and the woman of about forty-two with the key does not believe it. **HE SAYS NO IN ABOUT A QUARTER OF A SECOND, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME HE HAS SAID NO TO A PERSON WHO WANTED SOMETHING OFF HIM.** He could answer it until about nine o'clock on the morning of the eleventh of November 2015 and not one minute after it, and he tells her none of that. He does not take the wallet. He hands the question to **Tomas Renn**, who does not pick it up, asks whether he has spoken to the two people who wrote the letters, and puts one question to each of them: not *which letter is yours* but *what do you want the room to be like at four o'clock on the Sunday*. The woman of about forty-eight answers in four seconds and the woman of about twenty-one in four minutes, and the two of them come to the room on the Thursday before, unasked, and make a rule between themselves which is not about a date.
